* The Shaykh: "Ajal" correctly means an end point, but what is meant by this end point?
* The student: The Day of Resurrection.
* The Shaykh: The Day of Resurrection. Well done. What is the evidence?
* The student: ﴿When the sun is wound up, and when the stars fall, and when the mountains are set moving﴾ [al-Takwir 1-3].
* The Shaykh: Well done, excellent. His saying: ﴿Unquestionably He is the Mighty, the Forgiving﴾. ﴿Alā﴾?
* Student: An interrogative particle of opening used for alerting.
* The Shaykh: Alerting, well done. And what is the meaning of ﴿al-Ghaffar﴾?
* The student: ﴿al-Ghaffar﴾ is an intensive form (...).
* The Shaykh: From "al-ghafr," and what is al-ghafr? What is al-ghafr?
* The student: (...) an intensive form.
* The Shaykh: Yes, but what is al-ghafr? "Ghafara" means what?
* The student: "Yaghfir" (he forgives).
* The Shaykh: With the meaning of "yaghfir"? No, that is not correct; the present tense cannot be the meaning of (...).
* The student: Concealing the sin and overlooking it.
* The Shaykh: Al-ghafr, my brother, is concealing the sin and overlooking it. Why did we explain it that way?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Why did we explain it as concealing and overlooking? And why did we not explain it as overlooking only? This comes up a lot with us. Yes.
* Student: Because its linguistic meaning requires that, since al-ghafr derives from al-mighfar, which is what covers the head, so it must..
* The Shaykh: What covers the head?
* The student: What covers the head.
* The Shaykh: Just that?
* The student: And protects it.
* The Shaykh: And protects it from arrows, since it is derived from al-mighfar, which is what one covers the head with in war to protect it from arrows. I think we did not take the benefits?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: We took them? Just the last one?

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. The Almighty said: ﴿Unquestionably He is the Mighty, the Forgiving﴾.

* In this verse: an indication of the importance of knowing Allah's names and attributes, from His saying: ﴿Unquestionably He is the Mighty, the Forgiving﴾, since ﴿alā﴾ here is for alerting, and alerting is only needed for an important matter that deserves attention.
* Among its benefits: affirmation of these two names and what they indicate of attribute and ruling, namely al-'Azeez and al-Ghaffar. The rule in the field of the foundations (usul al-'aqidah, the foundations of creed) is that every name of Allah includes an attribute, and it may include, together with the attribute, a ruling, which is called the effect (al-athar) when the name is transitive (muta'addi). If it is not transitive, then it contains the name and the attribute.
* For example, al-Hayy (the Ever-Living) is one of Allah's names and includes an attribute, which is life, but it does not extend to others, because al-Hayy is an intransitive attribute, meaning it does not go beyond the one described.
* Al-Ghaffar: a name of Allah that includes an attribute, which is forgiveness, and it is transitive to others, namely that He forgives sins. So this is the rule regarding Allah's names, the Most Glorified, the Most High: every name includes an attribute, and it may include the resulting or consequent ruling of that attribute. When?
* Student: When it is transitive.
* The Shaykh: When it is transitive. As for when it is intransitive and does not extend beyond the one described, it has no ruling, meaning no ruling extending to others.

So in the verse there is affirmation of al-'Azeez and al-Ghaffar as names of Allah, affirmation of the attribute they indicate, affirmation of forgiveness, which is the ruling from His saying: ﴿al-Ghaffar﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 39, verse 6 (part 1 of 2):

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿He created you from a single soul﴾ [Az-Zumar 6]. The address here is to the children of Adam: ﴿He created you﴾, meaning, O children of Adam, ﴿from a single soul﴾, which is Adam. ﴿Then He made from it its mate﴾. The manner of Adam's creation is that Allah, Glorified and Exalted, created him from earth. This earth became clay by Allah's leave, and remained until it became like pottery, having a ringing sound when struck. Then Allah created Adam from it. After He had created Adam's body, He breathed into it the soul, and he became a living, complete, human being. This is the first creation of man, as the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, indicates. As for the monkeys who claimed that the origin of the human being is a monkey, we grant them that as far as they are concerned. As for us, we, praise be to Allah, are from the children of Adam, human beings. Allah, Exalted, created our father with His hand, taught him the names of all things, and commanded His angels to prostrate to him. As for them, they may have what they wish to return themselves to.

﴿Then He made from it its mate﴾. (Then) denotes sequence with an interval, because the creation of this mate came after the creation of Adam. Allah, Glorified and Exalted, left him for a period until he recognised that he needed a wife to find rest with her. So Allah created for him a wife and made this wife from Adam's own self. The Prophet's statement concerning women, ﹥"They were created from a rib"﹤[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (5186) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]], indicates that Eve was created from Adam's rib. And Allah is capable of all things, to create a human being without a wife, and even without a husband, for Eve was created without a mother or a father.

And His saying ﴿Then He made from it its mate﴾ does not contradict what Allah mentioned in another verse: ﴿And made from it its mate﴾ [Al-A'raf 189], because the waw (and) denotes general conjunction and does not necessarily imply sequence, or does not entail sequence. It does not entail sequence. So when another verse comes in which sequence is explicitly stated, the verse containing the waw that denotes general conjunction is interpreted in light of what? In light of sequence. The mention of one thing before another, even with waw, implies that it should be mentioned first; this is the original principle. For this reason, when the Prophet ﷺ approached al-Safa when he came to perform the sa'y, he recited: ﹥"Indeed, al-Safa and al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah"﹤ and said: ﹥"I begin with what Allah began with"﹤[[Recorded by Muslim (1218/147) from the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah.]], and so he began with al-Safa.

This indicates that what is mentioned first in speech is ahead of what follows it in rank, time or place, according to what the context requires. However, this is not necessarily binding: what comes after the waw may precede what is before it, and this is not considered a contradiction. But in His saying ﴿Then He made from it its mate﴾, we cannot say that the making here occurred before the creation of Adam. And as for His saying ﴿Then He made from it﴾, the (min) in ﴿from it﴾ denotes origin. Is ﴿from it﴾ in terms of substance, or in terms of attribute?

* Student: In terms of attribute.
* Shaykh: Both apply. She was created from Adam and is like Adam as well, so she is of his kind, and she is also from him in substance. She is a part of him and a piece of him. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ addressed the people and informed them that Fatimah is a part of him ﹥"a piece of him"﹤[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3714) and Muslim (2449) from the hadith of al-Miswar ibn Makhramah.]]. Yes.

He says: ﴿Then He made from it its mate﴾. The word zawj (mate/pair) is used with several meanings, among them a kind, as in His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿And others of similar kind, in pairs﴾ [Sad 58], meaning kinds.

And His saying, Exalted: ﴿Gather those who did wrong and their pairs﴾ [As-Saffat 22], meaning their kinds. The word zawj is also used for what is other than the single, that is, the even number, so one says "single" and "pair." The word ﴿zawjaha﴾ here includes both meanings: she is a kind of human being, and she is also a mate who made Adam an even number after he had been solitary. ﴿Then He made from it its mate﴾ is the beginning of the creation of man.

He said: (﴿And He sent down for you from the livestock﴾ the camels, cattle, sheep and goats ﴿eight pairs﴾).

﴿He sent down for you from the livestock﴾: here, sending down (inzal) means creation, because it is attributed to specific entities, namely the livestock. An-an'am is the plural of ni'm, like asbab is the plural of sabab. And His saying ﴿eight pairs﴾ means eight kinds. Allah explained these pairs in Surah Al-An'am, saying: ﴿Eight pairs: two of the sheep and two of the goats﴾ [Al-An'am 143], ﴿and of the camels two and of the cattle two﴾ [Al-An'am 144]. The total is eight: a male and a female from each of the four kinds, and when you multiply two by four, you get eight. ﴿And He sent down for you from the livestock eight pairs﴾. The author, may Allah have mercy on him, said: (each a pair, male and female, as explained in Surah Al-An'am).

Then He said: ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, a creation after a creation﴾. When Allah mentioned the beginning of the first creation, which is Adam, He mentioned the beginning of the second creation, which is the human species, and how it was created, saying: ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers﴾. (In) denotes location. Buṭūn (wombs) is the plural of baṭn (belly). The root of this word, ba, ta', nun, is the opposite of manifestness: the buṭūn are hidden, while the ẓuhūr are apparent. Among Allah's names are al-Ẓāhir and al-Bāṭin: al-Ẓāhir, the Exalted above all, and al-Bāṭin, to whom nothing is hidden. So buṭūn here is the plural of baṭn, and it is also derived from buṭūn: baṭana al-shay' buṭūnan, meaning it was hidden.

His saying ﴿ummahatikum﴾ is the plural of umm or ummah. For non-rational things one says ummāt, and for rational beings one says ummahāt. He says: ﴿a creation﴾ is the verbal noun of yakhluq, ﴿after a creation﴾, meaning a creation that develops, passing from one creation to another. The author said in his tafsir: (namely, nutfah (drop), then 'alaqah (clot), then mudghah (lump)). Allah alluded to these stages in His saying: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, indeed We created you from dust, then from a drop, then from a clot, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed﴾ [Al-Hajj 5]. ﴿From dust﴾ refers to Adam; ﴿from a drop﴾ refers to the human species; ﴿then from a clot, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed﴾. The mudghah is a piece of flesh the size of what can be chewed. The Prophet ﷺ explained the duration of this development in the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: ﹥"Indeed, one of you is gathered in his mother's womb for forty days as a drop, then he becomes a clot for a similar period, then a lump for a similar period. Then the angel is sent to him, and he breathes the soul into him, and he is commanded with four words: to write his provision, his term, his deeds, and whether he is wretched or blessed."﹤[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (7454) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud.]]

Forty days as a nutfah means water, which is the semen, but during this period it develops in a hidden way until it reaches its completion in forty days, so that it becomes an 'alaqah, that is, red blood. It is apparent that the intended meaning is not that it remains a drop until the end of the forty days and then instantly turns into blood. Rather it develops and transforms gradually until its becoming blood is complete in forty days, and then it remains in that state as a clot, but it also thickens gradually and grows until eighty days, and then after that it becomes a mudghah, a piece of flesh. ﴿Formed and unformed﴾ may possibly mean, Allah knows best, that ﴿formed﴾ refers to the end of the third stage and ﴿unformed﴾ to its beginning, meaning that in this stage it is unformed at the start and formed at the end. It is also possible that fetuses differ in this, so some of them become formed from the moment they pass into the mudghah, and some are delayed. Allah knows best, and in this matter one should refer to the scholars.

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿a creation after a creation in three darknesses﴾. ﴿Darknesses﴾ are places that light does not reach. ﴿Three﴾.

The author explained it by saying: (they are the darkness of the belly, the darkness of the womb, and the darkness of the placenta). These are three darknesses which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, made as a protection for this fetus, because if the rays of light reached it, they would corrupt it. But Allah, Mighty and Majestic, placed it in these three darknesses. Then He, Glorified and Exalted, made its back face the mother's belly and its face toward the mother's back, so that its face would not be harmed by the shocks that fall on the mother's belly; the back serves as a protection for the face. The side of the fetus that is toward the belly is strong, because it contains the spine and the ribs, so it is strong, that is, able to bear shocks. When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, wishes to bring it out, this fetus turns over, moves and is agitated by Allah's leave, and then it turns so that its head is lowermost, and the head comes out first, so that its exit is easy. For if it came out feet first, that would be harmful and dangerous too: one of the hands might catch on one side, which would cause harm, and perhaps injury to the fetus. And Allah, Glorified and Exalted, has affairs in His creation.

In sum, Allah, Glorified and Exalted, has cared for us with complete care while we were in our mothers' wombs and at the time of exiting them. For this reason He said: ﴿in three darknesses. That is Allah, your Lord﴾, and how excellent a Lord is Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿That﴾ refers to the one indicated, (Lord), and the addressee is ﴿that﴾, the human beings. ﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾. He used the demonstrative that denotes distance, ﴿dhalikum﴾, and did not say "this," to indicate the loftiness of Allah's station, the loftiness of His rank, Mighty and Majestic, and that He has highness: highness of essence, highness of worth, and highness of dominion.

His saying ﴿That is Allah, your Lord﴾: (Lord) is either an attribute or an appositive. It contains an allusion, that is, mentioning lordship after divinity refers to special nurture during pregnancy and complete care, because the fetus in its mother's belly cannot be reached by anyone, neither to bring benefit nor to ward off harm. But Allah, Glorified and Exalted, is the One who takes charge of its care.

He says: ﴿That is Allah, your Lord. To Him belongs the dominion﴾. This sentence is a declarative sentence in which the predicate is placed before the subject to convey restriction. ﴿To Him﴾ means alone, with none sharing with Him. ﴿The dominion﴾ means absolute sovereignty: sovereignty over substances and sovereignty over attributes. He is the owner of all substances and the owner of their attributes, their disposal and their management.

﴿There is no god but Him﴾. This is the tawhid of divinity (tawhid al-uluhiyyah). This sentence, as you see, consists of negation and affirmation. The negation is among the most emphatic forms of negation, because it begins with (la), the particle of generic negation (la al-nafiyah li al-jins). Grammarians and rhetoricians say that la of generic negation is explicit in generality: it is not merely apparently general but more emphatic than the apparent; it is explicit in generality. For this reason it is said that it negates the genus, not merely unity: the entire genus. So there is no god except Allah. But we must know that what is negated here is the true god, meaning: there is no true god except Allah. As for false gods, they exist, as Allah, Exalted, said: ﴿So their gods which they invoked besides Allah did not avail them anything﴾ [Hud 101]. ﴿Their gods﴾: He named them gods. And He said: ﴿And do not invoke with Allah another god﴾ [Al-Qasas 88]: ﴿another god﴾; He named it a god, but it is a false god, as He said: ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they invoke besides Him is falsehood﴾ [Al-Hajj 62].

If someone asks: Is there another god with Allah? The answer is given in detail: if you mean a true god, then no; if you mean a false god, which is called a god but is not God, then such exists.

As for His saying ﴿There is no god but Him﴾, if someone says: what is the predicate of (la)? Is it (huwa) or something else? We say: the predicate of (la) cannot be (huwa), because la of generic negation only operates on indefinite nouns, as Ibn Malik said:

"Give to (inna) the action of la on an indefinite noun..."

It only operates on indefinites, and (huwa) is definite. So where is the predicate? We say: the predicate is omitted, its estimated form being: there is no true god except Allah. This is how it must be said, and whoever says "there is no existing god except Allah" has erred, because this includes a serious matter: when you say "there is no existing god except Allah," you have made the existing gods to be Allah, and this is a grave error. Rather, one must say: there is no true god except Allah. As for in the verse, "except Him," what is the grammatical position of (huwa)? It is a substitute (badal) for the omitted predicate.

He says: ﴿Then how are you turned away?﴾ (Anna) is an interrogative particle, and it is meant as rebuke and wonder: how are you turned away from worshipping Allah, Mighty and Majestic, while you know that there is no god but Him? This is an error: foolishness in intellect and misguidance in religion.

His saying ﴿Then how are you turned away?﴾.

The commentator said: (from His worship to the worship of other than Him). Now, if this interrogation is for what, what did we say?

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: What? And wonder. It requires that this turning away be forbidden, or this turning away be forbidden, because one is only rebuked for something forbidden. And Allah knows best.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Because their desires overcame them. The word ﴿turned away﴾ indicates being turned away, because they were turned away, but it was their desires and the devils that turned them away.

* * *

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: ﴿If you disbelieve, indeed Allah is free of need from you, and He does not approve for His servants disbelief; and if you are grateful, He approves it for you. And no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you of what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of the contents of the breasts﴾ (7). ﴿And when adversity touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance; then when He bestows upon him a favour from Him, he forgets what he had been calling upon Him for before, and he sets up rivals to Allah to lead [others] astray from His way. Say, "Enjoy your disbelief for a little; indeed, you are of the companions of the Fire"﴾ [Az-Zumar 7, 8].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿He created you from a single soul, then made from it its mate﴾. What is meant by "soul" here?
* Student: Adam.
* Shaykh: Adam. And what is the meaning of His saying ﴿made from it﴾, the (min) here?
* Student: It means for the beginning.
* Shaykh: The beginning, because Eve...?
* Student: Was created from his rib.
* Shaykh: From Adam's rib.

His saying, Exalted: ﴿eight pairs﴾. What are these pairs?
* Student: (...) the cattle and camels.
* Shaykh: And the camels, from each one a male and a female.

His saying, Exalted: ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, a creation after a creation﴾. Describe for us this creation after a creation.
* Student: (...) Surah al-Hajj: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, indeed We created you﴾ [Al-Hajj 5].
* Shaykh: Yes, correct.
* Student: ﴿O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, indeed We created you from dust, then from a drop, then from a clot, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed﴾ [Al-Hajj 5].
* Shaykh: Well done. How long are these stages according to the Sunnah?
* Student: As in the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud: ﹥"The creation of one of you is gathered in his mother's belly for forty days as a drop, then he becomes a clot for a similar period, then a lump for a similar period."﹤[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (7454) from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud.]]
* Shaykh: So that is a hundred?
* Student: Twenty days.
* Shaykh: Twenty days, well done, may Allah bless you. Now His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿To Him belongs the dominion﴾ contains what indicates restriction. What is the means of this?
* Student: By placing the predicate before the subject.
* Shaykh: Placing the predicate before the subject. Now, what is the rule for this?
* Student: The rule?
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: If the predicate is placed before the subject, it indicates restriction.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 39, verse 6 (part 2 of 2):**

* The Shaykh: "But is the predicate (*al-khabar*) only for the subject (*al-mubtada'*)? Is there no general rule?"
* The student: "Fronting what should be delayed (*taqdim ma haqquhu al-ta'khir*) indicates restriction (*al-hasr*)."
* The Shaykh: "Well said. If what should be delayed is fronted, whether it is a predicate, a direct object, or something else, it indicates restriction. Now, ﴿لَهُ الْمُلْكُ﴾, 'to Him belongs dominion.' How do you reconcile this with His saying ﴿أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ﴾ ['or what your right hands possess'] [An-Nisa 3], where He affirms ownership for other than Allah?"
* Student: "Yes, Shaykh. This, with respect to human beings, becomes a specific ownership that belongs to the human being. As for the dominion mentioned in the verse, it is a general dominion (...)."
* The Shaykh: "So you mean that the dominion of Allah, glory be to Him, is a general, absolute dominion. General, meaning encompassing everything; absolute, meaning He disposes of it as He wills. As for human ownership, it is specific and restricted, correct?"
* The student: "Restricted by what is in his hand or by what he owns."
* The Shaykh: "'Specific' means it is limited to what he owns. 'Restricted' means by the requirements of the *Shar'* (the divine law). That is why a person may not squander his property wastefully. So this reconciliation is: the dominion of Allah is general and absolute, general to everything, absolute and unrestricted, He does as He wills; human ownership is specific and restricted, specific to what he owns alone. My property is not your property, for example. Restricted by what?"
* The student: "By the *Shar'*."
* The Shaykh: "By the *Shar'*. A person may not dispose of his property as he pleases. Now, His saying, exalted is He, ﴿فَأَنَّى تُصْرَفُونَ﴾ ['then how are you turned away?']. What is the interrogative here?"
* Student: "(...) for reproach and astonishment."
* The Shaykh: "For reproach and astonishment. Explain how it is for reproach and how it is for astonishment."
* The student: "For astonishment: how do you worship other than Allah, who created you..."
* The Shaykh: "And to Him belongs dominion."
* The student: "(...)."
* The Shaykh: "Well, this means it is a wondrous matter. Now, reproach?"
* The student: "(...) He reproaches them for worshipping other than Him."
* The Shaykh: "Yes, correct. That is, He blames them and makes this a discredit to them."
* * *
Then Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿إِنْ تَكْفُرُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ عَنْكُمْ﴾ ['If you disbelieve, then indeed Allah is free of need from you'] [Az-Zumar 7].
* Student: "(...)."
* The Shaykh: "Did we not take this from somewhere?"
* The student: "(...)."
* The Shaykh: "From where?"
* The student: "﴿خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ﴾ ['He created you from a single soul']."
* The Shaykh: "From the beginning?"

Well, Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ﴾ ['He created you from a single soul'].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the origin of mankind is Adam, and not, as the apes claim, that their origin was an ape which then evolved, because of His saying ﴿خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ﴾. Allah, glory be to Him, has explained how He created this soul in various places in the Qur'an.
* Among its benefits: that humankind is originated and not eternal, because of His saying ﴿خَلَقَكُمْ﴾ ['created you'], and creation implies origination.
* Among the benefits of this verse: that Allah made the spouses of the children of Adam from their own kind, because of His saying ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا﴾ ['then made from it its mate']. Had the wife been of a different kind, affection and tenderness would not have been achieved, but Allah made her of the same kind for this purpose.
* Among its benefits: what Allah has bestowed upon us..

Allah, mighty and majestic, said: ﴿خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ﴾ [Az-Zumar 6].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the origin of mankind is Adam, and not, as the apes claim, that their origin was an ape which then evolved, because of His saying ﴿خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ﴾. Allah, glory be to Him, has explained how He created this soul in various places in the Qur'an.
* Among its benefits: that humankind is originated and not eternal, because of His saying ﴿خَلَقَكُمْ﴾, and creation implies origination.
* Among the benefits of this verse: that Allah made the spouses of the children of Adam of their own kind, because of His saying ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا﴾ [Az-Zumar 6]. Had the wife been of a different kind, affection and tenderness would not have been achieved, but Allah made her of the same kind for this purpose.
* Among its benefits: what Allah has bestowed upon us by sending down the livestock, the eight kinds.
* Among its benefits: Allah's favour through these eight kinds is greater than His favour through other kinds, such as gazelles, hares, and the like, because Allah bestowed His favour through these eight kinds alone, since they are stronger (...) Allah's blessing is more evident and clearer; and because they are familiar and domestic livestock, unlike other livestock.
* Among its benefits: an indication that the creation of this creation is from pairs, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿وَمِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَا زَوْجَيْنِ﴾ ['And of everything We created two mates'] [Adh-Dhariyat 49]. Everything in creation must, for its composition, consist of a pair, even water, even air, even everything: ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْنَا زَوْجَيْنِ﴾. And here He says ﴿ثَمَانِيَةَ أَزْوَاجٍ﴾ ['eight mates'] [Az-Zumar 6].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the explanation of Allah's wisdom, mighty and majestic, in the development of creation, because of His saying ﴿يَخْلُقُكُمْ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ خَلْقًا مِنْ بَعْدِ خَلْقٍ﴾ ['He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation'] [Az-Zumar 6]. Had He willed, He could have created us in one stage, but His wisdom refuses that. Rather, a human being develops from one stage to another, for gradualness in creation, just as gradualness in legislation is wisdom. The *Shari'ah* was not sent down all at once, imposing upon people from beginning to end, but was sent down gradually. As for what we are discussing, pregnancy: if this pregnancy arose in the mother's womb all at once, it would be harmful to her. But it develops and grows little by little, until the belly expands little by little, without hardship to the mother.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah's, glory be to Him, favour upon mankind in that He develops them in this creation in a place no one can reach, because of His saying ﴿فِي ظُلُمَاتٍ ثَلَاثٍ﴾ ['in three darknesses'] [Az-Zumar 6], as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿فَجَعَلْنَاهُ فِي قَرَارٍ مَكِينٍ (٢١) إِلَى قَدَرٍ مَعْلُومٍ﴾ ['then We placed him in a secure resting place, for a known term'] [Al-Mursalat 21-22].
* Among its benefits: Allah's protection of the fetus by placing it in these three darknesses, since rays of light might harm it. So Allah, glory be to Him, placed it in these three darknesses.
* Among its benefits: that the one capable of this is the one deserving of divinity and worship, because of His saying ﴿ذَلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ لَهُ الْمُلْكُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَأَنَّى تُصْرَفُونَ﴾ ['That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion; there is no deity except Him; so how are you turned away?'] [Az-Zumar 6].
* Among its benefits also: the sole dominion of Allah, glory be to Him, because of His saying ﴿لَهُ الْمُلْكُ﴾ ['to Him belongs dominion']. There is no owner except Allah. Is the dominion the dominion of disposal in the *kawni* sense (the cosmic or decreed sense), or both the *kawni* and the *shar'i* (the legislative sense)?
* The student: "Both the *kawni* and the *shar'i*."
* The Shaykh: "Both the *kawni* and the *shar'i*. There is no owner except Allah in the *kawni* sense, and no owner except Allah in the *shar'i* sense. Therefore He alone has the *hukm* (judgment, ruling) in both the *kawni* and the *shar'i* sense, mighty and majestic is He."
* Among its benefits: the clear proclamation of the foolishness of those people who took others besides Him as protectors after these great signs became manifest, because of His saying ﴿فَأَنَّى تُصْرَفُونَ﴾, meaning: how are you turned away from the truth despite its clarity and explicitness?

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 39, verse 7 (part 1 of 3):

Then He said: ﴿If you disbelieve, indeed Allah is Free of need from you﴾ [Az-Zumar 7]. ﴿If you disbelieve﴾: disbelieve in whom?
* A student: In Allah.
* The Shaykh: If you disbelieve in Allah and in what belief in it is obligatory, then indeed you will not harm Allah, because Allah is free of need from you. Allah, glorified and exalted, did not command the servants to worship Him and to devote worship sincerely to Him out of any need on His part, but for their own benefit, for they are rewarded with the greatest reward for this and are saved by it from punishment. As for Allah, mighty and majestic, He is not harmed if all creation disbelieves ﴿If you disbelieve﴾, even if it is all of creation ﴿indeed Allah is Free of need from you﴾. There has come in the sacred hadith: "O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most wicked heart of one man among you, that would not decrease anything of My dominion."[[Narrated by Muslim (2577/55) from the hadith of Abu Dharr.]] If all people, indeed all humans and non-humans, were upon the most wicked heart of one man, that would not decrease anything of Allah's dominion, and they would not harm Allah in the least. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed Allah is Free of need from you, and He does not approve for His servants disbelief﴾ [Az-Zumar 7], meaning He does not approve for them that they disbelieve in Allah.
Consider His saying ﴿and He does not approve for His servants﴾. It means that disbelief is a matter that does not befit the servants, so He does not approve that they engage in it, because Allah created them, so how could a sensible person see fit to direct worship to other than the Creator? Therefore He said ﴿and He does not approve for His servants﴾ and did not say "from His servants" or "of His servants", because the lam (li) is more emphatic in expressing that this thing does not befit them.
His saying ﴿for His servants, disbelief﴾: servitude is divided into two kinds: general and specific.
From the first, i.e. the general: His saying, exalted is He: ﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾ [Maryam 93]. ﴿There is none﴾: the (in) here means what? ﴿In kullu man fi as-samawati wal-ard illa ati ar-Rahmana abdan﴾: (in)?
* A student: It means (ma).
* The Shaykh: It means (ma). The sign of (in) meaning (ma) is that (illa) comes after it: ﴿In anta illa nadhir﴾ [Fatir 23], meaning "you are nothing but a warner."
﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾: this is general servitude; even the devils and the disbelievers are all servants of Allah in the general sense.
The specific meaning, the specific kind of worship: the worship of the believers, which is the legislated worship, i.e. devotion to Allah exalted in the sense of the Sharia. This is specific to those who obey Him alone. Among that is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾ [Al-Furqan 63], and His saying about the messengers that they are the servants of Allah: ﴿And mention Our servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, possessors of strength and insight﴾ [Sad 45]. This is specific servitude.
His saying ﴿and He does not approve for His servants﴾: is this here of the general or of the specific?
* Students: Of the general.
* The Shaykh: Of the general; i.e., He does not approve disbelief for any one of Allah's servants.
﴿and He does not approve for His servants disbelief﴾. He said: (and if He wills it for some of them). This is a good statement: meaning He does not approve of it, but He wills it, He wills it from some of them, He wills it by the universal will (al-irada al-kawniyya), not the legislative will (al-irada ash-shar'iyya). This is a refutation of the saying of an innovator group who say: Allah only wills what He approves of, and what He does not approve of He does not will. On this false view, sins occur without Allah's will, and there is no doubt that this view is refuted by many texts, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whomever Allah wills to guide, He expands his breast to Islam; and whomever He wills to leave astray, He makes his breast tight and constricted, as if he were climbing into the sky﴾ [Al-An'am 125]. So Allah, mighty and majestic, wills this and that, but by the universal will, because all is His dominion, exalted is He. Therefore he said: (and if He wills it for some of them), meaning that His willing it for some of them does not necessitate that He is pleased with it, since He may will what He does not approve of.
If someone says: How does He will what He does not approve of? And is there anyone who compels Him?
We say: No, no one compels Him, but He wills what He does not approve of for a profound wisdom. If Allah, exalted is He, willed only what He approves of, all people would become believers, there would be no distinction for the believer from the disbeliever, the banner of jihad would not be raised, nor would commanding good and forbidding evil exist, nor would Hell be filled as Allah, mighty and majestic, promised, and other great benefits that result from the existence of disbelief among Allah's servants.
He said: ﴿And if you are grateful﴾ (to Allah, so you believe) ﴿He approves it for you﴾ [Az-Zumar 7].
﴿If you are grateful﴾ corresponds to ﴿If you disbelieve﴾ [Az-Zumar 7], because a person, among Allah's blessings, is either a disbeliever or a grateful one.
﴿If you are grateful, He approves it for you﴾, and He does not approve disbelief for His servants. Consider how, regarding disbelief, He said: Indeed Allah is ﴿Free of need﴾ and ﴿does not approve﴾; and here He said: ﴿If you are grateful, He approves it for you﴾. So in the answer to the condition ﴿If you disbelieve﴾ He began by declaring His freedom from need of creation, mighty and majestic.
As for gratitude, it is what He rewards; therefore He said: ﴿If you are grateful, He approves it for you﴾. So if He approves it, He will reward you. Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds, they are the best of creation. Their reward with their Lord is gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him﴾ [Al-Bayyinah 7-8]. Therefore He granted them the gardens. I ask Allah to make me and you among them.
He said: ﴿He approves it for you﴾. In this verb there is a grammatical difficulty, for it is the answer of the condition, and yet it is vowelled with a fatha. Answer this difficulty: how was it fatha while it is the answer of the condition?
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, ﴿If you are grateful﴾ is the condition verb, ﴿He approves it﴾ is the answer. So why was it fatha while it is the answer of the condition?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes. The present verb is it marfu' or majzum?
* A student: If a present verb comes and the first verb is a past verb, it is permissible..
* The Shaykh: The first is not a past verb, sheikh.
* A student: ﴿Tashkuru﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿Tashkuru﴾ a past verb? The past form would be (shakartum). Moreover, the principle you based this on is also wrong; it is not a past verb, and the reasoning is wrong.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Do you nullify its operation from the beginning of the world until today, so that it only jussivates one verb? Or according to the opinion of one who says: the religion is suitable for every time and place, and then twists the necks of texts so that they agree with his desire and his time?
* A student: Jussived by deleting the letter ya.
* The Shaykh: The ya, where is the ya?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Its last letter is ya, "yarda" meaning? "yardihi lakum"?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Is it the deletion of the ya or something other than the ya? You have now answered only half.
* The student: It is an alif with a kasra.
* The Shaykh: Yes, what was deleted is the alif. So it is jussived by deleting the alif. Is that correct, everyone?
* Students: Correct.
* The Shaykh: Yes. So (yardha) here is the answer of the condition, and it is jussived by deleting the alif; its original form is (yarda), but the alif was deleted for the jazm.
He said: ﴿yardhahu﴾ (with a sukun on the ha'). Read ﴿yardhah lakum﴾ ﴿wa in tashkuru yardhah lakum﴾, and this is very light, meaning you read it lightly.
The second reading says: (with a damma) ﴿yardhahu﴾ with damma, "with extension and without it." (With extension): ﴿yardhahu lakum﴾ you extend it until a waw comes out of it; and (without it): you delete the waw.
So we read: ﴿And if you are grateful, He approves it for you﴾ (yardhah), ﴿wa in tashkuru yardhahu lakum﴾, ﴿wa in tashkuru yardhahu lakum﴾; all of this is permissible, a mutawatir Sab'i reading.
As has passed over us, and we repeat it for the sake of the new brothers: a person should recite the Qur'an in all its readings, because all of them are truth. One should not abandon any of the truths, but on the condition that he is certain of the reading; mere preponderance of opinion is not sufficient. He must be certain, otherwise he should recite only what he is certain of.
Another condition: that it not be before the common people, for if the common people hear a reading that contradicts their mushaf, that causes confusion for them regarding the Qur'an and an evil opinion about you. May Allah have mercy on a man who keeps suspicion away from himself.
As for the setting of teaching, or reciting to yourself, then if you are knowledgeable in the reading, you should recite it sometimes with this and sometimes with that.
For example: ﴿The Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ [Al-Fatihah 3-4] contains the reading ﴿Malik﴾ and the reading ﴿Malik﴾ (Maalik); recite with both, once with this and once with that.
He says: ﴿And if you are grateful, He approves it for you﴾, ﴿yardhahu﴾. The author said: meaning the gratitude. So what is gratitude?
Some have defined gratitude with a comprehensive and exclusive definition, saying: gratitude is performing obedience to the Benefactor, acknowledging His favor, and it occurs with the heart, the tongue and the limbs. On this is the saying of the poet:
"The blessings have benefited you from me in three: my hand, my tongue, and the hidden conscience."
Yes, so what is gratitude, brother?
* A student: Performing the obedience of Allah.
* The Shaykh: Obedience of the Benefactor.
* The student: Obedience of the Benefactor in a way..
* The Shaykh: Acknowledging His favor. Good, where is its place?
* The student: Its place is the heart, the tongue and the limbs.
* The Shaykh: The heart: that a person believes in his heart that this blessing, or these blessings, are from Allah, mighty and majestic, by His bounty, and he does not say: "This is mine, I was given it because of knowledge I have," but says: "This is from the bounty of my Lord."
Second: with the tongue, that he worships Allah, exalted, with every legislated speech. Among that is that he speaks of Allah's blessing, for this is part of gratitude, because it is legislated speech. Allah, exalted, said: ﴿But as for the blessing of your Lord, speak of it﴾ [Ad-Duha 11].
As for the limbs, it is clear: that you manifest Allah's blessing upon you with your limbs. For example, if Allah gives you strength and courage, you show that by strength in the cause of Allah, by fighting the disbelievers, the hypocrites and others.
The main thing is that the effect of the blessing appears in your actions, so that you worship the Benefactor, mighty and majestic.
He said: ﴿If you are grateful﴾ (to Allah, so you believe), meaning so that you believe the belief that necessitates righteous action, not merely belief in Allah, mighty and majestic. Belief in Allah is not true belief until it necessitates acceptance and submission.
Many of the common people think that belief in Allah is only believing in the existence of Allah. This is wrong; rather, belief in Allah is the belief that necessitates acceptance and submission. Acceptance: to what He commanded, and the openness of the breast to it. Submission: complete compliance. Allah, exalted, said: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what is disputed between them, then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have decided, and submit in full submission﴾ [An-Nisa' 65].
According to the opinion of one who says that belief is belief in the existence of Allah, they think that the Jews and Christians are believers, and some of them openly say this: the Christian is a believer, he believes in Allah, and when one of his relatives dies, he says: "May Allah have mercy on him," and likewise the Jews.
We say: this is not belief in Allah. Belief in Allah is not valid, nor is it merely incomplete; it is not valid except with acceptance and submission: acceptance of what the revelation brought, and submission, which is complete compliance.
He says: ﴿He approves it for you, and no bearer bears the burden of another﴾ [Az-Zumar 7].
The author said in the tafsir: (﴿and no bearer bears﴾ a soul ﴿the burden of another﴾ a soul, i.e., ﴿does not bear it﴾).
﴿And no bearer bears﴾: (la) is a negation particle, (wazirah) is the subject, and it is an indefinite noun in a context of negation, so it generalizes to every bearer. But what is the meaning of the bearer (wazirah)?
The wazirah is the one who bears sin and undertakes it; this is the wazirah. Accordingly, one who has not reached puberty is not a wazirah soul, why? Because it does not bear sin. And one who is mature but has not committed sin is not a bearer. So wazirah means one capable of bearing burden, which is the accountable soul.
If we want to say wazirah in actuality, we say: it is the one who committed the sin.
So ﴿wazirah﴾ here includes the wazirah by legal judgment, and may also include the wazirah in action: the wazirah by judgment and in fact.
The wazirah by judgment is the one capable of sin, meaning one who may bear sin even if she has not done the wrong.
The wazirah in fact: the one who committed the sin. Example: a man who is mature and sane but righteous, we say: he is a wazir by judgment; another man who committed adultery or theft, we say: he is a wazir in act, if he is mature and sane.
So this is the secret of Allah's saying ﴿And no bearer bears﴾ and He did not say "and no soul bears the burden of another," but said ﴿no bearer bears﴾, because one who is not a bearer does not bear anything, neither for itself nor for another.
﴿And no bearer bears﴾: good. ﴿The burden of another﴾: i.e., the sin of another soul.
The meaning of (la tazir) is: its burden does not attach to it, i.e., the sin. Therefore the author explained it by saying (i.e., does not bear it): no bearer bears the burden of another.
Then He said: ﴿Then to your Lord is your return﴾ [Az-Zumar 7]. ﴿Then﴾ means: after the gratitude of the grateful and the disbelief of the disbeliever, the return is to Allah alone.
﴿Then to your Lord is your return﴾. In this sentence there is a restriction by the method of placing before what should be after: because His saying ﴿to your Lord﴾ is the fronted predicate, and ﴿your return﴾ is the delayed subject.
His saying ﴿Then to your Lord is your return﴾, and He did not say "to Allah", because the context here is one of lordship; the Lord is the owner, the disposer, the Creator, so it was fitting to say "to your Lord". Had He said "to Allah your return," it would be valid, because Allah, exalted, is also the one deserving worship, and only one who is a Lord deserves worship.
His saying ﴿to your Lord is your return﴾: when? On the Day of Resurrection.
But know that whoever dies, his resurrection has occurred, because he has moved from the house of action to the house of recompense.
Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyya, may Allah have mercy on him, said in al-'Aqida al-Wasitiyya: Among belief in the Last Day is belief in all that the Prophet ﷺ informed of what occurs after death, although what occurs after death before the Hour is established, yet whoever dies, his resurrection has occurred.
﴿Then to your Lord is your return, then He will inform you of what you used to do﴾ [Az-Zumar 7].
﴿Will inform you﴾: will tell you.
It has been said: news is only in a matter of importance, unlike information, which occurs even in trivial matters.
Some scholars said: they are of one meaning.
His saying ﴿Then to your Lord is your return, then He will inform you of what you used to do﴾: ﴿bima﴾ (ma) is a relative noun meaning "that which," and its returning pronoun is omitted, which is the direct object in His saying ﴿you used to do﴾, meaning "that which you used to do."
The relative (ma), and indeed all relative nouns, convey generality.
The evidence that relative nouns convey generality is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And he who brought the truth and believed in it, those are the righteous﴾ [Az-Zumar 33], where the demonstrative referring to it is repeated in plural though the relative is singular, which shows that it conveys generality.

Therefore, whatever good or evil, small or great, earlier or later, that we do, Allah the Exalted informs us of it; that is, He tells us about it. Reflect on the gentleness and kindness in His words ﴿He will inform you﴾, and not "He will call you to account." For it is established in the Sahih that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will meet His believing servant in privacy, make him acknowledge his sins, and say: "You did such-and-such on such-and-such day, and you did such-and-such on such-and-such day," until he confesses. Then Allah says to him: "I concealed them for you in the world, and I forgive them for you today."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2441) and Muslim (2768/52), from Ibn 'Umar.]] Consider, my brothers: this is informing without holding to account. For this reason He said here: ﴿He will inform you of what you used to do﴾. Then the holding to account is with Him. Informing is a promise, and the holding to account is up to Him: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [An-Nisa 48]. This is why the disbelievers are not informed of their deeds the way the believer is; that is, Allah meets them in private, conceals their sins from them, and makes them acknowledge their sins with Him alone. Rather, as they are, may Allah protect us, they will be called out before all witnesses: ﴿These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers﴾ [Hud 18]. And Allah knows best.

* Student: May Allah reward you well. Is thanking Allah for blessings by speech, meaning that a person speaks of them, for example...?
* Shaykh: No, it is among its forms that one speaks of them.
* Student: How does he speak of them in front of people? Does he boast with them or what?
* Shaykh: No, he informs them, such as saying: "I was poor and Allah made me rich. Praise be to Allah, I have a son, I have a wife, I have a house, I have a car, praise be to Allah, I am seeking knowledge, I have acquired much knowledge," and so on.
* Student: Would this be part of thanking Allah for His blessing?
* Shaykh: This is part of thanking, on condition that what drives him to it is not boasting or showing off. For some people speak of blessings as a form of praising Allah, that Allah gave him, bestowed favour upon him, and was gracious to him.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: It is acceptable, but the relative pronoun (al-mawsul) is better; it is acceptable.
* Student: ﴿Then He made from it its mate﴾ [Az-Zumar 6]. Some scholars say that it is not permissible for a human to marry a jinn, and vice versa?
* Shaykh: No. This verse ﴿Then He made from it its mate﴾ refers to Hawwa (Eve); it is not about the species. If it were about the species...
* Student: A boy who reaches ten years of age is commanded to pray...
* Shaykh: As for the matter of a human marrying a jinn, this is a matter that returns to the one legally authorized regarding the jinn; if he marries you, trust in Allah.
* Student: A boy who reaches ten years of age is obligated to pray. Is he then responsible for his own acts?
* Shaykh: No, he is not obligated.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes, he is beaten for it at ten, but as a form of discipline, to train him in obedience; otherwise, if he abandons it, he does not sin.
* Student: If a person recites, for example, in the first rak'ah ﴿Master of the Day of Judgment﴾ [Al-Fatihah 4] (māliki), and in the second rak'ah recites ﴿King of the Day of Judgment﴾ (maliki), is this considered valid?
* Shaykh: No, there is no harm in it, there is no impediment, there is no sin (...).

Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿If you disbelieve, then indeed Allah is free of need of you, and He does not approve for His servants disbelief﴾ [Az-Zumar 7].

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Then He will inform you of what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knower of what is within the breasts﴾ [Az-Zumar 7].

His words ﴿Indeed, He is Knower of what is within the breasts﴾: that is, Allah the Mighty and Majestic ﴿is Knower of what is within the breasts﴾, meaning the hearts. The evidence for this is His statement: ﴿For indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts﴾ [Al-Hajj 46]. So the meaning of "dhat al-sudur" (possessor of the breasts) is the hearts.

Allah mentioned this sentence after His words ﴿Then He will inform you of what you used to do﴾ to indicate that the reckoning is for what is in the heart, as in His statement: ﴿Indeed, He is able to return him. On the Day when secrets are examined﴾ [At-Tariq 8-9], and His statement: ﴿Does he not know that when what is in the graves is scattered, and what is in the breasts is obtained?﴾ [Al-'Adiyat 9-10]. So on the Day of Resurrection the basis is what is in the heart. As for in this world, the basis is outward deeds. For this reason the Prophet ﷺ treated the hypocrites as he treated the Muslims, because they outwardly displayed Islam. We judge people in this world by what appears of their deeds, and we leave their inner states to Allah. In the Hereafter, however, the reckoning is for what is in the heart. Therefore a person must attend to the rectification of his heart before the rectification of his body, because the rectification of the body is a façade before the creation, but the rectification of the heart is what lies between a person and his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic.

* From the benefits of this verse: a clarification that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, commanded His servants to worship Him because they need it and it benefits them, not because He needs it; this is shown by His words ﴿Indeed, Allah is free of need of you﴾ [Az-Zumar 7].
* And among its benefits: affirming the Name Al-Ghani (the Free of Need) for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and affirming the attribute indicated by it; for every Name of Allah includes an attribute, but not every attribute includes a Name. Hence we say that Allah's attributes are broader than His Names, in the sense that they are more numerous. The reason is clear: if we say that every Name includes an attribute, the Names and attributes would be equal, given that a single Name may include several attributes. But let us say at least that it includes only one attribute. If we say that every Name includes an attribute, then the Names and attributes are equal. However, there are attributes from which no Names can be derived, and they are very many. Thereby it becomes clear that the attributes are broader and more numerous than the Names.
* And among the benefits of this verse: that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, does not approve of disbelief for His servants, because it is unfitting for them; since they are the servants of Allah, what befits them is that they carry out His obedience and worship, and it is not fitting for them to disbelieve in Him.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of approval (ridā) for Allah, by His words ﴿and He does not approve﴾, and His words after it: ﴿And if you are grateful, He approves it for you﴾. Approval is one of Allah's attributes of action (sifah fi'liyyah), because it is connected to His will; and every attribute connected to the will of Allah is called, according to the people of the Sunnah, an attribute of action. And every attribute linked to a cause is among the attributes of action, because it exists when its cause exists.

The truth is that approval is a real attribute of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, like joy, wonder, laughter, and the like. The people of ta'til (negation of attributes) claimed that approval means reward, and they interpreted it as something separate and detached from Allah, out of fear that voluntary acts would be attached to Him. This is from their ignorance. For if we interpret it as reward, reward only occurs by will, and will only exists when the cause of approval exists, and then the will would be originated. They fled from one thing and fell into its like, along with distorting the texts by diverting them from their apparent meaning and negating the attribute indicated by the text. These are three pitfalls. Notice how those who distort words from their places fall into three matters, three pitfalls:
The first pitfall: they fell into what they fled from. If what they fled from was a pitfall, then what they fell into is also a pitfall.
The second: they distorted the text from its apparent meaning, diverting it to another meaning.
The third: they negated Allah of the attribute indicated by the text they distorted. For example, they negated Allah of the attribute of approval, distorted the text from its apparent meaning, and fell into what they fled from. And so on for all the attributes they distorted from their apparent meaning.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: there is no necessary connection between approval and will. Its basis is His saying ﴿and He does not approve for His servants disbelief﴾, while He has informed us in many verses that disbelief occurs by His will. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever Allah wills to misguide, He makes his breast tight﴾ [Al-An'am 125].
If we combine this and that, we know that there is no necessary connection between approval and will. He may will what He does not approve, and He may approve what He does not will... He does not approve, for example, that any person be ungrateful to Allah, yet has He willed that? No.
He says: ﴿and He does not approve for His servants disbelief﴾.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: an indication that disbelief is not pleasing to Allah, by His words ﴿for His servants﴾. A servant must be a believer in his master and obedient to him; how can he be a servant and then disbelieve in Him?!
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the excellence of gratitude, and that the grateful person attains the approval of his Lord, by His words ﴿And if you are grateful, He approves it for you﴾ [Az-Zumar 7]. And there has come in a hadith: "Indeed Allah is pleased with the servant who eats a morsel and praises Him for it, and drinks a drink and praises Him for it."[[Narrated by Muslim (2734/89), from Anas ibn Malik.]] Regarding "eats a morsel and praises Him for it": is the intended "akla" (morsel) a full meal or each bite?
* Student: A meal.
* Shaykh: Some hold that it means a meal, and some hold that it means a bite. Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, would praise Allah every time he took a bite. He was asked about this and said: "Eating and praising is better than eating and remaining silent," because the wording of the hadith, "yaʼkulu al-akla," may refer to a bite or to a meal. The same applies to drinking; a person should, when drinking, drink in three breaths, praising Allah with each breath, if we take "shurbah" to mean a breath.

He said: ﴿And if you are grateful, He approves it for you﴾ [Az-Zumar 7].
* Among its benefits: the excellence of gratitude.
* And among its benefits: that Allah approves gratitude for His servants. When Allah is pleased with a servant, that becomes a cause for the servant's being pleased; the evidence is His statement: ﴿Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 119]. Allah is pleased with them for their worship of Him, and they are pleased with Him for what He rewarded them with. We ask Allah to make me and you among them, that a person be pleased with his Lord and that Allah be pleased with him.
﴿And if you are grateful, He approves it for you﴾.
* And among the benefits of this verse: no soul bears the burden of another soul, even if the other soul takes on that sin. If another takes responsibility for that sin... for example, if a person says to another: "Do such-and-such a sin, and the sin is upon me," is this valid? He says: "I am a guarantor." Consider: if someone guarantees a debt for another person, is that valid? It is valid, and he burdens himself with that debt through this guarantee. If that is so, why would it not be valid for him to guarantee the sin of the one who commits the sin? We say: because of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, "Follow our way, and we will bear your sins"﴾ [Al-'Ankabut 12]: "We will carry the punishment for you." Allah says: ﴿But they will not bear anything of their sins. Indeed, they are liars﴾ [Al-'Ankabut 12]. Moreover, on the Day of Resurrection the matter will be even more severe: ﴿When those who were followed disown those who followed﴾ [Al-Baqarah 166]. They disown them, and they dispute in the Fire, each group disowning the other. So it is impossible for anyone to bear the sin of another, ever.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse..
Before we take this benefit, we must still ask a question.
If someone says: How can this noble verse be reconciled with the saying of the Messenger ﷺ: "Whoever establishes a bad practice in Islam, upon him is its burden and the burden of whoever acts upon it until the Day of Resurrection,"[[Narrated by Muslim (1017/69), from Jarir ibn 'Abd Allah.]] and his informing that: "No soul is killed unjustly except that upon the first son of Adam, the one who killed his brother, is a share of its guilt"?[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (7321) and Muslim (1677/27), from Ibn Mas'ud.]]
The answer: whoever establishes a bad practice bears the sins of those who follow him, because his act is the cause. In reality, he has not borne the sin of another except that he is the cause that drew people to this sin.
People may be repelled by this sin, fearing it and dreading it, but when a person commits it, the matter becomes easy for them, and they follow him, especially if the person is one whose word is obeyed, such as a ruler or a scholar, and the like.
Thus there is no contradiction between the verse and the hadith. The explanation is that whoever establishes a bad practice has done the deed which is the sin, and the cause is that people follow him.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: an indication that sin is borne only by one who is fit to bear it, by His words ﴿no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another﴾ [Az-Zumar 7]. The "wazirah" (bearer) is one who is fit to bear the burden, and the one fit to bear it is one who combines two qualities: puberty and reason. This is shown by the sound hadith: "The pen is lifted from three: from the sleeper until he awakes, from the insane until he recovers, and from the child until he reaches puberty."[[Narrated by Abu Dawud (4398), al-Nasa'i in al-Mujtaba (3432), and Ibn Majah (2041), from 'A'ishah.]] Many scholars have authenticated it.
If someone says: Is not the father, as a shepherd over his children, sinful if they neglect something, due to their neglect?
The answer: Yes, but his neglecting them is a burden and a sin, by the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire﴾ [At-Tahrim 6], and because the Prophet ﷺ said: "A man is a shepherd over his household and is responsible for his flock."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2554) and Muslim (1829/20), from Ibn 'Umar.]]
Then He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Then to your Lord is your return﴾ to the end of the verse [Az-Zumar 7].
* From the benefits of this sentence: that the return is to Allah on the Day of Resurrection.
* Following from this benefit: the obligation to prepare for this meeting and this return. Preparation for it is by abandoning sins and performing acts of obedience; this is the preparation. As long as the return is to Allah, you cannot return to anyone else, whoever he may be. Your return is to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; from Him is the beginning and to Him is the end.
* And among its benefits: an explanation of the comprehensiveness of Allah's knowledge, by His words ﴿Then He will inform you of what you used to do﴾ [Az-Zumar 7], of what you used to do, all of it, small and great. The address is to all people, and this indicates the comprehensiveness of the knowledge of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And so it is: Allah's knowledge is vast and encompasses everything.
Allah, glorified and exalted, has pointed out how vast it is, saying: ﴿Should not He who created know, while He is the Subtle, the All-Aware?﴾ [Al-Mulk 14]. ﴿Should not He who created know?﴾ means: if Allah is the Creator, which is acknowledged, it necessarily follows that He knows what He created, for how could He create what He does not know? That is impossible.
﴿Should not He who created know?﴾ We take a parenthetical remark from it. Is "man" (مَنْ) here a subject or an object?
* Student: A subject.
* Shaykh: Both are permissible. It can be a subject: "Does not He who created know whom He created?" And it can be an object: "Does not Allah know whom He created?" It is well known that the Creator and the created are mutually implicated: there is no creator without creation, and no creation without a creator.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: that Allah, glorified and exalted, knows the secrets of the servant, by His words ﴿Indeed, He is Knower of what is within the breasts﴾ [Az-Zumar 7]. Allah says: ﴿And We have certainly created man, and We know what his soul whispers to him﴾ [Qaf 16]. Indeed, He knows what will happen to a person. A person knows what his soul whispers to him, but he does not know what he will earn tomorrow, while Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, knows what the servant will earn tomorrow.
* And among the benefits of the verse: an indication that the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection will be for what is in the breasts. For when He mentioned the informing, He said: ﴿Indeed, He is Knower of what is within the breasts﴾, meaning that the basis of the reckoning is what is in the heart. So correct what is in your heart, for it is the basis. Evidence for this from the verses has been mentioned during the commentary.

* Among its benefits: it points to the fact that the heart is the thing on which righteousness depends. Since the reckoning is for what is in the heart, it is the heart on which righteousness depends. This is supported by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Indeed, in the body there is a piece of flesh; if it is sound, the whole body is sound, and if it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt. Indeed, it is the heart."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (52), and Muslim (1599 / 107), from the hadith of al-Nu'man ibn Bashir.]]

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 39, verse 8–9 (part 1 of 5):

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when harm touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him in repentance﴾ [az-Zumar 8].
﴿When it touches﴾ means: when it reaches him.
And as for ﴿man﴾, the author says: the intended meaning is (the disbeliever).
This general term was made specific because of the apparent context of the verse, as will become clear; otherwise the basic principle is that "man" (al-insan) is one of the words of generality. The "al" in it is for the comprehensiveness of the category, and the sign of the "al" that denotes comprehensiveness is that it can be replaced by (kull), i.e., "every person."
But the author, may Allah have mercy on him, made it a general term by which a specific meaning is intended, by the indication of the context, for the context shows that what is meant is the disbeliever, since what the context describes cannot apply to a believer.
﴿When harm touches man﴾: ﴿harm﴾ is an indefinite noun in a conditional context, so it is general; i.e., any harm that may occur, to his body, his family, his wealth, whether great or small, any harm that may occur falls under the phrase ﴿harm﴾.
﴿He calls upon his Lord﴾: note His saying ﴿calls upon his Lord﴾ and not "calls upon Allah." In this state, i.e., at the onset of harm, he recognizes his Lord, and that there is no refuge from it except in Him, so he calls upon his Lord, believing Him to be his Lord who owns whatever He wills and disposes of whatever He wills.
The author said: (tadarra'a, "humbly beseeches"), meaning he explained ﴿calls upon﴾ as meaning (tadarra'a), based on the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Call upon your Lord humbly and secretly﴾ [al-A'raf 55]. Tadarru' is submission and abasement before Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
(﴿turning﴾ returning ﴿to Him﴾) So when he calls upon his Lord turning to Him, Allah removes his harm, because He, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿Is not He who responds to the distressed one when he calls upon Him, and removes evil, and makes you successors on the earth?﴾ [an-Naml 62].
Allah's responding to the distressed one includes both the disbeliever and the Muslim, even the disbeliever whom Allah knows will disbelieve after his distress is lifted: He answers his supplication. ﴿And when they board ships, they call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion; but when He delivers them to the land, immediately they associate others with Him﴾ [al-'Ankabut 65]. He, Mighty and Majestic, knows that they will associate others with Him after deliverance, yet He answers them, because His mercy precedes His wrath. In a state of necessity the turning of man to his Lord is true, because he knows that none removes harm except Allah. So when he returns to his Lord, glorified and exalted, His mercy precedes His wrath, and He answers him out of mercy toward him.
Here the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Then when He bestows upon him a favor from Himself﴾ to the end [az-Zumar 8].
He said: ﴿Then when He bestows﴾ meaning, as if this, and Allah knows best, is an indication that after he is overwhelmed by blessing and continues in it for a time, he then disbelieves.
And His saying: ﴿when He bestows upon him a favor﴾. He said: (a'taahu, "gave him") is an explanation of ﴿bestows﴾.
(in'aaman, "a bestowal") is an explanation of ﴿a favor﴾.
As for explaining ﴿bestows﴾ as (a'taahu), it is clear; but explaining ﴿a favor﴾ as (in'aam, "bestowal") has no basis, because what is given is not the bestowal but the favor. Accordingly, leaving the verse on its apparent meaning is better than what the author, may Allah have mercy on him, adopted.
If we take it as "a bestowal," the sentence does not stand. Why? Because bestowal is an act of Allah, whereas what is given is the favor, not the act of Allah. So leaving the verse on its apparent meaning is without doubt the one that agrees with reality.
He says: ﴿Then when He bestows upon him a favor from Himself﴾. ﴿From Himself﴾: the (min) here is for origin; i.e., a favor proceeding from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, by which it becomes clear that it is pure grace from Allah.
(﴿forgets﴾ abandons ﴿what he used to call upon﴾, supplicate humbly ﴿to Him before﴾, and that is Allah.) Look, my brother: he used to humbly beseech Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that He remove the harm from him; Allah removed the harm from him and gave him a favor beyond the removal of harm. What then is his state?
He said: ﴿forgets what he used to call upon Him for before﴾. Forgetting here means heedlessness, not the forgetfulness of the heart; what is meant is heedlessness that implies abandonment. Among its examples is the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So woe to those who pray, who are heedless of their prayer﴾ [al-Ma'un 4-5], i.e., heedless of their prayer.
﴿forgets what he used to call upon Him for before﴾: he says (﴿what he used to call upon﴾ humbly beseech ﴿Him for before﴾).
The pronoun ﴿Him﴾ refers to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
And ﴿what﴾ refers to Allah. For this reason the author, may Allah have mercy on him, said: (fa-"ma" is in the place of "man"). The "ma" in His saying ﴿what he used to call upon﴾ is in the place of "man." The author's intent is that "ma" means "man," i.e., he forgot whom he used to call upon before, meaning whom he used to direct supplication to, or as the author said: (humbly beseeches Him, who is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic), so he became heedless, and "ma" is as if Allah had bestowed upon him the removal of harm and the granting of favor.
﴿He forgets what he used to call upon Him for before, and sets up rivals to Allah﴾ [az-Zumar 8].
The rivals are those he became heedless of, while the One, the Subduer, he became heedless of, may Allah protect us, even though the rivals did not benefit him and he did not humbly beseech them when harm touched him; yet he turns to them and abandons the One who bestowed favor upon him.
﴿and sets up rivals to Allah﴾ (partners).
Andad is the plural of nid, and the nid is the equal who rivals his counterpart, the like of him. So he sets up rivals to Allah in what? In worship: he worships these idols as he worships Allah, vows to them as he vows to Allah, sacrifices to them as he sacrifices to Allah, and so on.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿so that he may lead astray from His way﴾ (with the yā' vocalized with fatḥa or ḍamma) ﴿from His way﴾ (the religion of Islam).
﴿rivals so that he may lead astray﴾: this lām is either for causation (ta'līl) or for consequence (ʿāqiba). On the reading with fatḥa, ﴿li-yaḍilla﴾, the lām is for consequence, meaning that by setting up rivals to Allah he ends in misguidance. If the yā' is vocalized with ḍamma, ﴿li-yuḍilla﴾, the lām is for causation, meaning that he set up rivals to Allah so that others would follow him and go astray. The verse has two readings: ﴿yaḍilla﴾ and ﴿yuḍilla﴾; ﴿yaḍilla﴾ refers to himself and ﴿yuḍilla﴾ refers to others. Both readings are sound, or both are sound, and each conveys a meaning that completes the other: he goes astray himself and also leads others astray. We said the lām is for consequence; when? On which reading?
* Students: ﴿li-yaḍilla﴾.
* The Shaykh: On the fatḥa reading; meaning that when he takes rivals, his end is misguidance. And for causation, on which of the two readings?
* Students: The ḍamma.
* The Shaykh: On ḍamma; meaning he set up rivals to Allah so that he would be followed and others would go astray.

Does the lām for consequence occur in the Arabic language? Yes, it occurs. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Then the family of Pharaoh picked him up, that he might become for them an enemy and a grief﴾ [al-Qasas 8]. Did the family of Pharaoh pick up Moses so that he might become their enemy and grief? Never. They said: ﴿Perhaps he will benefit us, or we may adopt him as a son﴾ [al-Qasas 9], but the outcome was that he became an enemy and a grief.
And the lām may occur as an extra particle (za'ida), as in His saying: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the uncleanness﴾ [al-Ahzab 33]: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you﴾, i.e., to remove. And as in His saying: ﴿Allah desires to make clear to you﴾ [an-Nisa 26]: ﴿Allah desires to make clear﴾, i.e., to make clear. They said it is extra because (arada, "desire") takes its object directly, not with the lām, and it cannot be for causation, since causation is already derived from the act of desiring. Accordingly, they parse it as extra. Thus it becomes clear that the lām that enters the imperfect verb may be extra, causative (which is the most common), or consequential.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Is it not a disagreement?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, correct.
* The student: (...) in some things, will (irāda) without will (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes, correct.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Well done. He is pleased that the disbeliever should submit, but He did not will that he submit; so here..
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: That is it. This is the point: there is no necessary connection, since pleasure may exist without will, will may exist without pleasure, and pleasure and will may both exist.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: What does Allah be pleased with from the disbeliever? That he submit. He is not pleased with disbelief; Allah is not pleased with disbelief. He is pleased with gratitude, so He is pleased that this disbeliever be grateful and believe. But did Allah will that he be grateful and believe? If Allah had willed it, it would have happened.
* A student: O Shaykh, may Allah be good to you, O Shaykh, how do we reconcile ﴿and no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another﴾ [az-Zumar 7] with what is reported: "The dead person is punished by the weeping of his family over him"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1290), Muslim (927/19), from Ibn 'Umar.]]?
* The Shaykh: Yes, this is also correct, and it should be raised against the verse. It is established from the Messenger ﷺ that "the dead person is punished by the weeping of his family over him." 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "The intended meaning is the disbeliever."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1288), Muslim (929).]] Without doubt she, may Allah be pleased with her, was a human who errs and is correct, because the disbeliever is punished whether or not his family weep over him. But she wanted to say that the meaning of the hadith is that the disbeliever is punished while his family weep over him; she made this the meaning of the hadith and cited the verse as evidence.
But we say: this interpretation does not stand. Rather the meaning of the verse is that the punishment intended is psychological suffering, not physical suffering. A parallel to this is the Messenger ﷺ's saying: "Travel is a piece of punishment"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (1804), Muslim (1927/179), from Abu Hurayrah.]], though the traveler is not physically tormented. He may be among the most pleasant of situations when the land is fertile, the camels good, and the companions friends; what is travel then? Recreation. Yet it is still a piece of punishment of the heart, is it not?
We in the airplane are comfortable, air-conditioned, warm in winter and cool in summer, drinking coffee and juice, eating dates, and whatever we ask for comes; yet the heart is pained, unlike a person settled in his house. So the punishment in the grave is this kind of punishment.
Some scholars said: he is punished with physical punishment, a bodily penalty, but this applies to one who instructed his family to wail over him, though this is not mentioned in the hadith; the hadith is taken to mean what other texts require.
Some of them said: this applies to a man whose family he knows will wail over him and he does not forbid them. The difference between this view and the previous one is clear: the previous one instructed them, while this one did not forbid them; he did not instruct them but knew they would do it and did not forbid them. So these are four views on the hadith, and the soundest is that the intended punishment is psychological punishment, not physical punishment, because of His saying: ﴿and no bearer of burdens bears the burden of another﴾ [az-Zumar 7].
