Then from this we derive two meanings: the meaning of the command, and the meaning of worship, which has been omitted so that the particle can be correctly attached to it.

He said: ﴿And I have been commanded to be the first of the Muslims﴾ (of this ummah). ﴿To be the first of the Muslims﴾: the author said: (of this ummah).

And the word ﴿Muslims﴾: Islam is applied to submission, because it is derived from: aslama amrahu ila ghayrihi (he entrusted his affair to another), and from it comes istislam in war, because one who surrenders submits to the victor who has overcome him.

So Islam is outward submission, and on this basis the hypocrites would be, what? Muslims outwardly. For this reason, Islam is applied to one of weak faith, as Allah said: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not believed; but say, 'We have submitted'"﴾ [Al-Hujurat 14].

Sometimes Islam is applied to the entire Shari'ah, encompassing outward and inward submission, which is faith. Among this is His saying: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favor upon you, and approved for you Islam as a religion﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 3]. The intended meaning here is not merely outward submission, but all the laws: all the laws of Islam; ﴿I have approved for you Islam﴾, that is, all the laws of Islam, ﴿as a religion﴾.

The scholars say: when Islam is mentioned alongside faith, Islam is explained as outward deeds and faith as inward deeds. They said: among this is the hadith of Jibril, when he asked the Prophet ﷺ about Islam, and he said: "That you testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establish the prayer, pay the zakah, fast Ramadan, and make pilgrimage to the House." And when he asked him about faith, he said: "That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, and that you believe in divine decree, its good and its evil"[[Narrated by Muslim (8 / 1) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.]].

As for when one of them is mentioned alone, it includes the other: so Islam, when mentioned alone, encompasses all the laws, including faith; and faith, when mentioned alone, encompasses all the laws, including Islam.

He says here: ﴿And I have been commanded to be the first of the Muslims﴾ [Az-Zumar 12]. He said: (of this ummah). Why did he restrict the verse, although it is unrestricted: ﴿the first of the Muslims﴾? He restricted it because he, may Allah have mercy on him, understood that the priority here is priority in time; and if it is priority in time, it is not correct that the Prophet ﷺ be the first of the Muslims, why? Because before him there were many Muslim nations. So it was necessary to restrict this to the first of the Muslims of this ummah. Among this is His saying in Surat al-An'am, recite the verse: ﴿Indeed, my prayer, my sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. No partner has He. And this I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims﴾ [Al-An'am 162-163]. According to the understanding the author adopted, we say: ﴿and I am the first of the Muslims﴾ of this ummah.

There is another possibility: that the priority here is priority of quality; that is, that I precede the Muslims in terms of advancing to Islam, as you might say to someone addressing you: if what you have said is true, then I am the first to contribute. For example, if he said: a charitable project has been opened in the town, and you said: if it is true, then I am the first to contribute; that is, "first" in terms of submission and quality. This is a possibility. If this meaning is in the noble verse, then we do not need the restriction the author mentioned, because we know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the first to submit to Allah, the Exalted, and that he is the greatest of people in submission and the most intense in it.

Then He said: ﴿Say, "Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day."﴾ [Az-Zumar 13]. ﴿The punishment﴾ is the object of what? Of ﴿disobey﴾?

* Student: Or of ﴿I fear﴾.
* The Shaykh: Or of ﴿if I disobey﴾?
* The student: Its origin is: I fear the punishment of.
* The Shaykh: I fear the punishment of; and it is not the object of ﴿disobey﴾. Why?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Punishment is not disobeyed; the meaning would be corrupted.

﴿Say, "Indeed, I fear"﴾: fear cannot be defined more clearly than by its own word. Everyone knows fear, does he not? For this reason we say: psychological states cannot be defined by anyone, because nothing is clearer than their own word; there is nothing clearer than their word, ever.

If a person said: define for me hatred, what would you say? You would say: hatred is well known; hatred is hatred.

Define for me love. You cannot; love is love.

* Student: Inclination.

* The Shaykh: No, inclination is among the effects of love; after one loves, one inclines. For this reason Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, says in Rawdat al-Muhibbin (and Allah knows best whether it is his or not): love cannot be bounded by anything clearer than its own word, ever. All those who defined it, and there are more than twenty definitions of it, explain it only by its necessary consequences and results. He spoke the truth, may Allah have mercy on him: psychological states, a person cannot define them better than by their own word.

﴿Fear﴾: if you asked a child who does not know definitions: what is the meaning of fear? He would say: fear is that I tremble, I shake. That is not possible; that is among its effects. Fear is that I flee; that is among its effects. So we say: fear is what? It is well known; it is fear.

﴿Indeed, I fear if I disobey my Lord﴾. ﴿Disobey﴾ (ma'siyah): opposition, and it occurs in two ways: either by leaving what is commanded or by doing what is forbidden. This is when it is separated from obedience; but if it is paired with obedience, obedience becomes doing what is commanded and disobedience becomes committing what is prohibited.

Here we say: ﴿disobey﴾ is separated from obedience, so what is the meaning?

* Student: It includes two meanings.
* The Shaykh: It includes two meanings: opposing Him, ﴿if I disobey my Lord﴾, that is, I oppose Him by doing what is forbidden or by leaving what is commanded.

In His saying ﴿my Lord﴾ there is an indication that He, the Mighty and Majestic, is the one who holds the command and the prohibition, because He is Lord, and the Lord is the Creator, the Owner, the Governor.

﴿The punishment of a tremendous day﴾ is the Day of Resurrection. Allah the Exalted described it in the Noble Qur'an with several attributes, among them: greatness (al-'izam), because of its severity, the severity of its terrors, and the severity of what happens in it. When you hear the attributes Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mentioned for this tremendous day, there will certainly overcome you a fear in proportion to your faith in it. Observe: the stronger a person's faith in the Last Day, the greater his fear of it; and the weaker his faith in the Last Day, the weaker his fear of it. For this reason we have a well-known saying: whoever knows Allah best fears Him most. And whoever also knows the Last Day best and has the strongest faith, has the strongest fear.

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day (13). Say, "Allah I worship, being sincere to Him in my religion"﴾ [Az-Zumar 13-14]. In the first verse He said: ﴿So worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Az-Zumar 2], a command. In the second, He commanded him to announce that he is sincere to Allah in religion, to announce it. In the first, he himself does it: he worships Allah, being sincere to Him in religion. In the second, he was commanded to declare to the assembly that he is sincere, and declaring that he is sincere means that he disassociates himself from their shirk, because he is sincere to Allah.

﴿Say, "Allah I worship"﴾: its parsing? The name of Allah?

* Student: ﴿Say, "Allah"﴾?
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: A subject.
* The Shaykh: A subject! Continue.
* Student: An object.
* The Shaykh: A subject and an object! Not possible; it is either a subject or an object.
* Student: An object.
* The Shaykh: An object of what?
* Student: Of ﴿say﴾.
* The Shaykh: Of ﴿say﴾, ﴿Say, "Allah I worship"﴾!
* Student: Of ﴿I worship﴾.
* The Shaykh: The object of ﴿I worship﴾?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Good, correct. ﴿Say, "Allah I worship"﴾ placed the object first for restriction; that is: I do not worship other than Him.

Its counterpart in structure is His saying in Surat al-Fatihah: ﴿You alone we worship﴾ [Al-Fatihah 5], where He placed the object first.

Here, ﴿Say, "Allah I worship"﴾ placed the object first to convey restriction, then He emphasized this by His saying: ﴿being sincere to Him in my religion﴾; that is, I do not worship other than Allah, and in my worship of Him I am also sincere to Him; no shirk mixes with my worship of Him: ﴿being sincere to Him in my religion﴾.

His saying ﴿my religion﴾ means: my deed. The author said: (from shirk).

If you combine the two verses: the first, ﴿Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Az-Zumar 11], and the second, you know the intensity of the Messenger's, peace and blessings be upon him, compliance with the command of his Lord, and that he worshipped Allah, being sincere to Him in religion, and announced that to the assembly, unconcerned with their opposition.

﴿So worship what you will besides Him﴾ [Az-Zumar 15]. ﴿So worship﴾ may be a threat and may be a challenge. The author says: (it contains a threat), but it may be a challenge.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 39, verse 11–15 (part 2 of 3):

As for its being a threat, it is evident, ﴿So worship what you will besides Him﴾; because he said after it: ﴿Say, indeed the losers are those who have lost themselves﴾ and so on [Az-Zumar: 15].
As for its being a challenge, it is because when he mentioned that he worships Allah alone, sincerely, he challenged them; he said: I do not care. You worship whatever you wish, and I do not care about you. So I will not associate anything with Allah; I will worship Allah alone, sincerely.
The rule we have in tafsir is that if a verse can bear two meanings that do not contradict each other, it is to be understood as both of them together.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So worship what you will besides Him﴾. ﴿What you will﴾ means: that which you will. ﴿Besides Him﴾ means: other than Him. Worship whatever you wish other than Him: a king, a saint, a tree, a stone, the sun, the moon, whoever you worship does not concern me. I will remain sincere to Allah, and you worship whatever you will.
The author says: (﴿Besides Him﴾, other than Him) i.e., apart from Him (it contains a threat to them and a declaration that they do not worship Allah). (Declaration) means announcement; i.e., this sentence contains the threat, and it contains that they do not worship Allah but worship other than Him.
﴿Say﴾ means: say to them, along with your challenging them and your threatening them, ﴿Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves﴾ [Az-Zumar: 15]. The sentence contains emphasis and it contains restriction. Where is the emphasis?
* Students: ﴿Indeed (inna)﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿Indeed (inna)﴾, ﴿indeed the losers﴾.
The restriction: both parts of the sentence are definite: ﴿the losers﴾, ﴿those who have lost﴾; so it is as if he said: Indeed the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Thus there is in it emphasis and restriction.
﴿Indeed the losers﴾: who is the loser? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, explained the loser in His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss, except those who believe﴾ [Al-Asr: 2, 3]. That is, loss (khusran) is the opposite of profit; for the one who trades either takes his capital, or he loses and receives less than his capital, or he profits and receives more.
The true loss is what Allah mentioned here: ﴿those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Az-Zumar: 15]. These are the ones who have lost. The loser is not one who has lost millions of dirhams, nor one who has lost his family in this world, nor one who has lost himself in this world. The loser is one who has lost himself and his family, when? On the Day of Resurrection: he has lost himself and his family.
He says: (by the eternal abiding of their souls in the Fire, and by their not reaching the maidens of paradise prepared for them, had they believed).
His saying: (by the eternal abiding of their souls in the Fire) is an explanation of their losing themselves, for he has truly lost himself. What is the aspect of the loss?
The aspect of the loss is that he did not benefit from his life in this world for the Hereafter at all, so he lost himself, lost his life; all of it went as scattered dust. He lost himself. Had he been a sincere believer, he would have benefited; all his worldly life would have been a profit, because he would abide forever in Paradise, in which is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and what has not occurred to the heart of any human. But now he will abide forever in the Fire. This is the loss of the self.
The author explained the loss of the family as his missing the wide-eyed maidens in Paradise had he believed; and although this has a basis, it is far from the correct meaning. This is because the maidens in Paradise were never his family such that it could be said he lost them; rather, what is meant is that they lost their families, because their families, if they were believers, are in Paradise, and they will not gather with them; and if they were disbelievers, they are in the Fire and they will not gather with them either. Even if they were believers and their offspring were believers, they would be as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith – We will join them with their descendants﴾ [At-Tur: 21]. That is, no one will gather with his family in the Hereafter unless he and they are believers; then they will gather in a gathering with no separation after it. As for one who is not like that, there is no gathering.
In any case, the correct view is that what is meant by ﴿their families﴾ is their families who were in the world, since they lost gathering with them in the Hereafter. What is the aspect of the loss?
* Student: That if they were believers and they were disbelievers, they will not meet them.
* The Shaykh: Because the families are in Paradise and these are in the Fire, correct.
* Student: And if they were disbelievers, likewise they will not meet them.
* The Shaykh: Yes, because each one is occupied with himself, correct.
Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss﴾ [Az-Zumar: 15]. Yes, by Allah. ﴿Unquestionably, that﴾: note the strong emphasis. ﴿Unquestionably (ala)﴾ is an opening particle, and its benefit is emphasis and alerting.
﴿That﴾ is a demonstrative pointing to its remoteness, because it is a far-reaching loss, and we seek refuge in Allah. He did not say ﴿this﴾, although its mention is near; but it is a far-reaching loss, so it is pointed to with a demonstrative of distance. Then it is restricted: he said ﴿it is the loss﴾, meaning nothing else; then it is emphasized by its severity: he said ﴿the manifest﴾, that is, the clear one which is hidden from no one. We ask Allah to make me and you among the winners (...).
* * *
There is a discussion.
Allah the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿Say, indeed I have been commanded to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Az-Zumar: 11].
His saying: ﴿I have been commanded﴾, who is the one who commands?
* Student: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
* The Shaykh: It is omitted?
* Student: Because it is known.
* The Shaykh: Yes, for its being known.
His saying: ﴿sincere to Him in religion﴾, the i'rab of ﴿sincere (mukhlisan)﴾?
* Student: A circumstantial clause (hal).
* The Shaykh: From where?
* Student: From the subject of ﴿worship (a'bud)﴾.
* The Shaykh: From the subject of ﴿a'bud﴾. And ﴿religion (al-din)﴾?
* Student: ﴿Al-din﴾ is the direct object of ﴿mukhlisan﴾.
* The Shaykh: The direct object of ﴿mukhlisan﴾. What is the meaning of making religion sincere (ikhlas al-din)?
* Student: It means making religion sincere to Allah, the Glorified and Exalted; i.e., directing worship to Him, the Glorified and Exalted, not to other than Him (...).
* Another student: (...).
* Another student: Purifying it from the impurities of shirk.
* The Shaykh: Yes, ikhlas... the sincerity of a thing is its purification from impurities, and the impurities here are the impurities of shirk.
﴿And I have been commanded to be the first of the Muslims﴾ [Az-Zumar: 12]. What is the meaning of the lam here?
* Student: ﴿And I have been commanded li-an akuna (to be)﴾ (...) the ba', meaning...
* The Shaykh: With the meaning of ba'; i.e., that I should be. Good, is there another aspect?
* Student: Yes, it is that the verb includes another verb which is transitive with this particle.
* The Shaykh: The estimate?
* Student: And I have been commanded that I worship Allah li-an akuna awwal al-muslimin.
* The Shaykh: That I worship Allah sincere to Him, li-an akuna...?
* Student: The first of the Muslims.
* The Shaykh: That is: for the sake of my being the first of the Muslims. The priority here?
* Student: Priority of precedence.
* The Shaykh: Precedence. And according to what the author held?
* Student: He said: (of this nation), to guard against there having been Muslim people before the Messenger ﷺ.
* The Shaykh: Yes, but this... according to the author's view, what is the priority here?
* Student: Priority of precedence and bestowal.
* The Shaykh: (Precedence) you mentioned yourself at first.
* Student: Before.
* Student: Priority of time, according to the author's view.
* The Shaykh: According to the author's view: priority of time.
* Student: And the second: priority of attribute.
* The Shaykh: Yes, priority of attribute, meaning what?
* Student: Meaning: the first who preceded in submitting to Islam.
* The Shaykh: Yes, well done.
His saying: ﴿the punishment of a great day﴾ [Az-Zumar: 13]. What made it accusative?
* Student: Because it is a direct object.
* The Shaykh: Direct object of what?
* Student: Of ﴿I fear (akhaf)﴾.
* The Shaykh: Of ﴿akhaf﴾. What is meant by the day?
* Student: The Day of Resurrection.
* The Shaykh: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So worship what you will besides Him﴾ [Az-Zumar: 15]. What is meant by the command here?
* Student: (...).
* Another student: Threat and challenge.
* The Shaykh: How is it a threat and how is it a challenge?
* Student: The author says: (...) threat (...) challenge.
* The Shaykh: How is it a threat and how is it a challenge?
* Student: The aspect of the threat is that it is impossible for the Messenger ﷺ to command them to worship anything besides Allah, the Glorified and Exalted; but it threatens them that they may worship what they wish besides Him, and Allah the Mighty and Majestic will call them to account for this worship and punish them for it.
And the aspect of the challenge is that he does not care that he worships Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and you worship what you wish besides Him, and he does not care about what they worship.
* The Shaykh: Correct. Now, his saying: ﴿they lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Az-Zumar: 15]: how is that?
* Student: According to the author's view, he lost what was prepared for him in Paradise of wide-eyed maidens (...).
* The Shaykh: That is, their families in Paradise had they believed.
* Student: (...) he lost his family, not gathering with them in Paradise.
* The Shaykh: What is the aspect of that? That is, what is the aspect of the loss in the family if what is meant is their families in the world; how does he lose them on the Day of Resurrection?
* Student: That is, they are separated, they did not gather with them, (...) went to Paradise (...) gathers them and their offspring (...).
* The Shaykh: How is the loss of the self?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: That is, they lost themselves on the Day of Resurrection; how did they lose it?
* Student: (...) loses what is with Allah from (...).
* Another student: (...).
* Another student: That is, he does not benefit from his life.
* The Shaykh: That is: he did not benefit from his life in this world, so he lost it in the Hereafter, whereas the believers profited. Well done.
﴿Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss﴾ [Az-Zumar: 15]. ﴿Unquestionably (ala)﴾?
* Student: ﴿Ala﴾ is an opening particle that conveys alerting.
* The Shaykh: Is there restriction in the sentence?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: What is its method?
* Student: The separating pronoun ﴿huwa﴾.
* The Shaykh: The separating pronoun ﴿huwa﴾.
Good, ﴿al-mubin (the manifest)﴾ (...) means what?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, what is the meaning of ﴿al-mubin﴾?
* Student: Its meaning is the clear.
* The Shaykh: The clear? Does the quadriliteral (abana) come with the meaning of clear? Because (bayyin) is from the triliteral, and (mubin) is from the quadriliteral.
* Student: It does come.
* The Shaykh: It comes; it is said: bana al-subhu, and abana al-subhu.
* * *
Have we taken the benefits?
* Student: We have not taken the benefits.
* The Shaykh: We have not taken them; then, God willing, we will take them.
Allah the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿Say, indeed I have been commanded to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Az-Zumar: 11].
* Among the benefits of this verse: that a person is commanded to proclaim what Allah has commanded of His worship; ﴿I have been commanded to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾. And for this there are two benefits:
* The first benefit: urging people to follow him in this.
* The second benefit: showing that Allah, the Glorified and Exalted, deserves this, and that He alone is deserving of being worshipped; ﴿Indeed I have been commanded to worship Allah, sincere﴾.
* Among the benefits of this verse: that sincerity is obligatory in worship, because he was commanded to worship Allah in this description: ﴿sincere to Him in religion﴾.
* Among its benefits: that whoever is not sincere has not carried out the command.
* It follows from this rule: that his deed is rejected, because of his saying..., so if he associates, he has done a deed on which there is no command of Allah and His Messenger, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever does a deed on which there is not our command, it is rejected" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697), and Muslim (1718/18), the wording is his, from the hadith of 'A'isha].
* Among the benefits of His saying: ﴿And I have been commanded to be the first of the Muslims﴾ [Az-Zumar: 12]: that it is obligatory to hasten to Islam without delay, because Allah commanded that; and this is based on the meaning of priority here being priority of attribute; i.e., precedence.
* Among the benefits of this verse: that the Messenger ﷺ is a commanded servant.
It follows from this that he has no part in the command, and Allah has declared this in His saying: ﴿You have no part in the affair﴾ [Al 'Imran: 128].
It also follows from this the misguidance of those people who call upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to relieve them, or to bring them good and ward off evil from them.
Then He said, the Exalted: ﴿Say, indeed I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a great day﴾ [Az-Zumar: 13].
* Among its benefits: that it is fitting, indeed obligatory, upon the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, to make this declaration known to the assembly: that he fears the punishment of a great day if he disobeys Allah; and its benefit, as we mentioned a little while ago: for the sake of following him in that, and for showing the greatness of Allah and that He deserves to be feared.
* Among its benefits: affirmation of the Last Day; because of His saying: ﴿the punishment of a great day﴾.
* Can it be derived from it that the Prophet ﷺ may commit sin?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Because of His saying: ﴿if I disobey﴾.
But someone may say: there is consideration in this; because the condition may be fulfilled or may not be fulfilled, and its fulfillment may be impossible, like His saying: ﴿Say, if the Most Merciful had a son, then I would be the first of the worshippers﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 81], and His saying to His Messenger: ﴿And it has already been revealed to you and to those before you: If you should associate others with Allah, your work would surely become worthless and you would surely be among the losers. But worship Allah, and be among the grateful﴾ [Az-Zumar: 65, 66].
So this benefit is open to consideration; because His saying: ﴿if I disobey﴾ does not indicate that disobedience occurs from him; but on the assumption that it occurs, then I fear.
Someone may say: his fearing is a certain matter: ﴿Indeed I fear﴾; and if it is a certain matter, then what is conditioned upon it, which is disobedience, is likewise; i.e., it may mean that if I disobey, then I fear.
In any case, it is established from the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, that he used to supplicate Allah to forgive him his sin, first and last [Muslim (483/216), from the hadith of Abu Hurayra]; and it is established that he ﷺ said: "O Allah, distance between me and my sins," "O Allah, cleanse me of my sins," "O Allah, wash me of my sins" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (744), and Muslim (598/147), from the hadith of Abu Hurayra].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the magnification of the Day of Resurrection and that it is a great day, and it follows from this that the sensible person should beware of it.
* Among its benefits: the permissibility of describing other than Allah with greatness; because of His saying: ﴿a great day﴾, and Allah the Exalted said about the Queen of Sheba: ﴿And she has a great throne﴾ [An-Naml: 23], and He described the slander as great... and so on; so describing other than Allah with greatness is not objectionable, but absolute greatness belongs only to Allah the Mighty and Majestic.
Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say, "It is Allah I worship, sincere to Him in my religion" (14). So worship what you will besides Him﴾ [Az-Zumar: 14, 15].
* It is derived from these two verses: that a person should proclaim the truth he is upon and not care about whoever opposes him; because of His saying: ﴿Say, "It is Allah I worship, sincere to Him in my religion" (14). So worship what you will besides Him﴾; i.e., I do not care about you; I will worship Allah and proceed on the sound path, and you proceed as you will.
* Among the benefits of the two verses: that the Prophet ﷺ is among the most adherent of people to the command of Allah; because he said earlier: ﴿Say, indeed I have been commanded to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Az-Zumar: 11], then he said here: ﴿Say, "It is Allah I worship, sincere to Him in my religion"﴾ [Az-Zumar: 14].
* Among the benefits of the two verses: that the Prophet ﷺ is in need of the deed that saves him from the punishment of Allah; because of His saying: ﴿sincere to Him in my religion﴾ with the yā' (my), by the addition, and this is so. And when he informed his companions that no one will enter Paradise by his deed, they said: "Nor you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Nor I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6463), and Muslim (2816/71), from the hadith of Abu Hurayra].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 39, verse 11–15 (part 3 of 3):

* Among the lessons of the two verses: the prohibition of worshipping other than Allah, which is derived from His saying: ﴿So worship what you wish besides Him﴾ [Az-Zumar 15], because we have mentioned that the command here is one of threat, and there is no threat except for something that opposes and disobeys.

* Among the lessons of the noble verse—His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves﴾ [Az-Zumar 15], and so on to the end—is the clarification that the grave loss with no gain accompanying it is the loss of these people: ﴿who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection﴾.

* In this verse there is also an indication that polytheism is the cause of this loss, because He followed His saying: ﴿So worship what you wish besides Him﴾ with ﴿Say, "Indeed, the losers..."﴾.

* Among its lessons: that the people of polytheism will not be gathered with their families on the Day of Resurrection, due to His saying: ﴿who have lost themselves and their families﴾.

* Among the lessons of the verse: the true lifespan of a person is what he has spent in obedience to Allah. For this reason Allah described these people as having lost themselves, because they did not do any good.

* Among the lessons of the verse: this loss is the greatest loss that can be, due to His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss﴾.

* * *

We did not speak yesterday about the pronoun of separation (ḍamīr al-faṣl), but you must have some knowledge of it. The pronoun of separation is a pronoun, not a noun according to the preferred opinion, so it has no place in i'rab (grammatical case analysis). Yet it is brought for three benefits:
The first?
* Student: So that the predicate is not confused with the adjective.
* Shaykh: So that the predicate is not confused with the adjective; that is, it separates the predicate from the adjective. This is clarified by an example: if you say, "Zayd al-fāḍil" (Zayd the virtuous), it is possible that "al-fāḍil" is an adjective and the predicate is omitted, i.e., Zayd the virtuous in the house, for example. But if you say, "Zayd huwa al-fāḍil" (Zayd is the virtuous one), it becomes definite that "al-fāḍil" is the predicate.
The second benefit of the pronoun of separation?
* Student: Restriction (al-ḥaṣr).
* Shaykh: Restriction, because when you say, "Zayd huwa al-fāḍil," it means: not anyone else, unlike if you say, "Zayd al-fāḍil," where he is virtuous but others may also be virtuous.
The third benefit?
* Student: Emphasis (al-tawkīd).
* Shaykh: Emphasis, because the speaker's saying, "Zayd huwa al-fāḍil," is more emphatic than his saying, "Zayd al-fāḍil."
As for (huwa), it has no place in i'rab, and the evidence for this in the Qur'an is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Perhaps we will follow the magicians if they are the victors﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara' 40]. Had it had a place in i'rab, it would have been a subject (mubtada'), and the word following it would have been in the nominative, and the verse would read: "Perhaps we will follow the magicians if they are the victors" (al-ghālibūna in the nominative).

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 39, verse 11–15 (part 1 of 3):

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say, "Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion."﴾ [Az-Zumar 11] ﴿Say﴾ means: O Muhammad. ﴿Indeed, I have been commanded﴾ means: my Lord has commanded me. This form comes in the passive voice because the one who commands is known. This resembles the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger ﷺ said: "I have been commanded to prostrate on seven bones"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (812) and Muslim (490 / 227), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]].

That the earth belongs to Allah, as His saying: ﴿And the earth of Allah is vast﴾ [Az-Zumar 10]. This is like what Musa said to his people: ﴿Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as inheritance to whom He wills of His servants, and the good outcome is for the righteous﴾ [Al-A'raf 128].

* Among its benefits: the virtue of patience, and that its possessor will be given his reward without account, by His saying: ﴿Indeed, the patient will be given their reward without account﴾ [Az-Zumar 10].
* Among its benefits: the generosity of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in that He made the reward equivalent to a wage, as if it were an exchange by which the worker is compensated, by His saying: ﴿their reward﴾.
* * *

Then He, the Exalted, said, at the beginning of today's lesson: ﴿Say, "Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion."﴾ [Az-Zumar 11].

﴿Say﴾ means: O Muhammad. ﴿Indeed, I have been commanded﴾ means: my Lord has commanded me. This form comes in the passive voice because the one who commands is known. This resembles the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger ﷺ said: "I have been commanded to prostrate on seven bones"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (812) and Muslim (490 / 227), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas.]], "I have been commanded"; because the one who commands is known, and He is Allah.

﴿Say, "Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion."﴾ The phrase ﴿I have been commanded to worship﴾ is used to point to the station of the Prophet ﷺ, that he is a servant who is commanded and forbidden, and that he has no share in the rights of Lordship.

He said: ﴿to worship Allah﴾, meaning: to humble myself before Him. Worship (al-'ibadah) is applied to two meanings:

The first meaning: humbling oneself before Allah, which is the act of the worshipper.

The second matter: that which is worshipped, namely the acts of worship in all their types.

On this basis, the definition of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah of worship in his saying is: "Worship is a comprehensive term for everything that Allah loves and is pleased with, of statements and deeds, both inward and outward." This is because worship, as I have said, is applied to two meanings.

* Student: "Humbling oneself," which is the act of the servant.
* The Shaykh: "Worship" (ta'abbud), and what is it?
* The student: Humbling oneself.
* The Shaykh: It has two meanings: the first meaning?
* The student: Humbling oneself (...), the second meaning...
* The Shaykh: That is, worship, which is the act of the servant. And the second?
* The student: The acts of worship.
* The Shaykh: Yes, that which is worshipped, namely the acts of worship. And according to this meaning is the explanation of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah in his saying: "Worship..."
* Student: (...).
* Another student: "Worship is a comprehensive term for everything that Allah loves and is pleased with, of statements and deeds, outward and inward."
* The Shaykh: Well done, complete.

Here, ﴿that I worship Allah, being sincere﴾ encompasses both meanings; that is, that I worship Him with worship.

His saying ﴿being sincere﴾ is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the subject of ﴿worship﴾; that is, while I am sincere to Allah. From what? From shirk (associating partners with Allah). Because sincerity (ikhlas) means purification, and purified from what? Purified from shirk. For when an act is mixed with shirk, it spoils and nullifies it. Allah said in the sacred hadith: "I am the most self-sufficient of partners in regard to partnership. Whoever does a deed in which he associates others with Me, I abandon him and his partnership"[[Narrated by Muslim (2985 / 46) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]].

His saying ﴿being sincere to Him in religion﴾: he said (from shirk). The meaning of religion (din) here is the deed that a person performs in order to be recompensed for it. Observe the explanation: the deed that a person does in order to be repaid for it. As for a deed that one does not hope to be repaid for, this is not called din, even though it is a deed. One must be acting in order to be repaid for this deed.

He, the Exalted, says: ﴿being sincere to Him in religion﴾. It has often passed for us that din is applied to the deed and is applied to the recompense. In His saying, ﴿Master of the Day of Recompense (din)﴾ [Al-Fatihah 4], it means the recompense; and in His saying: ﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion﴾ [Al-Kafirun 6], it means the deed.

﴿And I have been commanded to be the first of the Muslims﴾ [Az-Zumar 12]. The author, the commentator, said: (that is, "that"), making the lam (li) carry the meaning of the ba' (bi). This is because amara (to command) is normally transitive with ba' and not with lam; therefore the author explained it with ba'. This is one of the two approaches of the grammarians when a verb is followed by a particle with which it is not usually transitive: they make this particle carry the meaning of the particle with which the governing word (the verb or other word) is usually transitive. So here: ﴿I have been commanded li-an akuna﴾ they take the lam to mean ba'. And in His saying: ﴿a spring from which the servants of Allah drink﴾ [Al-Insan 6], they take the ba' to mean min ("from"); that is, they drink from it.

The second approach of the grammarians is that they change the verb into a verb suitable to the complement, and they call this tadmin (implication or conveying of meaning); that is, the verb has been made to imply another verb that is transitive with the particle mentioned. For example: ﴿the servants of Allah drink from it (bi-ha)﴾; they say the meaning is: they are quenched with it (yarwa bi-ha), so drinking (shurb) has been given the implied meaning of quenching (ri). There is no doubt that this gives the verse or text a greater meaning, because it keeps the particle as it is and gives the mentioned verb a meaning beyond what its wording indicates; therefore this approach is preferable.

But sometimes it is difficult for a student of knowledge, especially a beginner, to determine the suitable verb that would be implied by the mentioned verb; in that case he resorts to the easier option, which is changing the particle into a particle that suits the mentioned verb.

So here, in ﴿I have been commanded li-an akuna﴾, there is no doubt that it is easy to say: the lam means ba', and move on; that is: I have been commanded bi-an akuna.

But if we wish to imply in ﴿I have been commanded﴾ a meaning that suits the lam in ﴿li-an akuna﴾, it requires reflection and thought about the meaning: why did He say ﴿I have been commanded li-an akuna﴾? One may estimate: I have been commanded an a'bada Allah li-an akuna awwala al-muslimin (to worship Allah in order that I may be the first of the Muslims), so the lam is a causal particle linked to the omitted verb, which is: an a'bada Allah li-an akuna awwal al-muslimin. That is: the command was directed to me first so that I would be the first of the Muslims, that is, those who submit to the command of Allah. Then from this we derive two meanings: the meaning of the command, and the meaning of worship, which has been omitted so that the particle can be correctly attached to it.

He said: ﴿And I have been commanded to be the first of the Muslims﴾ (of this ummah). ﴿To be the first of the Muslims﴾: the author said: (of this ummah).

And the word ﴿Muslims﴾: Islam is applied to submission, because it is derived from: aslama amrahu ila ghayrihi (he entrusted his affair to another), and from it comes istislam in war, because one who surrenders submits to the victor who has overcome him.

So Islam is outward submission, and on this basis the hypocrites would be, what? Muslims outwardly. For this reason, Islam is applied to one of weak faith, as Allah said: ﴿The Bedouins say, "We have believed." Say, "You have not believed; but say, 'We have submitted'"﴾ [Al-Hujurat 14].

Sometimes Islam is applied to the entire Shari'ah, encompassing outward and inward submission, which is faith. Among this is His saying: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favor upon you, and approved for you Islam as a religion﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 3]. The intended meaning here is not merely outward submission, but all the laws: all the laws of Islam; ﴿I have approved for you Islam﴾, that is, all the laws of Islam, ﴿as a religion﴾.

The scholars say: when Islam is mentioned alongside faith, Islam is explained as outward deeds and faith as inward deeds. They said: among this is the hadith of Jibril, when he asked the Prophet ﷺ about Islam, and he said: "That you testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, establish the prayer, pay the zakah, fast Ramadan, and make pilgrimage to the House." And when he asked him about faith, he said: "That you believe in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, and that you believe in divine decree, its good and its evil"[[Narrated by Muslim (8 / 1) from the hadith of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab.]].

As for when one of them is mentioned alone, it includes the other: so Islam, when mentioned alone, encompasses all the laws, including faith; and faith, when mentioned alone, encompasses all the laws, including Islam.

He says here: ﴿And I have been commanded to be the first of the Muslims﴾ [Az-Zumar 12]. He said: (of this ummah). Why did he restrict the verse, although it is unrestricted: ﴿the first of the Muslims﴾? He restricted it because he, may Allah have mercy on him, understood that the priority here is priority in time; and if it is priority in time, it is not correct that the Prophet ﷺ be the first of the Muslims, why? Because before him there were many Muslim nations. So it was necessary to restrict this to the first of the Muslims of this ummah. Among this is His saying in Surat al-An'am, recite the verse: ﴿Indeed, my prayer, my sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds. No partner has He. And this I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims﴾ [Al-An'am 162-163]. According to the understanding the author adopted, we say: ﴿and I am the first of the Muslims﴾ of this ummah.

There is another possibility: that the priority here is priority of quality; that is, that I precede the Muslims in terms of advancing to Islam, as you might say to someone addressing you: if what you have said is true, then I am the first to contribute. For example, if he said: a charitable project has been opened in the town, and you said: if it is true, then I am the first to contribute; that is, "first" in terms of submission and quality. This is a possibility. If this meaning is in the noble verse, then we do not need the restriction the author mentioned, because we know that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is the first to submit to Allah, the Exalted, and that he is the greatest of people in submission and the most intense in it.

Then He said: ﴿Say, "Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day."﴾ [Az-Zumar 13]. ﴿The punishment﴾ is the object of what? Of ﴿disobey﴾?

* Student: Or of ﴿I fear﴾.
* The Shaykh: Or of ﴿if I disobey﴾?
* The student: Its origin is: I fear the punishment of.
* The Shaykh: I fear the punishment of; and it is not the object of ﴿disobey﴾. Why?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Punishment is not disobeyed; the meaning would be corrupted.

﴿Say, "Indeed, I fear"﴾: fear cannot be defined more clearly than by its own word. Everyone knows fear, does he not? For this reason we say: psychological states cannot be defined by anyone, because nothing is clearer than their own word; there is nothing clearer than their word, ever.

If a person said: define for me hatred, what would you say? You would say: hatred is well known; hatred is hatred.

Define for me love. You cannot; love is love.

* Student: Inclination.

* The Shaykh: No, inclination is among the effects of love; after one loves, one inclines. For this reason Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, says in Rawdat al-Muhibbin (and Allah knows best whether it is his or not): love cannot be bounded by anything clearer than its own word, ever. All those who defined it, and there are more than twenty definitions of it, explain it only by its necessary consequences and results. He spoke the truth, may Allah have mercy on him: psychological states, a person cannot define them better than by their own word.

﴿Fear﴾: if you asked a child who does not know definitions: what is the meaning of fear? He would say: fear is that I tremble, I shake. That is not possible; that is among its effects. Fear is that I flee; that is among its effects. So we say: fear is what? It is well known; it is fear.

﴿Indeed, I fear if I disobey my Lord﴾. ﴿Disobey﴾ (ma'siyah): opposition, and it occurs in two ways: either by leaving what is commanded or by doing what is forbidden. This is when it is separated from obedience; but if it is paired with obedience, obedience becomes doing what is commanded and disobedience becomes committing what is prohibited.

Here we say: ﴿disobey﴾ is separated from obedience, so what is the meaning?

* Student: It includes two meanings.
* The Shaykh: It includes two meanings: opposing Him, ﴿if I disobey my Lord﴾, that is, I oppose Him by doing what is forbidden or by leaving what is commanded.

In His saying ﴿my Lord﴾ there is an indication that He, the Mighty and Majestic, is the one who holds the command and the prohibition, because He is Lord, and the Lord is the Creator, the Owner, the Governor.

﴿The punishment of a tremendous day﴾ is the Day of Resurrection. Allah the Exalted described it in the Noble Qur'an with several attributes, among them: greatness (al-'izam), because of its severity, the severity of its terrors, and the severity of what happens in it. When you hear the attributes Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mentioned for this tremendous day, there will certainly overcome you a fear in proportion to your faith in it. Observe: the stronger a person's faith in the Last Day, the greater his fear of it; and the weaker his faith in the Last Day, the weaker his fear of it. For this reason we have a well-known saying: whoever knows Allah best fears Him most. And whoever also knows the Last Day best and has the strongest faith, has the strongest fear.

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous day (13). Say, "Allah I worship, being sincere to Him in my religion"﴾ [Az-Zumar 13-14]. In the first verse He said: ﴿So worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Az-Zumar 2], a command. In the second, He commanded him to announce that he is sincere to Allah in religion, to announce it. In the first, he himself does it: he worships Allah, being sincere to Him in religion. In the second, he was commanded to declare to the assembly that he is sincere, and declaring that he is sincere means that he disassociates himself from their shirk, because he is sincere to Allah.

﴿Say, "Allah I worship"﴾: its parsing? The name of Allah?

* Student: ﴿Say, "Allah"﴾?
* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: A subject.
* The Shaykh: A subject! Continue.
* Student: An object.
* The Shaykh: A subject and an object! Not possible; it is either a subject or an object.
* Student: An object.
* The Shaykh: An object of what?
* Student: Of ﴿say﴾.
* The Shaykh: Of ﴿say﴾, ﴿Say, "Allah I worship"﴾!
* Student: Of ﴿I worship﴾.
* The Shaykh: The object of ﴿I worship﴾?
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: Good, correct. ﴿Say, "Allah I worship"﴾ placed the object first for restriction; that is: I do not worship other than Him.

Its counterpart in structure is His saying in Surat al-Fatihah: ﴿You alone we worship﴾ [Al-Fatihah 5], where He placed the object first.

Here, ﴿Say, "Allah I worship"﴾ placed the object first to convey restriction, then He emphasized this by His saying: ﴿being sincere to Him in my religion﴾; that is, I do not worship other than Allah, and in my worship of Him I am also sincere to Him; no shirk mixes with my worship of Him: ﴿being sincere to Him in my religion﴾.

His saying ﴿my religion﴾ means: my deed. The author said: (from shirk).

If you combine the two verses: the first, ﴿Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Az-Zumar 11], and the second, you know the intensity of the Messenger's, peace and blessings be upon him, compliance with the command of his Lord, and that he worshipped Allah, being sincere to Him in religion, and announced that to the assembly, unconcerned with their opposition.

﴿So worship what you will besides Him﴾ [Az-Zumar 15]. ﴿So worship﴾ may be a threat and may be a challenge. The author says: (it contains a threat), but it may be a challenge.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 39, verse 11–15 (part 2 of 3):

As for its being a threat, it is evident, ﴿So worship what you will besides Him﴾; because he said after it: ﴿Say, indeed the losers are those who have lost themselves﴾ and so on [Az-Zumar: 15].
As for its being a challenge, it is because when he mentioned that he worships Allah alone, sincerely, he challenged them; he said: I do not care. You worship whatever you wish, and I do not care about you. So I will not associate anything with Allah; I will worship Allah alone, sincerely.
The rule we have in tafsir is that if a verse can bear two meanings that do not contradict each other, it is to be understood as both of them together.
Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So worship what you will besides Him﴾. ﴿What you will﴾ means: that which you will. ﴿Besides Him﴾ means: other than Him. Worship whatever you wish other than Him: a king, a saint, a tree, a stone, the sun, the moon, whoever you worship does not concern me. I will remain sincere to Allah, and you worship whatever you will.
The author says: (﴿Besides Him﴾, other than Him) i.e., apart from Him (it contains a threat to them and a declaration that they do not worship Allah). (Declaration) means announcement; i.e., this sentence contains the threat, and it contains that they do not worship Allah but worship other than Him.
﴿Say﴾ means: say to them, along with your challenging them and your threatening them, ﴿Indeed, the losers are those who have lost themselves﴾ [Az-Zumar: 15]. The sentence contains emphasis and it contains restriction. Where is the emphasis?
* Students: ﴿Indeed (inna)﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿Indeed (inna)﴾, ﴿indeed the losers﴾.
The restriction: both parts of the sentence are definite: ﴿the losers﴾, ﴿those who have lost﴾; so it is as if he said: Indeed the losers are those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection. Thus there is in it emphasis and restriction.
﴿Indeed the losers﴾: who is the loser? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, explained the loser in His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss, except those who believe﴾ [Al-Asr: 2, 3]. That is, loss (khusran) is the opposite of profit; for the one who trades either takes his capital, or he loses and receives less than his capital, or he profits and receives more.
The true loss is what Allah mentioned here: ﴿those who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Az-Zumar: 15]. These are the ones who have lost. The loser is not one who has lost millions of dirhams, nor one who has lost his family in this world, nor one who has lost himself in this world. The loser is one who has lost himself and his family, when? On the Day of Resurrection: he has lost himself and his family.
He says: (by the eternal abiding of their souls in the Fire, and by their not reaching the maidens of paradise prepared for them, had they believed).
His saying: (by the eternal abiding of their souls in the Fire) is an explanation of their losing themselves, for he has truly lost himself. What is the aspect of the loss?
The aspect of the loss is that he did not benefit from his life in this world for the Hereafter at all, so he lost himself, lost his life; all of it went as scattered dust. He lost himself. Had he been a sincere believer, he would have benefited; all his worldly life would have been a profit, because he would abide forever in Paradise, in which is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and what has not occurred to the heart of any human. But now he will abide forever in the Fire. This is the loss of the self.
The author explained the loss of the family as his missing the wide-eyed maidens in Paradise had he believed; and although this has a basis, it is far from the correct meaning. This is because the maidens in Paradise were never his family such that it could be said he lost them; rather, what is meant is that they lost their families, because their families, if they were believers, are in Paradise, and they will not gather with them; and if they were disbelievers, they are in the Fire and they will not gather with them either. Even if they were believers and their offspring were believers, they would be as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith – We will join them with their descendants﴾ [At-Tur: 21]. That is, no one will gather with his family in the Hereafter unless he and they are believers; then they will gather in a gathering with no separation after it. As for one who is not like that, there is no gathering.
In any case, the correct view is that what is meant by ﴿their families﴾ is their families who were in the world, since they lost gathering with them in the Hereafter. What is the aspect of the loss?
* Student: That if they were believers and they were disbelievers, they will not meet them.
* The Shaykh: Because the families are in Paradise and these are in the Fire, correct.
* Student: And if they were disbelievers, likewise they will not meet them.
* The Shaykh: Yes, because each one is occupied with himself, correct.
Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss﴾ [Az-Zumar: 15]. Yes, by Allah. ﴿Unquestionably, that﴾: note the strong emphasis. ﴿Unquestionably (ala)﴾ is an opening particle, and its benefit is emphasis and alerting.
﴿That﴾ is a demonstrative pointing to its remoteness, because it is a far-reaching loss, and we seek refuge in Allah. He did not say ﴿this﴾, although its mention is near; but it is a far-reaching loss, so it is pointed to with a demonstrative of distance. Then it is restricted: he said ﴿it is the loss﴾, meaning nothing else; then it is emphasized by its severity: he said ﴿the manifest﴾, that is, the clear one which is hidden from no one. We ask Allah to make me and you among the winners (...).
* * *
There is a discussion.
Allah the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿Say, indeed I have been commanded to worship Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ [Az-Zumar: 11].
His saying: ﴿I have been commanded﴾, who is the one who commands?
* Student: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
* The Shaykh: It is omitted?
* Student: Because it is known.
* The Shaykh: Yes, for its being known.
His saying: ﴿sincere to Him in religion﴾, the i'rab of ﴿sincere (mukhlisan)﴾?
* Student: A circumstantial clause (hal).
* The Shaykh: From where?
* Student: From the subject of ﴿worship (a'bud)﴾.
* The Shaykh: From the subject of ﴿a'bud﴾. And ﴿religion (al-din)﴾?
* Student: ﴿Al-din﴾ is the direct object of ﴿mukhlisan﴾.
* The Shaykh: The direct object of ﴿mukhlisan﴾. What is the meaning of making religion sincere (ikhlas al-din)?
* Student: It means making religion sincere to Allah, the Glorified and Exalted; i.e., directing worship to Him, the Glorified and Exalted, not to other than Him (...).
* Another student: (...).
* Another student: Purifying it from the impurities of shirk.
* The Shaykh: Yes, ikhlas... the sincerity of a thing is its purification from impurities, and the impurities here are the impurities of shirk.
﴿And I have been commanded to be the first of the Muslims﴾ [Az-Zumar: 12]. What is the meaning of the lam here?
* Student: ﴿And I have been commanded li-an akuna (to be)﴾ (...) the ba', meaning...
* The Shaykh: With the meaning of ba'; i.e., that I should be. Good, is there another aspect?
* Student: Yes, it is that the verb includes another verb which is transitive with this particle.
* The Shaykh: The estimate?
* Student: And I have been commanded that I worship Allah li-an akuna awwal al-muslimin.
* The Shaykh: That I worship Allah sincere to Him, li-an akuna...?
* Student: The first of the Muslims.
* The Shaykh: That is: for the sake of my being the first of the Muslims. The priority here?
* Student: Priority of precedence.
* The Shaykh: Precedence. And according to what the author held?
* Student: He said: (of this nation), to guard against there having been Muslim people before the Messenger ﷺ.
* The Shaykh: Yes, but this... according to the author's view, what is the priority here?
* Student: Priority of precedence and bestowal.
* The Shaykh: (Precedence) you mentioned yourself at first.
* Student: Before.
* Student: Priority of time, according to the author's view.
* The Shaykh: According to the author's view: priority of time.
* Student: And the second: priority of attribute.
* The Shaykh: Yes, priority of attribute, meaning what?
* Student: Meaning: the first who preceded in submitting to Islam.
* The Shaykh: Yes, well done.
His saying: ﴿the punishment of a great day﴾ [Az-Zumar: 13]. What made it accusative?
* Student: Because it is a direct object.
* The Shaykh: Direct object of what?
* Student: Of ﴿I fear (akhaf)﴾.
* The Shaykh: Of ﴿akhaf﴾. What is meant by the day?
* Student: The Day of Resurrection.
* The Shaykh: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So worship what you will besides Him﴾ [Az-Zumar: 15]. What is meant by the command here?
* Student: (...).
* Another student: Threat and challenge.
* The Shaykh: How is it a threat and how is it a challenge?
* Student: The author says: (...) threat (...) challenge.
* The Shaykh: How is it a threat and how is it a challenge?
* Student: The aspect of the threat is that it is impossible for the Messenger ﷺ to command them to worship anything besides Allah, the Glorified and Exalted; but it threatens them that they may worship what they wish besides Him, and Allah the Mighty and Majestic will call them to account for this worship and punish them for it.
And the aspect of the challenge is that he does not care that he worships Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and you worship what you wish besides Him, and he does not care about what they worship.
* The Shaykh: Correct. Now, his saying: ﴿they lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Az-Zumar: 15]: how is that?
* Student: According to the author's view, he lost what was prepared for him in Paradise of wide-eyed maidens (...).
* The Shaykh: That is, their families in Paradise had they believed.
* Student: (...) he lost his family, not gathering with them in Paradise.
* The Shaykh: What is the aspect of that? That is, what is the aspect of the loss in the family if what is meant is their families in the world; how does he lose them on the Day of Resurrection?
* Student: That is, they are separated, they did not gather with them, (...) went to Paradise (...) gathers them and their offspring (...).
* The Shaykh: How is the loss of the self?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: That is, they lost themselves on the Day of Resurrection; how did they lose it?
* Student: (...) loses what is with Allah from (...).
* Another student: (...).
* Another student: That is, he does not benefit from his life.
* The Shaykh: That is: he did not benefit from his life in this world, so he lost it in the Hereafter, whereas the believers profited. Well done.
﴿Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss﴾ [Az-Zumar: 15]. ﴿Unquestionably (ala)﴾?
* Student: ﴿Ala﴾ is an opening particle that conveys alerting.
* The Shaykh: Is there restriction in the sentence?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: What is its method?
* Student: The separating pronoun ﴿huwa﴾.
* The Shaykh: The separating pronoun ﴿huwa﴾.
Good, ﴿al-mubin (the manifest)﴾ (...) means what?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: No, what is the meaning of ﴿al-mubin﴾?
* Student: Its meaning is the clear.
* The Shaykh: The clear? Does the quadriliteral (abana) come with the meaning of clear? Because (bayyin) is from the triliteral, and (mubin) is from the quadriliteral.
* Student: It does come.
* The Shaykh: It comes; it is said: bana al-subhu, and abana al-subhu.
