* Shaykh: Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Then is one upon whom the word of punishment has come﴾ [Az-Zumar 19]. The hamzah here is for interrogation. It may be that what is meant is a genuine question, or that what is meant is denial, i.e., negation; this will become clear from its interpretation.

His saying: ﴿upon whom the word has come﴾, i.e., it became obligatory upon him. The verb is masculine even though *kalimah* (word) is feminine, for two reasons:

The first reason: the feminine marking of *kalimah* is metaphorical (majazi).

The second: it is separated from its governing element, and the verb must be feminine only when the subject is a real feminine, attached to it, as Ibn Malik said:

*"It is obligatory for the verb only with a pronoun attached, or one that conveys a feminine of real gender."*

His saying: ﴿Then is one upon whom the word of punishment has come﴾, i.e., the word of punishment became obligatory upon him, which is that they will not believe, even if every sign comes to them; or, as the author said: ﴿"I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind, all together"﴾ [Hud 119]. The first is more apparent.

His saying: ﴿the word of punishment﴾ means the word by which they deserve punishment, which is that everyone who opposes the command of Allah deserves punishment. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Would you then save one who is in the Fire?﴾ [Az-Zumar 19]. ﴿Would you then﴾: the address is to the Messenger ﷺ. That is: would you save him if the word of punishment has come upon him? The answer is no. And if the answer is no, when the answer to an interrogative is "no," this is a sign that the interrogation is for negation. Here we ask about the hamzah in ﴿Then is one who﴾ and the hamzah in ﴿Would you then﴾: does each have an independent meaning, or is the second an emphasis of the first?
* Student: An emphasis of the first.
* Shaykh: If we consider the two sentences as one sentence, that is, if we consider the speech as one in both sentences, then the second is an emphasis of the first. And if we consider each sentence independent of the other, then the second is original, that is, foundational, not emphatic. In any case, such a construction, that is, when the interrogative hamzah comes followed by a conjunctive particle, has previously been mentioned to us many times: the grammarians have two views on its i'rab (grammatical analysis). Some hold that the hamzah is attached to an implied sentence suited to the context, and the fa' and the conjunctive particle are attached to that omitted sentence.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 39, verse 16–20 (part 4 of 5):

Some scholars hold that the interrogative particle (hamza) governs the sentence that follows the conjunction, so the conjunction links it to what came before. The hamza is placed first because it has precedence (ṣadr). We have mentioned that the second view is easier, because the first view may make it difficult for a person to know what fits the context, or he may assume what he thinks fits when it does not fit.

Allah the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Then are you going to rescue﴾. To whom is the address? To the Prophet (ﷺ). ﴿Rescue﴾ means: bring out. But explaining ﴿tunqidh﴾ as (bring out) is deficient, because the word "bring out" does not indicate that the one brought out has been saved from destruction. However, "rescue" (tunqidh) indicates a more specific meaning than "bring out", is that not so? Therefore we should not explain the more specific by the more general, because if you explain the more specific by the more general, you diminish the explanation: bringing out may be a rescue and may be not a rescue, but rescue occurs from destruction. For this reason, if you explained tunqidh as tunji (deliver), it would be clearer, because deliverance (injā') also occurs from destruction. ﴿Then are you going to rescue﴾, i.e. deliver ﴿those who are in the Fire﴾ from its punishment. ﴿Man fī al-nār﴾: (man) means "the one who", and it is the object of (tunqidh). ﴿Fī al-nār﴾ is a prepositional phrase (jār wa majrūr) attached to what? 
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: The estimated verb?
* Student: As if it means "settled in the Fire".
* Another student: "Remained in the Fire".
* The Shaykh: "Who entered the Fire".
* Student: "Remained" or "entered"?
* The Shaykh: It is estimated according to what fits.
* Student: "Inside" (dākhil).
* The Shaykh: No, "dākhil" does not suit the relative clause (ṣilat al-mawṣūl), pay attention.
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: "Dākhil" does not suit the relative clause, because if you estimate "dākhil" you need to estimate a subject (mubtada') to make it a sentence; but if you estimate a verb, we need nothing else. For example, in every relative clause, only a verb is estimated, because if you estimate a noun you need to estimate a subject to complete the sentence, so the estimation becomes twofold, whereas if you estimate a verb the estimation is single.
﴿Then are you going to rescue those who are in the Fire﴾, i.e. those who have settled in the Fire, or those who entered the Fire, or those who were in the Fire, the meaning is close.

The author said: (the answer to the condition). Where is the condition? The condition is (man) in His saying ﴿Then is he who has been justly due...﴾, and this is one of the two views regarding (man): that it is a conditional noun. Some scholars said: (man) is a relative pronoun, meaning: "Is then he upon whom the word of punishment is due, can you rescue him?" Conditional nouns and relative nouns are always interchangeable; that is, each is used in place of the other.

He says: (the answer to the condition, and the apparent noun was placed in the position of the pronoun). The apparent noun, which is (man), was placed in the position of the pronoun which would be used if not for the apparent noun in this way: "Then are you going to rescue him?" "Then is he upon whom the word of punishment is due, then are you going to rescue him?" This statement of the author suggests that the two sentences are connected to each other and that neither is independent of the other ("then are you going to rescue him").

But we say: there is another possibility, different from what the author said, namely that the second is separate from the first, and that the estimate of the first is: ﴿Is then he upon whom the word of punishment is due﴾ [do you] repel from (ʾaw a word similar to it), meaning: "Then do you repel from him upon whom the word of punishment is due?" Then he resumed and said: ﴿Then are you going to rescue those who are in the Fire﴾. That is, the first is that you make him a believer so that he does not deserve the Fire, and the second is that you rescue him from the Fire once he has entered it. This is one view of the exegetes.

The second view is that the two sentences are one; the meaning of ﴿Then is he upon whom the word of punishment is due﴾ is "he is in the Fire; then are you going to rescue him from it?" This is the view the author followed.

Ultimately, the two sentences amount to the same thing: that whoever the word of punishment is due upon, it is not possible, neither for the Messenger (ﷺ) nor for anyone else, to rescue him from the Fire.

The author says: (and the apparent noun was placed in the position of the pronoun). Placing the apparent noun in the position of the pronoun here conveys several meanings, among them: that whoever the word of punishment is due upon is in the Fire; because if He had said, "Then are you going to rescue him?", a person would say, "From what would I rescue him?"

When He says, "Then are you going to rescue those who are in the Fire?", we know that the one upon whom the word of punishment is due is in the Fire.

The author says: (and the interrogative hamza is for denial). The hamza in ﴿afa-man﴾ and in ﴿afa-anta tunqidh﴾ is one hamza, according to the view that the two sentences are one, so the second is an emphasis of the first. The summary is that Allah says to the Messenger (ﷺ), peace be upon him: can you prevent the one for whom the word of punishment has been decreed from deserving it? Can you rescue the one who has entered the Fire?

The answer: No, neither this nor that; because the Prophet (ﷺ) does not have the power to guide anyone so that the word of punishment is not due upon him, nor can he rescue anyone from the Fire.

The Prophet (ﷺ) said, when the verse was revealed, "And warn your closest kindred" [al-Shu'ara' 214]: he gathered his relatives and began to single them out: "O so-and-so, son of so-and-so, I cannot avail you anything against Allah," until he said, "O Fatimah, daughter of Muhammad, ask me for whatever you wish from my wealth, I cannot avail you anything against Allah" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3527), and Muslim (204 / 348) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. She was his daughter. He is saying: wealth I can benefit you with, but I cannot avail you anything against Allah. And if he cannot avail his own daughter anything, then anyone else is all the more so.

If someone asks: how do we reconcile this with the intercession of the Prophet (ﷺ) for his uncle Abu Talib, "until he was in a shallow part of the Fire, and upon him were two sandals of fire, from which his brain boils" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3883), and Muslim (209 / 357) from the hadith of al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib.]]? How? Here I could avail, and here intercession was made and it benefited. It is said: first, the Messenger (ﷺ) was not able to bring him out of the Fire, and if he was not able to bring him out of the Fire, there is no contradiction with the verse, because Allah said: ﴿Then are you going to rescue those in the Fire?﴾ He did not rescue him.

Second: the lightening of punishment for Abu Talib was not because he was the uncle of the Messenger (ﷺ), for Abu Lahab was his uncle too, yet he availed him nothing. Rather, it was because of his great defence of Islam and of the Messenger of Islam, for he defended him with a tremendous defence; indeed he used to praise the Messenger (ﷺ) in gatherings, and even testified to his prophethood, saying:

They have certainly known that our son is not a liar among us, nor is he one who is concerned with false words.

This is a verse from his famous lamiyya, of which Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said: this should be counted among the Mu'allaqat; indeed it is more eloquent than the Mu'allaqat.

The Mu'allaqat are odes that the Arabs selected; they called them the Seven Mu'allaqat, and they added three to them and called them the Ten Mu'allaqat. These odes were hung inside the Ka'bah to preserve them and to honour them. But the lamiyya of Abu Talib is more and more (i.e. better, sweeter and more eloquent). He testified for the Messenger (ﷺ) that he is not a liar, and that he is not concerned with the speech of the falsehood-mongers. Indeed the Prophet (ﷺ) was the most truthful of people and the most pure of people. Then he says in another ode:

And I have known that the religion of Muhammad is among the best religions of mankind in religion.
Were it not for blame, or fear of insult, you would have seen me gladly declaring it clearly.

Such words, if people hear them, would lead them to faith; in reality it is a call to Islam, but he himself was not a Muslim. We ask Allah for well-being.

So the lightening of punishment for him was not because he was the uncle of the Messenger, but because he defended Islam and protected the Prophet (ﷺ) with complete protection. Also he supported him, for after the death of his grandfather 'Abd al-Muttalib he was with his uncle Abu Talib, as is well known. So from Allah's justice, the Mighty and Majestic, He thanked him for his deed and lightened his punishment through the intercession of the Prophet (ﷺ), until he became, as you have heard, in a shallow part of the Fire, with two sandals of fire upon him from which his brain boils. May Allah protect me and you from the Fire. ﴿Then are you going to rescue those who are in the Fire?﴾

He says: (the meaning: you cannot guide him so as to rescue him from the Fire). This is the meaning, and Allah the Glorified and Exalted spoke the truth. A human being can never rescue anyone from the Fire at all. If the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) cannot do that, then whoever is below him is all the more so.

Then Allah the Exalted says: ﴿But those who feared their Lord﴾. This exception is among the finest, for when He said ﴿Then are you going to rescue those who are in the Fire?﴾, He made an exception to this situation, the situation of those who do not enter the Fire; so He said: ﴿But those who feared their Lord, for them are chambers above which are built chambers, beneath which rivers flow﴾ [al-Zumar 20], and so on to the end. Here "lakin" (but) does not operate because it is?
* Student: Lightened (mukhaffafa).
* The Shaykh: Lightened, and "lakin" when lightened is only for mere conjunction, and its meaning is exception (istidrak). So ﴿alladhina﴾ is the subject (mubtada'), and its predicate is the clause ﴿lahum ghuraf﴾; this is the predicate.

He says: (﴿But those who feared their Lord﴾: by obeying Him). The exegete, may Allah have mercy on him, informed us that taqwa is obedience, and this is the most comprehensive of what has been said about taqwa: that it is obedience to Allah the Mighty and Majestic by carrying out His command and avoiding His prohibition; because He commands and forbids, not for desire. For this reason, whoever obeys Allah merely out of desire is not like whoever obeys Allah because Allah commanded or forbade. Many people obey Allah because their souls desire that, but true obedience is that whose motive is carrying out Allah's command, abandoning what is forbidden and doing what is commanded.

﴿But those who feared their Lord﴾: He said ﴿feared their Lord﴾, indicating that their taqwa toward Allah is founded on a basis, because He is their Lord; and lordship here includes both divine lordship (rubūbiyya qadariyya) and legislative lordship (rubūbiyya shar'iyya), because Allah is Lord, possessor of the universe by decree (qadar) and possessor of judgment by legislation (shar'). So they fear their Lord because He created them, provided for them, equipped them and sustained them; they worship their Lord because He is the one who judges over them, who commands them and forbids them, so they carry out His command and abandon His prohibition.

﴿For them are chambers above which are built chambers﴾ [al-Zumar 20]: ghuraf is the plural of ghurfa, and a ghurfa is a high building; if it is at the bottom it is called ḥujra, and if it is above it is called ghurfa, so a high building is called a ghurfa. These chambers are built chambers; He says ﴿above which are built chambers﴾, meaning: storeys, lofty palaces, built of bricks of gold and silver: two gardens of gold, their vessels and what is in them, and two gardens of silver, their vessels and what is in them. These chambers built of gold and silver are also not like what is seen in this world of shine and attractive beauty; rather they are far greater and more magnificent. We cannot at all imagine the beauty of these chambers or the materials of their construction. Why? Because Allah says: ﴿No soul knows what has been hidden for them of comfort for their eyes as a reward for what they used to do﴾ [al-Sajdah 17], and in the sacred hadith He says: "I have prepared for My righteous servants what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived" [[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3244), and Muslim (2824 / 2) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]].

The Garden, in it, there is nothing of what is in this world except the names alone, but the realities differ greatly from it: there are grapes, date palms, pomegranates, but they are not like what we have in this world; rather they are something no human being can imagine. This Garden is prepared for the God-fearing who fear their Lord, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And race towards forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is the heavens and the earth, prepared for the muttaqun﴾ [Aal 'Imran 133]. The work is light and the reward is great, but the work is light, my brothers, for whoever Allah makes it easy for; and Allah makes it easy for whoever is sincere in intention toward Allah and does not incline toward this world, because inclining to this world, especially for one whom Allah has given knowledge, is humiliation and degradation: ﴿And recite to them the story of the one to whom We gave Our verses, but he detached himself from them, so Satan followed him, and he became of those who go astray. And had We willed, We would have raised him thereby, but he inclined toward the earth and followed his desire﴾ [al-A'raf 175-176].

And the example, the basest of examples: ﴿So his example is like the example of the dog: if you chase it, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants. That is the example of the people who denied Our signs﴾ [al-A'raf 176]. ﴿So relate the stories﴾, and so on to the end.

So we say: these chambers are what Allah prepared for the God-fearing who sincerely intended Allah, hoping to reach His reward, and who perform no act of obedience except while believing that it has a reward in this Garden; because this belief and this feeling move you to perfect worship. When you know that there is no act of worship you perform except for the sake of reaching this reward, you will be eager to act and to perfect the action.

﴿For them are chambers above which are built chambers, beneath which rivers flow﴾: ﴿beneath which﴾ means: beneath these high chambers and what is below them. ﴿The rivers﴾ is the plural of nahar or nahr; because nahar or nahr, with a guttural letter as its second radical, like nahar and bahar, allows both vowelling the second letter and not vowelling it; you say nahar and nahr, and bahar and bahr. Here we say anhar is the plural of nahr. They are four kinds, which Allah clarified in Surah Muhammad, saying: ﴿The example of the Garden which the God-fearing have been promised: in it are rivers﴾ [Muhammad 15]. Read.
* Student: ﴿Therein are rivers of water unaltered, and rivers﴾.
* The Shaykh: ﴿And rivers of milk﴾, before it.
* Student: ﴿And rivers of milk whose taste does not change, and rivers of wine, delicious to those who drink, and rivers of purified honey﴾ [Muhammad 15].
* The Shaykh: Yes. These are four kinds: in it are rivers of water unaltered, meaning not liable to becoming altered, and "āsin" means changed; and you know that when water remains in a vessel for a period, or in its place in a well for a period, it changes. ﴿And rivers of milk whose taste has not changed, and rivers of wine, delicious to those who drink﴾, and in it is no intoxication.
﴿And rivers of purified honey﴾: rivers, not milked from udders, nor coming from bees; rivers flowing over the earth, running, and it has come in a report that they flow without a trench. Do you know the trench? What do you call it?
* Students: A channel.
* The Shaykh: Yes. They remain as channels on the surface of the earth, not needing digging of irrigation ditches nor walls preventing the flow of water; rather they flow without anything, and it is also reported that they flow at the person's choice, he directs the river wherever he wishes, and holds it wherever he wishes, because Allah says: ﴿And therein is what the souls desire and what the eyes delight in, and you therein will abide forever﴾ [al-Zukhruf 71]. We ask Allah to make us and you among them.
* Student: Shaykh, may Allah reward you well, there is a saying that the Nile, Seyhan, Ceyhan and the Euphrates are from Paradise?
* The Shaykh: Yes, indeed, there is a hadith about it.
* Student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: There is a hadith about it, but they said: they resemble the rivers of Paradise in clarity; it does not mean they came down from heaven.
* Student: A eloquent simile (tashbih baligh).
* The Shaykh: Yes, an eloquent simile.
* Student: Divine lordship (rubūbiyya qadariyya) and legislative lordship (shar'iyya)?
* The Shaykh: What?
* Student: The qadariyya and the shar'iyya.
* The Shaykh: I don't know what you are saying?

* The Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: The qadariyya and the shar'iyya.
* The Shaykh: Yes.

* The Shaykh: You did not understand it. Yes, legislative lordship is the disposal of people by the Shari'a.
* Student: That is (...).
* The Shaykh: The command and prohibition; and the decreed one is well known, and this is why such a thing has passed us before: the ruling is kawni (cosmic)...
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: And shar'i (legislative), the same disposal according to the requirement of lordship, cosmic and legislative.
* Student: (...), O Shaykh.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 39, verses 16–20 (part 5 of 5):**

* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Tafsir (explanation) here means strengthening oneself through obedience, yes.
* Student: Some people (...).
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: Does he receive reward for this act of his?
* Shaykh: By Allah, in every case, his duty (dhimmah) is discharged by it. But he will not reach the level of perfection. For this reason we always say: when a person performs an act of worship, he should have two intentions: the intention of the act (niyyat al-'amal) and the intention of the one for whom the act is done (niyyat al-ma'mul lah). The intention of the act is one that everyone has. They intend, so this one comes to pray Dhuhr and intends the Dhuhr prayer. But the intention of the one for whom the act is done, that he seeks by it nearness to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is something a person often neglects, and Satan prevents him from it.
Here there is also a third intention: the intention of following the Messenger (ﷺ), the intention of following him. All these meanings, we ask Allah to pardon us, are often absent from us: neither the intention of complying with the command, which is the intention of the one for whom the act is done, nor the intention of following the Messenger (ﷺ). For when you intend this, or when you feel this intention, you love Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and you love the Messenger, and you feel that you are a servant of Allah who follows the Messenger of Allah, and you find in the worship a flavor you do not find when you perform it merely as a habit. For this reason we say: the habits of the one granted success are acts of worship, and the acts of worship of the heedless are mere habits. Yes indeed (...).
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: (Man)?
* Student: (Man) as a relative pronoun (...).
* Shaykh: Is there no other opinion?
* Student: Or as a conditional particle.
* Shaykh: Or as a conditional particle.
What is meant by His saying: ﴿Then, would you save one who is deserving of the punishment in the Fire?﴾ [Az-Zumar 19]? To whom is the address directed?
* Student: The address is to the Prophet (ﷺ).
* Shaykh: Yes.
* Student: The interrogation is for negation.
* Shaykh: For negation, like the first.

* Shaykh: Well done. His saying: ﴿But those who feared their Lord﴾ — what is the benefit of this exception (istidrak)?

* Shaykh: Yes, conjunction. But the istidrak is from what?
* Student: The istidrak: it clarified that the punishment befalls some people, so it corrected this with this verse, bringing out the people...
* Shaykh: That is, when He said, for example: ﴿Is then one against whom the word of punishment has been justified﴾ [Az-Zumar 19], He corrected it by saying: ﴿But those who feared their Lord﴾ [Az-Zumar 20], meaning: they are not those upon whom it has been justified. What is the i'rab (grammatical analysis) of ﴿alladhina ittaqaw﴾?
* Student: ﴿Alladhina ittaqaw﴾, the i'rab?
* Shaykh: Yes, ﴿But those who feared﴾.
* Student: ﴿ittaqaw﴾?
* Shaykh: ﴿Alladhina﴾.
* Student: ﴿Alladhina﴾ is one of the demonstrative nouns.
* Shaykh: ﴿Alladhina﴾ a demonstrative noun?!
* Student: ﴿Lakin﴾...
* Shaykh: ﴿Lakin﴾ is a particle of istidrak. And ﴿alladhina﴾?
* Student: ﴿Alladhina﴾ is a demonstrative noun.
* Shaykh: A demonstrative noun ﴿alladhina﴾?! The demonstrative noun is: this, these, those.
* Student: ﴿Alladhina﴾...
* Shaykh: Have you not studied grammar?
* Student: ﴿Alladhina﴾ is a relative pronoun (ism mawsul), built on the fatha, in a position of nominative as a subject (mubtada').
* Shaykh: Yes. ﴿Alladhina﴾ is a relative pronoun built on the fatha, in a nominative position as a subject. Where is its predicate? The predicate of ﴿alladhina﴾?
* Student: ﴿Ittaqaw﴾.
* Shaykh: No, ﴿ittaqaw﴾ is the relative clause (silat al-mawsul).
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Where is it? Is the prepositional phrase its predicate or not?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: The prepositional phrase. Apparently it is contradicted (mu'arid), yes.
* Student: The sentence: ﴿For them are chambers﴾ [Az-Zumar 20].
* Shaykh: The sentence ﴿For them are chambers﴾: a prepositional phrase serving as a fronted predicate for (ghuraf, chambers).
* We take the benefits. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The promise of Allah; Allah does not fail in (His) promise﴾ [Az-Zumar 20]. ﴿Promise﴾ (wa'd). The author says: (in the accusative by an implied verb). That is: they were promised the promise of Allah. Or, according to another possible opinion, the estimate is: the promise of Allah was fulfilled for them, meaning Allah fulfilled His promise to them. On this view it is in the accusative by a verb supplied from outside its own verb. As for the author's view, it is a verbal noun (masdar) with its governing verb omitted.
He, may Allah have mercy on him, says: Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The promise of Allah; Allah does not fail in (His) promise﴾. The commentator said: (His promise). This indicates that the definite article (al) here stands in place of a pronoun, and that al-mi'ad (the promise) means al-wa'd (the promise). His saying: ﴿Allah does not fail in the promise﴾ means that He does not fail in what He promised by anything else, because (akhlafa, to fail/break) indicates the replacement of one thing by another, as Allah said: ﴿And whatever you spend, He will replace it﴾ [Saba' 39]. Unlike (khalafa), which indicates that one thing succeeds another; one says khalafahu, meaning he came after him. Akhlafahu means he made a substitute for him. For this reason the afflicted person says: "O Allah, reward me in my affliction and give me in exchange something better than it," meaning give me a substitute for it.
His saying: ﴿Allah does not fail in the promise﴾ is so because of the perfection of His truthfulness and the perfection of His power, since failing in a promise is either due to the lying of the promiser or due to his inability, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is exalted above both. So He is perfect in truthfulness and perfect in power.
In this verse, ﴿Is then one against whom the word of punishment has been justified﴾, to its end, there is evidence. Among its benefits: whoever has the word of punishment justified against him has no guide. Supporting this is His saying: ﴿Whomever Allah sends astray, there is no guide for him, and He leaves them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [Al-A'raf 186].
* Among its benefits: the affirmation of the speech of Allah, for the one who decrees the punishment is Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and no other. So the word of punishment proceeds from Allah, and in this is the affirmation of speech for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. The whole Qur'an, every letter of it, affirms the speech of Allah. Why?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No. In every letter of the Qur'an there is an affirmation of the speech of Allah.
* Student: Because it is with words, sound and letters.
* Shaykh: Because it is the speech of Allah, so every letter of it is the speech of Allah, since the speech of Allah consists of letters and sound.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the Prophet (ﷺ) cannot save those in the Fire. And if this holds for the Messenger (ﷺ), then it holds for others all the more.
* Among its benefits: whoever has the word of punishment justified against him is in the Fire, because we said that the apparent noun here stands in place of the pronoun, and the estimate is: "Will you save him?"
* Among the benefits of this verse: the eloquence of the Qur'an and the severity of its warnings, for it presents this severe style that cuts through the heart that is alive and aware: ﴿Is then one against whom the word of punishment has been justified, will you save one who is in the Fire?﴾ [Az-Zumar 19]. This is a very severe style, and there is no doubt that a severe style in its proper place counts as eloquence (balaghah), because eloquence is for speech to correspond to what the situation requires, meaning what the situation calls for of gentleness, severity, extension or brevity.
* Among the benefits of this verse: the affirmation of the Fire. The Fire is the second abode in which humans and jinn settle. It is the abode of those who transgress and disbelieve. It exists now, and it will remain forever and ever.
Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿But those who feared their Lord﴾, to its end. In this is a clarification of the high rank of the God-fearing, for the istidrak here is as if it lifts them out of what was mentioned earlier of the severe threat to those against whom the word of punishment has been justified.
* Among its benefits: piety is a cause for entering Paradise, by His saying: ﴿For them are chambers﴾, to its end.
* Among its benefits: their fear of Allah has a prior cause and a subsequent cause. The special lordship in His saying ﴿their Lord﴾ required that they fear Him, and they fear their Lord who will reward them. So piety has a cause, which is Allah's care for them, the Mighty and Majestic; this is the prior cause. And it has a subsequent cause, which is the reward from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, that they hope for. All of this is attributed to piety. He is their Lord in that He granted them success in piety, and He is their Lord in that He rewarded them for it.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the dwellings of Paradise are chambers built one above another, by His saying: ﴿For them are chambers, above them are chambers built﴾ [Az-Zumar 20]. Do these chambers differ according to the deeds? The answer is yes. The Messenger (ﷺ) explained that there are two gardens of Paradise made of gold, their vessels and what is in them, and two gardens made of silver, their vessels and what is in them.[Narrated by al-Bukhari (4878) and Muslim (180/296) with their chains from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Two gardens of silver, their vessels and what is in them, and two gardens of gold, their vessels and what is in them..." — the hadith.]
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the perfection of bliss, for these chambers have rivers flowing beneath them, and in them are trees and everything a person could wish for, and even more than that.
* Among the benefits of the verse: this bliss is established by the promise of Allah, by His saying: ﴿The promise of Allah﴾.
* Among its benefits: the affirmation that Allah does not fail in His promise, because of the perfection of His truthfulness and His power. In it is the affirmation of perfect truthfulness and the affirmation of perfect power.

Then Allah the Exalted said, and we begin this lesson with it: ﴿For them there will be layers of fire above them, and beneath them layers﴾ [al-Zumar 16]. The pronoun in ﴿for them﴾ refers to ﴿the losers who have lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [al-Zumar 15], and they are the disbelievers.

﴿Layers of fire above them﴾: from above their heads. The phrase ﴿from above them﴾ indicates that these layers encompass them.

As for His saying ﴿layers﴾, the author said: (tiers, ﴿of fire﴾). These tiers of fire, we do not know their modality. We do not know whether they are heated iron, or stones, or something else. But if we reflect on His saying the Exalted: ﴿Its fuel is people and stones﴾ [al-Baqarah 24], we may say that they are of stones, though not like our stones; rather they are stones whose modality is unknown.

As for His saying ﴿and beneath them layers﴾, meaning (of fire), as the author said. This is like His saying the Exalted: ﴿For them there will be a bed of Hell, and above them coverings﴾ [al-A'raf 41], meaning: something that covers them, that is, envelops them.

﴿That is what Allah frightens His servants with﴾ [al-Zumar 16]. ﴿That﴾ means: the thing referred to, namely the mention of these layers. ﴿Allah frightens His servants with it﴾: the pronoun in ﴿with it﴾ refers to the punishment mentioned, and the particle "bi" (with) denotes causation, i.e., He frightens by means of it. It may also be taken as transitive, i.e., He frightens with it Himself.

﴿His servants﴾: he said: (i.e., the believers, so that they may fear Him, as indicated by ﴿O My servants, so fear Me﴾ [al-Zumar 16]). The author, may Allah have mercy on him, took the view that the word "servants" here refers to a specific group, namely the believers, although the apparent meaning of the verse is general, and that "servants" here refers to all who worship Allah in the general sense, which is the universal servitude (al-'ubudiyyah al-kawniyyah). This is because worship is of two kinds: worship by which a person serves Allah through the Sharia, and this is specific to whom? To the believers. And worship in which a person is a servant of Allah by the cosmic order and decree, in which Allah does what He wills, and this is general, as the Exalted said: ﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾ [Maryam 93]. So is the intended meaning here the general worship, and that Allah addresses the command to all servants, all people, to fear Him, or is it specific?

The author, may Allah have mercy on him, holds that it is specific, but there is no evidence for that. When there is no evidence, it is better to keep the text on its general meaning. Just as the believer is frightened by this threat, so too is the disbeliever; the disbeliever is also frightened, and indeed frightening the disbeliever is more emphatic than frightening the believer, because the believer has what saves him from eternal abiding in the Fire, whereas the disbeliever has nothing that saves him from eternal abiding in the Fire. So is the intended meaning the general or the specific?

* Student: The general.
* Shaykh: What is the reason?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: What is the basis for the general being preferred?
* Student: There is no evidence from the author, and it is better to keep the text on its apparent meaning.
* Shaykh: That this is the apparent meaning of the text, correct?

Second: the disbeliever is more deserving of being frightened with the Fire than the believer, because the believer has something that saves him from eternal abiding in the Fire, while the disbeliever has nothing to save him. So how can the frightening be diverted away from the one who most deserves it? Therefore the correct view is that the intended meaning of "servants" is the general: that Allah frightens all people with this punishment.

Then Allah addressed people in general, saying: ﴿O My servants, so fear Me﴾. ﴿O My servants﴾ means all servants, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord and dread a Day when no father will avail his son at all﴾ [Luqman 33], and ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul﴾ [al-Nisa' 1]. The verses calling all people to taqwa are many, and the disbeliever needs taqwa just as the believer does.

So the author's statement "indicates it" (yadullu 'alayhi) is open to question: there is a problem both in the author's ruling and in the argument for that ruling.

﴿O My servants, so fear Me﴾: it is strange that the nun appears with the imperative verb. The known rule is that the imperative attached to the plural waw, the dual alif, or the feminine yā of address drops the nun.

* Student: This is the nun of protection (nūn al-wiqāyah).
* Shaykh: This is the nun of protection? What made you know it is the nun of protection?
* Student: Because its origin is (ittaqūnanī).
* Shaykh: Ittaqūnī?
* Student: (fa-ittaqūnanī).
* Shaykh: Yes, (fa-ittaqūnanī), its origin is?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: This word ﴿fa-ittaqūnī﴾: you said the nun here is not the nun of the nominative but the nun of protection. So what made you know?
* Student: (...) its origin is (ittaqūnanī).
* Shaykh: Ittaqūnanī?! No, this is not an origin at all?
* Student: Because the kasra on it indicates that the yā was dropped; its origin is (fa-ittaqū), the imperative, and (nī), the nun of protection with the yā of the speaker; then the yā was dropped for lightness, and the kasra remained to indicate its dropping.
* Shaykh: Correct. The evidence is clear, brothers: the nun is kasra, because if it were the nun of the nominative it would be with a fatha, since the nun of the nominative is fathah.

An example of this also is His saying in Surat al-Dhariyat: ﴿So let them not seek to hasten Me﴾, ﴿Indeed, for those who did wrong is a portion like the portion of their companions, so let them not seek to hasten Me﴾ [al-Dhariyat 59]. ﴿So let them not seek to hasten Me﴾ is the wording of the verse; when you pause, how do you say it? ﴿So let them not seek to hasten Me (59). So woe﴾ [al-Dhariyat 59–60]. So the nun here is the nun of protection, not the nun of the nominative.

﴿O My servants, so fear Me﴾, and the meaning of taqwa has been mentioned repeatedly before, so there is no need to repeat it.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who avoid the Taghut, not worshipping it, and turn back to Allah﴾ [al-Zumar 17].

﴿Those who avoided﴾: that is, they kept away from the Taghut, because it is derived from "janb" (side), which is a thing separate from another thing. You say: "to the side of so-and-so," meaning he is separate, not joined. ﴿Those who avoided the Taghut﴾ means they distanced themselves from it.

﴿The Taghut﴾ is a noun from "tughyan" (transgression), and the taa' in it is for intensification. So what is the Taghut that is derived from tughyan?

Ibn al-Qayyim, may Allah have mercy on him, said: the Taghut is everything by which a servant exceeds his limit, whether a deity worshipped, a leader followed, or an authority obeyed. Everything by which a person exceeds his limit, and he said "by which he exceeds his limit" so that it truly qualifies as transgression: a deity worshipped, a leader followed, or an authority obeyed. For example, the idols worshipped by the disbelievers are called taghut; the scholars who are followed are taghut; the rulers who are obeyed are likewise taghut. But it is not on its apparent sense: Ibn al-Qayyim's words are not to be taken absolutely. What is meant is the worshipped being that has no will, such as idols of inanimate things, or a worshipped being that is pleased with being worshipped. As for a worshipped being who is worshipped while not being pleased with worship, he is not called taghut. For this reason we cannot call 'Isa ibn Maryam taghut. Likewise the leader: scholars who do not want people to worship them are not taghut; the obeyed one: rulers who do not want people to worship them are not called taghut.

So Ibn al-Qayyim's statement is not absolute.

One may say that Ibn al-Qayyim's words "by which a servant exceeds his limit, whether a worshipped, a followed or an obeyed" refer to the action: that is, the taghut is the servant's action regarding those he worships, or those he obeys or follows; that is, disobedience to Allah in obeying these. Then the description of transgression returns to the act, not the object, and thus we are spared the difficulty we mentioned: that the worshipped, followed and obeyed must be qualified as pleased.

In any case, ﴿al-Taghut﴾ is derived from tughyan, which is exceeding the limit, and its form is that of intensification.

The author said: (the idols), explaining taghut as the worshipped things, which are idols, and therefore he said: ﴿that they worship it﴾.

﴿That they worship it﴾: "an" here is the verbal particle (masdariyyah), and the resulting infinitive phrase is in the accusative as a substitute (badal) for "al-taghut." Of what kind of substitute?

* Student: Substitution of whole for whole.
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: Substitution of part for whole.
* Shaykh: Nor part; because worship is not a part of the idols.
* Student: Substitution of inclusion (badal al-ishtimal).
* Shaykh: Substitution of inclusion. Good, then we say: ﴿that they worship it﴾ is in the accusative position as a substitute for ﴿al-taghut﴾.

As for His saying ﴿that they worship it﴾: they worship the idols by calling upon them, but they claim that they only worship them in order to bring them closer to Allah.

Then He said: ﴿and turn back to Allah﴾, and the rest in the next lesson, God willing.

* Shaykh: Yes, indeed. What about it?
* Student: What is this awe?
* Shaykh: It is not the fear of worship; this is not fear of worship, but fear of reverence and respect.

* Student: The author, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, said: ﴿O My servants﴾, and by the servants is meant the believers, (...).
* Shaykh: Now, is the disbeliever not commanded to have taqwa?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No. Among the components of taqwa is abandoning disbelief, because taqwa is taking a protection from the punishment of Allah, and among it is faith. That is why the verse came: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord and dread a Day when no father will avail his son at all﴾ [Luqman 33], ﴿O mankind﴾ in general. And another verse came: ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord; indeed, the convulsion of the Hour is a tremendous thing﴾ [al-Hajj 1], and ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate﴾ [al-Nisa' 1].

* Student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. ﴿And those who avoid the Taghut, not worshipping it, and turn back to Allah – for them is good tidings. So give good tidings to My servants (17) Who listen to speech and follow the best of it. Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, and those are the people of understanding (18). Then is one upon whom the word of punishment has come [equal to one who is saved]? Would you then save one who is in the Fire? Indeed in that is a reminder for those of understanding﴾ [al-Zumar 17–21].
* Shaykh: Enough. I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Allah the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And those who avoid the Taghut, not worshipping it, and turn back to Allah; for them is good tidings﴾. ﴿Those who avoid the Taghut﴾: what is the meaning of ﴿avoid the Taghut﴾?
* Student: Avoiding the worship of the Taghut, which is what is worshipped besides Allah while being pleased.
* Shaykh: Yes. And what is the meaning of ﴿avoid﴾?

What is the grammatical position of ﴿that they worship it﴾? ﴿Avoid the Taghut, that they worship it﴾.

The saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And those who avoided the Taghut, not worshipping it, and turned back to Allah﴾ [al-Zumar 17]. He says: (﴿Anabu﴾ means they turned toward ﴿Allah﴾). Repentance (inabah) may mean turning toward, as the author said, and may mean returning: they returned to Allah. Returning to Allah entails turning toward Him, because a person flees from Allah through disobedience; when he repents and turns back and returns to Allah, he is turning toward Him.

﴿For them is good tidings﴾ [al-Zumar 17]: this sentence is a declarative one, in which the predicate ﴿for them﴾ is placed first to convey restriction (hasr), because what should be delayed, when placed first, conveys restriction.

As for His saying ﴿for them is good tidings﴾: this sentence is the predicate of ﴿those who﴾: those who avoided the Taghut, for them is good tidings. Clear? So this sentence is in the nominative position as a predicate. What then is the good tidings?

Good tidings is that by which glad news is conveyed; and glad news is essentially information that delights, and it is called bushra because its effect appears on the skin (al-bashrah), for when a person is told what pleases him, his face brightens and changes, so it is called bushra.

The author's statement "Paradise" is undoubtedly among the good tidings, but it is more general than what the author said, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿For them is good tidings in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾ [Yunus 64]. So among the good tidings is a righteous dream that a person sees for himself, or that a believer sees for him. This is among the good tidings, as the Prophet ﷺ said: "That is the early good tidings of the believer" [narrated by Muslim (2642/166) from Abu Dharr al-Ghifari]. A righteous dream seen by him or seen for him, such as seeing one who gives him good news of Paradise, or seeing that he is in bliss, and the like, these are among the good tidings.

Also among the good tidings is that one is enabled to do righteous deeds: when you see that Allah the Exalted has enabled you to do righteous deeds built on sincerity and following the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, this is among the good tidings.

Also among the good tidings is that Allah the Mighty and Exalted enables you to keep company with the righteous. "A man is upon the religion of his close friend," as in the hadith: "Let each of you look at whom he takes as a close friend" [narrated by Abu Dawud (4833) and al-Tirmidhi (2378) from Abu Hurayrah]. So when you find that Allah has enabled you to keep company with the righteous, this is a sign of happiness.

Among the glad tidings is also that a person loves whom Allah loves. The Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about a man who loves a people but has not yet joined them, and he (ﷺ) said: «A person is with the one he loves.» Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "After Islam, we were never happier at anything than at this hadith." Then he said: "I love the Prophet (ﷺ), and I love Abu Bakr and 'Umar."[[These are three hadiths mentioned in the context of one narration. The first: what al-Bukhari (6170) and Muslim (2640 / 165) recorded from the hadith of Abu Musa, who said: It was said to the Prophet (ﷺ): A man loves a people but has not yet joined them? He said: «A person is with the one he loves.» As for the hadith «Whoever loves a people...», al-Tabarani (2519) recorded it from the hadith of Abu Qarasafa al-Kinani (may Allah be pleased with him) with the wording: «Whoever loves a people, Allah will raise him among their company.» The third is the hadith of Anas, which al-Bukhari (3688) and Muslim (2639) recorded through their two chains from him, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: O Messenger of Allah, when is the Hour? He said: «What have you prepared for the Hour?» He said: The love of Allah and His Messenger. He said: «You will be with the one you love.» Anas said: After Islam, we were never happier than at the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): «You will be with the one you love.» Anas said: So I love Allah and His Messenger, and Abu Bakr and 'Umar, and I hope to be with them even though I have not done their deeds.]], so these are among the glad tidings.

The point is that "glad tidings" is every pleasing report. It includes what the author mentioned: Paradise, which is the goal for every person, and it includes whatever is a sign of that. ﴿For them are glad tidings﴾.

He says: ﴿So give good news to My servants﴾ [Az-Zumar 17]. Allah commanded the Prophet (ﷺ) to give good news to the servants of Allah. Give them good news of what? Give them good news of Paradise and of everything that gladdens them. Even in this world, the believer is always glad; and if he is afflicted with a trial, he is still glad, because if he is afflicted with a trial and is patient, it is better for him.

His words: ﴿So give good news to My servants﴾. The dal is kasra although it is the object. Why?

* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Because its origin is (ʿibādī), and the yā' was dropped for lightness, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they have besides Him no protector (wāl)﴾ [Ar-Ra'd 11], meaning: wālī. Although the yā' in ﴿wāl﴾ is not the yā' in (ʿibādī), because the yā' in ﴿wāl﴾ is from the root of the word, whereas here it is another word; the yā'.

﴿So give good news to My servants﴾: Who is meant by the servants here? The meaning is the special quality of servanthood; that is, the righteous servants of Allah, not every servant.

Then He explained their attributes, saying: ﴿Those who listen to the word and follow the best of it﴾ [Az-Zumar 18]. This is one of the signs of the servants of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: they do not waste opportunities.

﴿They listen to the word﴾ means: they give ear to it. He did not say "yasmaʿūn" (they hear), because istimaʿ (listening) is following the speaker and attending to him, unlike samaʿ (hearing). Let us give an example: a man passes by a reciter and hears him reciting; and another man passes by a reciter who is reciting, so he sits with him and listens attentively. The first is a hearer (sāmiʿ), and the second is a listener (mustamiʿ). For this reason, based on this distinction, the scholars said: If the reciter recites a verse containing a prostration and prostrates, the hearer does not prostrate but the listener does, because the listener is following along and the hearer is not following. So these people listen to the word and do not waste opportunities.

﴿The word﴾: the alif-lam here is for a known reference, and it is likely to be for a mentioned reference (al-ʿahd al-dhikrī), due to His saying: ﴿and follow the best of it﴾; that is, they listen to the good word, not every word. So the alif-lam here we say is for reference, and it is likely to be for a mentioned reference, due to His saying: ﴿and follow the best of it﴾.

So what is meant by "word" here? The good word. As for idle talk or bad speech, Allah says: ﴿And when they pass by idle talk, they pass by with dignity﴾ [Al-Furqan 72], and ﴿And when they hear idle talk, they turn away from it and say: "For us are our deeds and for you are your deeds"﴾ [Al-Qasas 55]. If they turn away from idle talk because it has no benefit, then what is forbidden is even more so. So these are people with resolve; they are stingy with their time, listening only to the good word.

Now, if they listen to the good word, we know that good has what is better and what is good. So what do they follow? He says: ﴿and follow the best of it﴾. For example, if they hear encouragement to the night prayer, and that its most excellent form is - for example - eleven rakʿahs, and its least is one rakʿah, what do they follow?

* Students: Eleven.
* The Shaykh: Eleven, because it is better.

If they hear about spending on seeking knowledge, and spending on a poor person who is not in dire need, what do they follow?

* Student: Spending on seeking knowledge.
* The Shaykh: Spending on seeking knowledge, because they follow the better. So they do not squander their time, nor do they squander what is most excellent; rather, they listen to every good word and follow the best of it.

Now, if they follow the good and leave the better, they are not blamed for that, but they are not at the peak of perfection. The one at the peak of perfection is the one who follows the best.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿and follow the best of it﴾ (which is what is good for them), but the more beneficial; they follow the most beneficial, then the more beneficial.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has guided﴾ [Az-Zumar 18].

First: ﴿Those﴾ is a demonstrative for the distant, and He pointed to them with the distant demonstrative despite their being mentioned nearby, to indicate the elevation of their rank. This occurs often in the Qur'an: Allah points to a near thing with the form of the distant because of its high rank, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim. That is the Book, there is no doubt in it﴾ [Al-Baqarah 1-2], although He says ﴿That is the Book﴾, and the Book is near. But the demonstrative is for what? For its high rank. Sometimes He points to it with the near demonstrative because of its nearness to the one who seeks it, as in His saying: ﴿And this is a Book We have sent down, blessed﴾ [Al-An'am 92], meaning it is not far from them; it is near to them.

Here He says: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has guided﴾; He pointed to them with the distant demonstrative, to indicate the elevation of their rank.

﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has guided﴾: this is a declarative sentence whose two parts are definite, and the scholars said that a declarative sentence whose two parts are definite conveys restriction (ḥaṣr); ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has guided﴾ means: and no others.

His words: ﴿Allah has guided them﴾ include both guidance of indication (hidāyat al-dalālah) and guidance of success (hidāyat al-tawfīq); that is, He made the truth clear to them, they knew it, and then they were guided by it. People in this position are of three categories: one category went astray from guidance in knowledge and in action; one category was guided to the truth in knowledge and in action; and one category was guided to the truth in knowledge but was not guided to it in action. Do you understand?

Can I say: and a category who were guided to the truth in action but not guided to it in knowledge?

* The students: It is not possible.
* The Shaykh: It is not possible. Why? Because there is no acting upon the truth except with knowledge of the truth. So the division is quadripartite, but the fourth part does not occur; it is impossible.

So ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has guided﴾ is guidance of indication and success. If you wish, say: guidance of knowledge and action. Which of them is the indication?

* The students: Knowledge.
* The Shaykh: Knowledge. And success?
* The students: Action.
* The Shaykh: Action.

﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, and those are the people of understanding﴾ [Az-Zumar 18]. ﴿And those﴾: He repeated the demonstrative to call attention to their elevated rank.

﴿They are the people of understanding﴾: that is, (possessors of intellect), because the more a person follows the truth, the more complete his intellect; and the more his following of the truth is lacking, the more it indicates the weakness of his intellect. So the most intelligent of people are the ones who follow the religion of Allah most, without doubt, because they are the ones who have resolve, seize opportunities, and guard time. For this reason He said: ﴿Those are the people of understanding﴾ (possessors of intellect).

If someone says: Are not the disbelievers possessed of intellect?

The answer: Yes, but they have a perceptive intellect, not a rightly-guiding intellect. For this reason they were accountable and obligated, because they had perceptive intellect; but they were not granted success, because they lacked the intellect of right guidance.

Allah the Exalted said, explaining the punishment of the losers who lost themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection, explaining their punishment: ﴿For them there will be layers of Fire above them, and beneath them layers﴾ [Az-Zumar 16].

* Among the benefits of this verse: the severity of the punishment for the people of the Fire, because the punishment envelops them from above and from beneath their feet. If a person cannot bear the Fire when it comes to him from one direction, even a distant one, how much more so when it comes to him from both directions: above and below!

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is obligatory for a person to fear what Allah has warned him of, until he fulfils servanthood; as He says: ﴿With this Allah makes His servants fear﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: it is fitting for a person to travel to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, with a side of fear, the fear of punishment. This has come up for us many times: does the one traveling to Allah give preference to the side of fear or the side of hope? This was mentioned before.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, is the Lord of everything, and everything is a worshipper of Allah; as He says: ﴿With this Allah makes His servants fear﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the obligation of taqwa; as He, exalted is He, says: ﴿O My servants, fear Me﴾.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who avoided the Taghut from worshipping it and turned back to Allah, for them is good news﴾ to its end [Az-Zumar 17].

* Among its benefits: praise for the one who avoids the Taghut.
* Among its benefits: that they have this great reward; which is His saying: ﴿For them is good news﴾.
* Among its benefits: that tawhid is not complete except by avoiding the Taghut and sincerity to Allah; as He says: ﴿Those who avoided the Taghut from worshipping it and turned back to Allah, for them is good news﴾.
* Among the benefits of this verse: that those who are characterized by this quality — avoiding the Taghut and turning back to Allah — are the people of good news; ﴿For them is good news﴾. Allah did not specify the time of the good news, so it includes good news in this world and in the Hereafter.
* Among its benefits: the deprivation of whoever associates others with Allah from this good news; because He made the good news for whom? For those who avoid the Taghut from worshipping it and turn back to Allah.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the establishment of special servanthood; as He says: ﴿So give good news to My servants﴾. Special servanthood is divided into a more special kind and a less special kind; so all believers are servants of Allah, while the messengers' servanthood is more special.

Now, ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night﴾ [Al-Isra 1]: is this of the special kind or the more special?

* The students: The more special.
* The Shaykh: Of the more special. ﴿And mention Our servant Abraham﴾ [Sad 45]?

* The students: The more special.
* The Shaykh: This is of the more special servanthood.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the servants of Allah are eager to listen to what contains benefit and profit; as He says: ﴿Those who listen to the word﴾ [Az-Zumar 18].

* Among its benefits: that these noble people do not waste any time; even listening to others' speech, and it must be that they act upon it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the servants of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, whom He described with what was mentioned, take the best of speech; as He says — ?

* Student: ﴿Those who listen to the word and follow the best of it﴾ [Az-Zumar 18].

* The Shaykh: How?

* The student: Because of His saying: ﴿the best of it﴾.

* The Shaykh: Because of His saying: ﴿and follow the best of it﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that these people are those whom Allah has guided; as He says: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has guided﴾ [Az-Zumar 18].

Branching from this rule: if you see in yourself eagerness to listen to words of goodness and to follow the best of them, know that this is from Allah's guidance to you, since He said: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has guided﴾. And if you see in yourself aversion to listening to good speech, then suspect yourself, because Allah placed guidance in these people. So if this is not present in you, suspect yourself, correct the error, and turn to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the actions of servants occur by Allah's decree and that they do not independently accomplish them. From where is this taken? ﴿Allah has guided them﴾. For this reason, the People of the Sunnah and the Jama'ah held that the actions of servants are created by Allah and willed by Him, contrary to those who said that the actions of servants are neither willed by Allah nor created by Him; and they are the Qadariyya, the Magians of this Ummah.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the demonstration of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic's favour upon those who were granted success in listening to speech and following its best; meaning the showing of Allah's favour upon them in His saying: ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has guided﴾.

* Among its benefits: that it is obligatory by reason that you praise Allah, glorified and exalted is He, when He guides you to the like of this; because if you know that guidance is from Allah, then reason requires what? That you praise Him and thank Him. And this blessing is greater than the favour of food and drink; because eating and drinking, everyone eats and drinks, even animals; but not everyone is guided. So Allah's favour upon a person with knowledge-guidance and action-guidance is greater than His favour upon him with food and drink.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that those who hold fast to the religion of Allah and follow the best speech are the people of understanding. Among what is common among people today is that when they see a person who is intelligent and deliberate in affairs, they say: "This is intelligent, masha'Allah, intelligent." Even if he is among the most wicked of people. The reality is that we say: the intelligent one is the one whom Allah, exalted is He, has granted success in knowledge and action, even if he is among the dullest of people in terms of cleverness.

* Among the benefits of this verse: that there is no necessary connection between cleverness and intellect. Cleverness is one thing and intellect is another. Even in perceptive intellect there is no necessary connection between cleverness and perceptive intellect; for among people you find someone who is clever, very observant, who grasps a thing quickly and gives an answer quickly, but in conduct he is foolish.

This favour is greater than the favour of food and drink, because everyone eats and drinks, even animals; but not everyone is guided. So Allah's favour upon a person with knowledge-guidance and action-guidance is greater than His favour upon him with food and drink.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that those who hold fast to the religion of Allah and follow the best speech are the people of understanding. Among what is common among people is that when they see a person who is intelligent and deliberate in affairs, they say: "This is intelligent, masha'Allah, intelligent," even if he is among the most wicked of people. The reality is that we say: the intelligent one is the one whom Allah has granted success in knowledge and action, even if he is among the dullest of people in terms of cleverness.

* Among the benefits of this verse: that there is no necessary connection between cleverness and intellect. Cleverness is one thing and intellect is another. Even in perceptive intellect there is no necessary connection between cleverness and perceptive intellect; for among people is one who is clever, very observant, grasps a thing quickly and gives an answer quickly, but in conduct he is foolish, having no intellect; and among people is one who, on the contrary, has some dullness but in conduct is intelligent and deliberate. But the most intelligent of people are the most obedient of people to Allah. There is no doubt that the most intelligent of people are the most obedient of them to Allah, the Exalted; and for this reason He said: ﴿And those are the people of understanding﴾ [Az-Zumar 18].

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on Surah 39, verses 16–20 (part 3 of 5):**

* Among the benefits of the verse is the indication that people are divided into two groups: those who are granted success (muwaffaq) and those who are denied it (mukhfaq). His saying, ﴿Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, and those are the people of understanding﴾, indicates that there is another group, namely those whom Allah has not granted success and has not guided. The matter is so, the reality is so, the verse points to this, and reality bears witness to it.

If someone asks: Why did Allah, glorified and exalted is He, not make people follow one religion, one community? We say: Because this contradicts wisdom. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And if your Lord had willed, He would have made mankind one community; but they will not cease to differ, except those upon whom your Lord has mercy. And for that He created them. And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind, all together."﴾ [Hud 118–119].

Had this division not existed, Hell would not have been filled, nor would anyone have entered it. Had this division not existed, a person would not have known the value of Allah's blessing upon him in faith and righteous deeds. Had this division not existed, the one who believes and does righteous deeds would not have been praised. Why? Because people are like this, and no one can step outside what people are upon. Had this not existed, there would have been no market for jihad, because you cannot wage jihad against someone who is just like you in faith and righteous deeds. Had this not existed, there would have been no market for enjoining good and forbidding evil, and no market for calling to Allah, and other numerous interests that would be lost with the loss of this division.

As for the divine power, Allah is able to make people one community upon the true religion, but divine wisdom refuses that. You have known something of the great wisdom behind the differentiation of people into believers and disbelievers.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Then is one upon whom the word of punishment has come [equal to one who will be saved]? Would you then save one who is in the Fire?﴾ [Az-Zumar 19].

﴿Then is one upon whom the word of punishment has come﴾: what is "the word of punishment"?

The author [Ibn Kathir] said it is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind, all together."﴾ [Hud 119]. This is what he adopted.

It has also been said that "the word of punishment" is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, even if every sign should come to them until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus 96–97]. This view is closer to the truth, because it is more specific than what the author said. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind, all together"﴾ does not indicate a particular person; it indicates that the word of Allah, mighty and majestic, required that Hell be filled. But ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect﴾ refers to specific people, who will not believe even if every sign comes to them. So the correct view is that what is meant by the word of Allah is what Allah mentioned: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect﴾, that they are among the people of the Fire, and that these people cannot believe.

﴿Then is one upon whom the word of punishment has come﴾, i.e., "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind, all together." This is one view. The second view: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe﴾, meaning that what is meant by the "word" of punishment is that Allah, the Exalted, decreed that these people are among the people of the Fire, so they cannot believe.

﴿Afaman﴾ [the word "afaman" (then is one who)] contains three elements: the hamzah (interrogative particle), the fa' (conjunctive), and man (who). The hamzah is for interrogation, the fa' is conjunctive, and "man" the author says is conditional (shartiyyah), while others say it is relative (mawsulah): "then is the one upon whom the word of punishment has come [...]". According to the author's view, it is conditional. The rest of the discussion on it will come, Allah willing.
