The saying of God, Exalted: ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; then to Him you will be returned﴾ [Az-Zumar 44]. This sentence contains restriction, which is fronting of what should be delayed. Here the predicate is fronted: ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens﴾, meaning, not to anyone else.
His saying: ﴿the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ includes dominion over essences, that is, dominion over the very existence of the heavens and the earth, and dominion of disposal over them. He disposes of them as He wills. So to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth in creation, management, and disposal, and everything returns to Him, Glorified and Exalted. These gods possess none of that.
So, ﴿the dominion of the heavens﴾ means dominion over essences and disposal as He wills. Then we detail: He created them first, and He holds them lest they cease; He folds up the heaven like the folding of a scroll for writings, and on the Day of Resurrection He will seize the earths. All of these are among His acts of disposal over these things which are owned, the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And since the dominion of the heavens and the earth is His, no one intercedes except by His permission, and no one deserves worship except Him.
Then He said: ﴿Then to Him you will be returned﴾. When? On the Day of Resurrection. We will be returned to God, Mighty and Majestic, and He will call us to account according to our deeds. God, Exalted, has made clear to us, explained, and established the proof. "And He has explained that a good deed is multiplied tenfold up to seven hundred times and beyond, to many multiples, and that an evil deed is recompensed with its like."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (41), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]] He has explained the things that are considered good deeds so that we may do them, and the things considered evil so that we may avoid them. Then our return to Him, Mighty and Majestic, will be a return with insight, and we will have no argument against opposing Him.
Now we return to the benefits of this noble verse. What comes before it, where?
﴿Or have they taken intercessors besides God?﴾ [Az-Zumar 43].
* In this verse: a denunciation of those who worship idols, a denunciation of whoever worships idols and takes them as intercessors. From where do we derive the denunciation? From the hamza contained in (am), because (am) means (bal) and the hamza.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the gross error of these polytheists, in that they worshipped idols and thought them to be intercessors, though they only increase them in distance from God.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: establishing the rational proof in disputation with an opponent, which is His saying: ﴿Say: Even though they possess nothing and do not understand?﴾ [Az-Zumar 43]. If they possess nothing, how do you take them as intercessors and worship them besides God?
Know that we need rational proofs urgently when faith weakens. Whenever faith weakens, we need rational proofs, because the believer is sufficed by transmitted evidence, by the revealed text. God, Exalted, says: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice in their affair﴾ [Al-Ahzab 36]. And 'A'ishah, may God be pleased with her, argued against the woman who asked her: "Why does a menstruating woman make up the fasts but not the prayers?" She said: "This used to happen to us, and we were commanded to make up the fasts, and we were not commanded to make up the prayers."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (321), and Muslim (335 / 69), and the wording is his, from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]] So when faith is strong, deriving proof from the Sunnah and the Qur'an suffices. When faith is weak, convincing rational proof is necessary. For this reason we find God, Glorified, in the Mighty Book often arguing with sensible, observable rational matters to establish and confirm the meanings He wishes to affirm, such as the revival of the dead and similar things. We are now in an age where faith is weak and disputation is abundant, and we need to understand rational proofs so that we can convince our opponents. You know now that many people, if brought every verse, would not follow it, but if brought a rational proof, they are convinced. This is one point.
You also know that the enemies of Islam and the Muslims look for opportunities to refute the arguments of the Muslims. You find them in every gathering speaking about things with which they cast doubt upon the Muslim youth. If a person does not have a rational argument to refute their argument, he may be silenced, and that fierce adversary will prevail over him, as God, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿And among the people is one whose speech in the life of this world pleases you, and he calls God to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the most stubborn of opponents﴾ [Al-Baqarah 204]. So I urge you to take from rational proofs whatever will save you from the opposition of those fierce disputants, so that you may contend with them, argue against them, and overcome them with proof. Abraham, peace be upon him, argued with his people by reason. How? When the night covered him, he saw a star and said: "This is my lord." When it set, he said: ﴿I do not love the setting ones﴾ [Al-An'am 76], I do not love a deity that disappears from me and does not know my state. Then when he saw the moon rising, he said: "This is my lord." When it set, he established the proof against the error of those who worshipped the stars, saying: ﴿If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be among the people who are astray. Then when he saw the sun rising, he said, "This is my lord; this is greater." But when it set, he said, "O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate.﴾ [Al-An'am 77, 78].
Likewise, he argued against the one who disputed with him: ﴿Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord, because God had given him dominion? When Abraham said﴾, to the end of the verse: ﴿Indeed, God brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west﴾ [Al-Baqarah 258], and so on. So today we need to exercise our minds in rational proofs, so that we may argue with them against those whose faith is weak through transmitted evidence, or against those whose faith in transmitted evidence has been lost.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: idols possess nothing for their worshippers, neither bringing benefit nor repelling harm.
If someone says: Some people call upon an idol and it answers them, as we often hear. How is the answer to this verse?
The answer to this verse: the words of God are true and right, exactly conforming to reality. God has explained in another verse that there is no one more misguided in mind or more foolish in way: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than God those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and who are unaware of their supplication? And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ [Al-Ahqaf 5, 6]. But whatever such things occur, such as a man calling upon a saint or the owner of a grave, or similar, and his harm is removed, that is only a trial from God, Mighty and Majestic, a trial that occurs at the thing, not through the thing.
For example: if a man calls upon a grave and his harm is lifted, do we say that the owner of the grave is the one who lifted it? Not at all. We are certain, like the sun, that the owner of the grave did not benefit him. Rather, God tested the worshipper of this grave by making the thing happen at his hand, not by it. There is a difference between a thing that happens by means of something and a thing that happens at something. God, Mighty and Majestic, may test a person with such a thing. He may make the means of disobedience and polytheism easy for him as a trial and test.
Have you considered the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ, when God forbade them hunting during the state of ihram? With what did God test them? God tested them with game that their hands and spears could reach. The bird is reached by the spear, and the ordinary running animal is reached by hands: that is, gazelles, hares, and similar, they catch with their hands, and birds with their spears, not with arrows; they did not need arrows. God tested them with this, so that God might know who fears Him in the unseen. God may test the servant by making the means of disobedience easy for him, until God, Glorified and Exalted, knows whether he will be patient or will proceed. Because some people find it easy to refrain from disobedience when it is difficult for them, as it requires effort and requires wealth. But when it becomes easy, and then he refrains, it is known that the man is sincere in his faith. Is that not so?
So we have understood the answer to His saying: ﴿Even though they possess nothing and do not understand?﴾ [Az-Zumar 43]: that what happens which is thought to be due to these gods has in fact occurred at them, not by them.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 39, verses 43–44 (part 3 of 3):

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: these deities lack intellect. This applies to those who worship what has no intellect, such as idols and trees, based on His words: ﴿and they do not understand﴾. Accordingly, if we restrict the matter to those who worship idols, trees, and the like, it is not objected that some people worshipped the Messiah, peace be upon him, who was among the most perfect of people in intellect, since he is one of the Messengers of firm resolve (Uli al-'Azm). We would say: God means by this the idols, which are what? Inanimate objects that do not understand.
Then God Most High said: ﴿Say: "To God belongs all intercession. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth"﴾ [az-Zumar 44], to the end.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of intercession, ﴿To God belongs all intercession﴾. The proof of its affirmation is that, were it not existent, it would not be correct to say ﴿To God belongs all intercession﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the refutation of the Mu'tazilah and the Khawarij, since the Mu'tazilah and the Khawarij deny intercession?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes. The Mu'tazilah and the Khawarij reject intercession for the people of major sins, whether they enter the Fire or not. This is because, according to the Mu'tazilah and the Khawarij, the people of major sins are eternal in the Fire. However, according to the Khawarij they are disbelievers, and according to the Mu'tazilah they are neither believers nor disbelievers, being in an intermediate position between two positions.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of multiple intercessions, based on His words: ﴿all﴾, since ﴿all﴾ requires that there be something gathered together.
* Among its benefits: no one intercedes except by God's permission. The reason is that if intercession belongs exclusively to God, then it exists only from Him and returns only to Him.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of God's dominion over the heavens and the earth, and His sole sovereignty, based on His words: ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾.
* Among its benefits: the affirmation of the Resurrection and the return to God, based on His words: ﴿Then to Him you will be returned﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: warning and glad tidings, based on His words: ﴿Then to Him you will be returned﴾. The believer is undoubtedly delighted to meet God and loves to meet God, while the disbeliever is the opposite. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever loves to meet God, God loves to meet him, and whoever dislikes to meet God, God dislikes to meet him"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6507) and Muslim (2683/14), from the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit.]]. So when we know that we will return to God, we love to meet God, and the disbeliever dislikes meeting God.
﴿Then to Him you will be returned﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that God, glorified and exalted, mentions a thing by warning of its necessary consequence, since mere return contains nothing worth mentioning. Rather, what is meant is the return by which reckoning and recompense take place.
God Most High said: ﴿Or have they taken intercessors besides God?﴾ [az-Zumar 43]. He said: (﴿Or﴾ means "rather," and ﴿they have taken besides God﴾). We do not, however, read ("ittakhadhu") with the cutting hamzah (hamzat al-qat'), because in the Qur'an the hamzah is not a cutting hamzah. But if the construction were outside the Qur'an, we would say: "Bal ittakhadhu min dunihi" (rather, they have taken besides Him). If we say "ittakhadhu," someone will ask: where did the connecting hamzah (hamzat al-wasl) in ﴿ittakhadhu﴾ go? We say: because the cutting hamzah entered upon the verb, we dispensed with the connecting hamzah, since the connecting hamzah is only brought in to facilitate beginning with a consonant cluster. When we do not begin with it, and begin with a cutting hamzah, we dispense with it and delete it. Recite: ﴿Has He chosen daughters over sons?﴾ [as-Saffat 153], "asta fa." Its original form is "istafa," and the hamzah was added to it. When the hamzah was added to it, we no longer needed the connecting hamzah, since the connecting hamzah is brought in only out of necessity. For this reason it is called the connecting hamzah: it is brought in out of necessity, to avoid beginning with a consonant. When that necessity disappears, it is dropped.
He said: (﴿Or have they taken besides God intercessors﴾ [az-Zumar 43], meaning the idols are gods that ﴿intercede﴾ with God ﴿according to their claim﴾). That is, they made these idols gods that would intercede for them with God.
The author's words "according to their claim" mean not in reality, because these idols do not intercede for them. Rather, on the Day of Resurrection, whoever took a god alongside God will disavow the worship of those who worshipped him. Is that correct? From where do we derive this? ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than God, one who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they are unaware of their supplication? And when mankind are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ [al-Ahqaf 5–6]. Likewise what you mentioned: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection, they will deny your association﴾ [Fatir 14]. Moreover, even those who took others than the Messengers as leaders, followers of misguidance, will disown them: ﴿When those who were followed disown those who followed﴾ [al-Baqarah 166]. Observe, glory be to God, that the Qur'an declares disbelief for those who were made partners in messengership, and declares disbelief for those who were made partners in worship. This is because each of them did not fulfil the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. As for those who took partners in worship, you have heard: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection, they will deny your association﴾, and ﴿When mankind are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾. As for those who took partners in messengership: ﴿When those who were followed disown those who followed﴾. This is because whoever follows someone other than the Messengers, opposing the words of the Messengers with his own words, has associated him with the Messengers in messengership.
Who among mankind must be followed? The Messengers. So if a person makes his leader equal in status to the Messenger, peace be upon him, taking from him in action, abandonment, and affirmation, he has made him a messenger. For this reason some scholars say: tawhid is of two kinds, tawhid of worship and tawhid of messengership. Tawhid of worship concerns the right of God, and tawhid of messengership concerns the right of the Messenger ﷺ. God Most High joins these two in the Qur'an: ﴿Do they not ponder the Word, or has there come to them what did not come to their forefathers of old? Or do they not recognize their Messenger, so that they deny him?﴾ [al-Mu'minun 68–69]. The conclusion is that those who took intercessors have strayed into manifest error, because these intercessors will not benefit them.
He said: (﴿Say﴾ to them: will they intercede even though ﴿they possess nothing and do not understand﴾). Will they intercede even though they are...? The author, may God have mercy on him, followed in this commentary one of the two well-known opinions regarding the case where the interrogative hamzah enters upon a conjunctive particle. What are the two?
* Student: (...) before the hamzah, or before the interrogative particle.
The second: that the conjunction is upon what follows the interrogative hamzah or the interrogative particle.
* The Shaykh: There are two views. The first view: that the conjunction is upon what preceded, and in this case the hamzah is understood to come after the conjunctive particle.
The second view: that the conjunction is upon an implied sentence whose content is determined by the context. Did the author follow the first or the second?
* Student: The first.
* Another student: The second.
* The Shaykh: Look, everyone, "will they intercede even though"?
* Students: The second.
* The Shaykh: Then it is the second, because he supposed the conjoined element between the hamzah and the conjunctive particle. "Will they intercede even though they possess nothing and do not understand" (﴿they possess nothing﴾ of intercession and other things, ﴿and do not understand﴾ that you worship them, nor anything else). The answer is no: these do not intercede, because they do not understand, and they do not possess. They do not understand the worship of one who worships them, and they do not possess anything for him, neither intercession nor anything else.
Then He said: (﴿Say: To God belongs all intercession﴾, meaning He alone is its possessor). From where did he derive "He alone is its possessor"? From the restriction, which is the fronting of the predicate. (He alone is its possessor, so no one intercedes except by His permission), and this is one of the two conditions of intercession. The second is God's approval of the intercessor and His approval of the one for whom intercession is made.
﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; then to Him you will be returned﴾. He mentioned the comprehensiveness of His dominion and His sole sovereignty after mentioning intercession, because intercession in reality derives from sovereignty, and so it falls within God's general dominion over the heavens and the earth. ﴿Then to Him you will be returned﴾. He did not explain it, because it is clear.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 39, verses 43–44 (part 1 of 3):

Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah?﴾ [az-Zumar 43]. Here "am" (أم) is *munqati'a* (disjunctive, lit. "cut off"). For this reason it is to be interpreted as "bal" (بل, "rather") together with the interrogative hamza (الهمزة), meaning that it carries the sense of "bal" and the hamza. Our saying "munqati'a" implies that there is a counterpart to this meaning, and that is the case. The counterpart is *muttasila* (connective), and at this point we need to distinguish between the disjunctive and the connective. The distinction between them is in two respects. In the Arabic language, "bal" comes in two types, connective and disjunctive. The difference between them is that disjunctive "am" has no *mu'adil* (correspondent), meaning that no correspondent is mentioned with it, unlike connective "am", which requires a correspondent. So the words of the Exalted: ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them﴾ [al-Baqarah 6]. What is this? It is connective. Why? Because the correspondent is mentioned: ﴿whether you warn them or do not warn them﴾. Good. And like His words: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"? Rather, they do not believe﴾ [at-Tur 33]. This is disjunctive, because it means "bal" (rather): "Rather, do they say he invented it?" Since no correspondent is mentioned in it, it is disjunctive.

The second difference between them is that connective "am" means "aw" (أو, "or"), while disjunctive "am" means "bal" together with the hamza. In ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them﴾ [al-Baqarah 6], if "aw" were placed after it, that would be the meaning: "whether you warn them or do not warn them". Disjunctive "am" means "bal" with the hamza, not "aw". Let us apply this difference to what we have here: ﴿Or have they taken intercessors besides Allah?﴾ [az-Zumar 43]. What is it then? It is disjunctive. Firstly, because no correspondent is mentioned. Secondly, because it is to be interpreted as "bal" with the hamza.

﴿Besides Allah﴾ means "other than Him". "Dun" (دون) here means "siwa" (سوى, "other than"), not "dun" in the sense of rank; rather, "dun" means "siwa". ﴿Besides Allah﴾ means "other than Allah". The verb "ittakhadha" (اتخذ, "to take") here takes two objects. The first is "shufa'a" (intercessors), and the second is "min dunillah" (besides Allah). That is, they have taken, besides Allah, [things as] intercessors. It is also permissible to say that the first object is omitted, its implied form being "ālihah" (gods), and the second is "shufa'a" (intercessors). That is, they have taken objects of worship which they worship, claiming that they are intercessors for them with Allah. Allah the Exalted said about them: ﴿We only worship them so that they may bring us near to Allah in position﴾ [az-Zumar 3]. So they openly declared that they worship these deities, but they want them to bring them closer to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Glory be to Allah! How can one take as a means to draw near to Allah those whom one disobeys Allah about? This is from their foolishness.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: (﴿intercessors﴾ with Allah, according to their claim). The plural "shufa'a" is of "shafi'" (intercessor). The *shafi'* is one who mediates on behalf of another to bring about a benefit or to repel a harm. Intercession for the people of the Gathering (on the Day of Judgment), when distress and grief befall them, is that Allah judges between them, which is repelling a harm. Intercession for the people of Paradise is that they enter it, which is bringing about a benefit. This is intercession. Intercession means that you mediate for someone else, for what? For bringing about a benefit or repelling a harm. Intercession is, without doubt, good: ﴿Whoever intercedes with a good intercession will have a share of it﴾ [an-Nisa' 85], except in some circumstances, such as intercession concerning a *hadd* (prescribed punishment) once it has reached the ruler. Whoever intercedes to prevent one of the prescribed punishments of Allah has indeed opposed Allah in His command, and when the *hudud* (prescribed punishments) reach the ruler, then Allah curses both the intercessor and the one for whom intercession is made. So these people who worship idols claim that they are intercessors. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: "Even though they possess nothing and do not understand?"﴾ [az-Zumar 43]. That is: do you take them as intercessors while they possess nothing, neither intercession nor anything other than intercession? Here He said: ﴿they possess nothing﴾, and "shay'an" (شيئًا, "anything") is indefinite in a negative context, so it is general. The context would have required that He say: "even though they do not possess intercession", but He used the general form to show that these idols bring no benefit at all: they do not intercede, nor do they repel. Intercession has been denied to them because they are included in the generality; that is, they possess neither intercession nor anything else. Yes. ﴿Even though they possess nothing and do not understand?﴾ [az-Zumar 43]. Here "awalaw" (أولو) contains a conjunction after the hamza, and we have mentioned many times what the grammarians say about this construction. Who will recall what we have said? When a conjunction comes after the interrogative hamza, what do the grammarians say in its *i'rab* (grammatical analysis)? We have gone over this many times.

*Student:* We said that the waw is a conjunction joining it to the preceding clause.

*Shaykh:* That the conjunction is joining to what precedes it.

*Student:* And the implied form is: "wa-alaw" (and "alaw").

*Shaykh:* "Wa-alaw"? Or "aw".

*Student:* (...).

*Shaykh:* This is what he said.

*Student:* (...) with an implied verb.

*Shaykh:* Or the hamza stays in its place, and the conjunction joins something implied that suits the context. We have mentioned that the second view is that of the Basrans and the first is that of the Kufans, and we have mentioned that the view that the conjunction joins to what precedes it is preferable, because it spares you the need for an implied element, and because sometimes a person cannot work out the appropriate thing to supply. If he says: the hamza is interrogative and the waw is a conjunction, and what follows it is joined to what precedes, he is relieved. Here He said: ﴿Even though they possess nothing﴾ [az-Zumar 43]. According to the view that the conjunction joins to an implied element, one says: "Do they take them as intercessors, even though they possess nothing?"

According to the second view, one says: the waw is a conjunction, and what it joins is what precedes in the sentence.

﴿Even though they possess nothing and do not understand﴾ [az-Zumar 43]. What do they not understand? That is, they do not understand that you worship them. Idols are stones that know nothing. Nor do they understand anything of intercession by which they could benefit. So they are ignorant of their own situation and ignorant of what they deserve.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: "To Allah belongs all intercession."﴾ [az-Zumar 44]. Who is addressed by "say"? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ, or anyone who is capable of being addressed and whose address is valid. The latter is more general than the former, because it includes the Prophet ﷺ and others.

Well then, He says: ﴿Say﴾, O addressee who is fit to be addressed, ﴿To Allah belongs all intercession﴾. "To Allah belongs intercession" is a declarative sentence that conveys restriction (*hasr*). What is its method? Brother?

*Student:* The operator has been placed first.

*Shaykh:* No, there is no operator.

*Student:* (...) a prepositional phrase. That the predicate has been placed first...

*Shaykh:* That the predicate has been placed first, while its proper place is later. Every fronting of what should be delayed conveys restriction. Well then, "to Allah belongs intercession", not to anyone else. He is the One who possesses it. The "li-" (لِ, "to") in His words ﴿li-llah﴾ denotes ownership. That is, He is the One who possesses intercession, meaning He possesses the authority to permit it. Allah, glory be to Him, has explained that intercession has three conditions:

The first condition: His permission, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ [al-Baqarah 255].

The second condition: His pleasure with the intercessor, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿On the Day when the Spirit and the angels will stand in rows, they will not speak except one whom the Most Merciful has permitted and who speaks what is correct﴾ [an-Naba' 38].

The third: His pleasure with the one for whom intercession is made, as in His words: ﴿And how many an angel there is in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all except after Allah gives permission to whom He wills and approves﴾ [an-Najm 26]. This also serves as evidence that Allah's pleasure with the intercessor is a condition. And He said: ﴿And they do not intercede except for those whom He approves﴾ [al-Anbiya' 28]. So the conditions for Allah's acceptance of intercession are three. Count them for us, brother.

*Student:* Permission for the intercessor, pleasure with the one interceded for.

*Shaykh:* Yes.

*Student:* Permission for the one interceded for.

*Shaykh:* No.

*Student:* Permission for the intercession, and pleasure with both of them, the intercessor and the one interceded for...

*Shaykh:* With the intercessor and the one interceded for. These are three. And you know their evidence. ﴿Say: "To Allah belongs all intercession."﴾ [az-Zumar 44]. Now, if I say: "O Messenger of Allah, intercede for me with Allah", is that permissible? It is not permissible, because he does not possess that. He does not intercede for you or for anyone else except by Allah's permission. An example of this is what some of the mujahideen brothers in Afghanistan do: one of them says to another, "Intercede for me with Allah", because the mujahid has intercession if he is killed as a martyr. You find some of his relatives or companions saying, "Intercede for me with Allah." This is not permissible, because he has asked of him what he does not possess. If he says, "Intercede for me", say: "Intercession belongs to whom?" To Allah. Say: "O Allah, grant him intercession for me." There is no harm in that. Ask for intercession from the One who possesses intercession. As for one who does not possess it, do not ask him. That is a question in the wrong place. So intercession belongs to Allah, and if it belongs to Allah, then it is only to be asked of Allah.

And His words: ﴿Say: "To Allah belongs all intercession."﴾ [az-Zumar 44]. "Jami'an" (جميعًا, "all") is a circumstantial qualifier (*hal*) of "shafa'a" (intercession). What is the meaning of plurality here? Is intercession plural? The answer: yes, intercession is plural. There is intercession in this world and intercession in the Hereafter, intercession for bringing about a benefit and intercession for repelling a harm. So there is no intercession except that which belongs to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. All intercessions belong to Allah. Intercession in this world is, for example, when a person prays for someone. When a person prays for someone, that is intercession. The Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no Muslim man who dies and forty men stand over his funeral prayer, who do not associate anything with Allah, except that Allah accepts their intercession for him"[[Narrated by Muslim (948/59) from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas.]]. So a person's supplication for his brother is intercession for him with Allah. This is intercession in this world.

Intercession in the Hereafter is well known. The intercession in the Hereafter, or the Great Intercession (ash-shafa'a al-'uzma), belongs to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and it belongs to no one else. And what is the Great Intercession? It is that the people on that Gathering, as you know from the texts, are barefoot, naked and uncircumcised, their eyes fixed, their hearts like air. The sun draws close to them to the distance of a mile. The sweat bridles some of them. No one turns to anyone else, and no one seeks help from anyone else. ("To whom belongs the dominion today?" "To Allah, the One, the Subduer.") They are afflicted with grief and distress beyond what they can bear. Some of them say to others: "Look for someone who will intercede for us with Allah, so that we may find rest from this station." They go to Adam, then to Noah, then to Abraham, then to Moses, then to Jesus, and they obtain nothing. Then they come to Muhammad ﷺ, and he asks permission. They ask him for intercession, and he does not intercede until he has first asked Allah for permission, because the sovereignty is great and the authority is complete. He asks Allah to grant him permission to intercede, and He grants it. Then he prostrates beneath the Throne, a long prostration, and Allah opens to him praises that he had not known before. Then he intercedes with Allah that He judge among creation and give them rest from this station, and Allah accepts his intercession. This intercession is called the Great Intercession, because of its generality and the intensity of the need for it. It belongs only to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and it falls under His words: ﴿It may be that your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station﴾ [al-Isra' 79], because in this station the first and the last will praise him, both those of his nation and those who are not of his nation.

In it there is also intercession for those who have entered the Fire, that they may be brought out of it, and for those who deserve it, that they may not enter it. This intercession is of two kinds: intercession for those who have entered it, that they be brought out, and intercession for those who deserve it, that they not enter it. This is general, for the Messengers, the truthful ones, the martyrs, the righteous, the angels, and mankind in general.

However, two groups of the misguided sects within this Ummah deny it: who are they? The Mu'tazilites and the Khawarij. Why? Because they say that the perpetrator of a major sin is eternally in the Fire, sentenced to that by decree and destiny, and if that is so, this decree will not be reversed, and they cannot come out of the Fire. Do you understand? Well then. The Great Intercession is for the one who deserves the Fire so that he does not enter it, and for the one who has entered it so that he is brought out.

The fourth intercession: concerning entry into Paradise. When people cross the Sirat (the bridge over Hell) (may Allah make me and you among those who cross it safely), when they cross the Sirat they do not enter Paradise immediately, but are held back at a *qantarah* (bridge-span), which is the end of the bridge that lies over the Fire, or something else; Allah knows best. Then retribution is exacted from some of them against others. This is *qisas al-tanqiya* (retribution for purification), whereas the retribution earlier on the plain of Resurrection is *qisas al-takhliya* (retribution for clearance). That is: today, on the plain of Resurrection, justice is exacted for the wronged from the wrongdoer. But this is retribution for purification. What does purification mean? It means that the rancour and hatred in their hearts are removed. Because the settlement of a person's right does not necessarily remove the enmity and hatred in his heart. Is that right? Does settling a person's right remove the enmity and hatred in his heart? Yes, perhaps and perhaps not. I might say: "He wronged me, and now I have taken my right from him, but the effect of that aggression remains in my heart." Is that not so? This exists, brothers, no one denies it. But the one who is successful strives to remove it. Yet it must remain: the mark of a wound must remain even when it has healed. If a wound heals, does the thing return to how it was? It leaves marks. Aggression must leave its effect, even if a person takes retribution for himself against another person's heart. So when they exact retribution from one another on the plain of Resurrection and cross the Sirat, they need purification: their hearts are cleansed and purified, so that they enter Paradise with no rancour in their hearts, in the most perfect way.

Well then, after retribution has been exacted between them, they also do not enter Paradise immediately. They find the gates of Paradise closed, so they ask for someone to intercede for them, and the Prophet ﷺ intercedes specifically. This is specific to the Messenger, but it is not the Great Intercession, nor is it the greatest, because it is for the people of Paradise specifically. He intercedes that the gates of Paradise be opened, and he is given permission, and the gates of Paradise are opened. The first of creation to enter it is he, peace and blessings be upon him. The first of the nations to enter it is his nation, immediately after the Prophets. The Prophets first, then the nations. The leader of the Prophets is Muhammad ﷺ, and the leader of the nations is this Ummah, because this Ummah, praise be to Allah, comes late in time in this world, but it is foremost in all the stations of the Hereafter. The Prophet ﷺ said: "We are the last, but the foremost on the Day of Resurrection"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (876) and Muslim (855/19) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah.]]. So in all the stations, praise be to Allah, we are foremost in crossing the Sirat, in judgment between people, on the plain of Resurrection, in entering Paradise, in everything. We are foremost on the Day of Resurrection in everything. So they enter Paradise.

Reflect on this in the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Allah said about the people of the Fire: ﴿until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened﴾ [az-Zumar 71], while they are unwilling to enter it. From the moment they arrive at it, its gates are opened, and they are driven into it with force. As for Paradise, He said: ﴿until, when they reach it and its gates have been opened, and its keepers say to them﴾ [az-Zumar 73]. So His words ﴿and its gates have been opened﴾ indicate that there is something between their arrival and the opening. Those among the scholars who say that the waw here is superfluous, and that the meaning is "until, when they reach it, its gates were opened", are mistaken. I say: glory be to Allah! Do you know the words of Allah better than Allah does? Allah, Mighty and Majestic, distinguishes in the Fire, saying: ﴿when they reach it, it is opened﴾ [az-Zumar 71], and regarding Paradise He says: ﴿until, when they reach it, and its gates have been opened﴾, and you say that this waw is superfluous! This is dangerous. Even more dangerous is the one who said that the waw is the "waw of eight" (waw ath-thamaniya), claiming that there is a waw in the language called the waw of eight. This claim is false. He said: No, I have evidence: ﴿It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for you wives better than you, submissive, faithful, devout, repentant, worshipping, travelling, previously married and virgins﴾ [at-Tahrim 5]. The waw is the waw of eight, because these are eight. We say: who said this? Say instead: "Zayd and Bakr came", the waw is for two? "And Khalid", the waw for three? Keep going. Who told you this? The correct view is that the waw here is conjunctive, and that what it conjoins to is implied. I have explained what it conjoins to, and I explained it from the Sunnah. On this basis, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has two specific intercessions: the Great Intercession, and the intercession for entry into Paradise.

There is also a special intercession for him that no one else had: his intercession for his uncle Abu Talib. His uncle Abu Talib died upon disbelief and polytheism, may God protect us, and he is in the Fire. But "God permitted His Prophet to intercede for him, so he is in a shallow part of the Fire, and on his feet are two sandals whose heat makes his brain boil."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (3885) and Muslim (210 / 360), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]] He has the lightest punishment among the people of the Fire. So, how many kinds of intercession are special to the Messenger ﷺ? Three kinds. God, Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Say: To God belongs all intercession﴾ [Az-Zumar 44]. He is the One who grants it to whom He wills and withholds it from whom He wills. And He has explained the conditions. What are they?
* Student: Permission, His approval of the intercessor, and His approval of the one interceded for.
* Shaykh: Permission, His approval of the intercessor, and His approval of the one for whom intercession is made.
* Student: We said, O Shaykh, that applying a name to God, Exalted is He, without a textual basis is not permitted. As for the expression (...).
* Shaykh: It is permitted, except what is not fitting for God.
* Student: But, O Shaykh, applying (...) to God, Exalted is He, is an overstepping against God.
* Shaykh: No. Informing about Him is broader than naming Him. I do not want to describe God with this in an absolute sense.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No, not in an absolute sense. Only what God has described Himself with, in an absolute sense.
* Student: So we do not describe Him (...).
* Shaykh: We do not describe Him in an absolute sense, but we report about Him. For example, the word "existent" (mawjud). "Existent" is not in the Qur'an or the Sunnah. Is it correct to say, "God exists"? Yes, without doubt it is correct, even though He is not described except as "Living, Self-Subsisting, All-Hearing, All-Seeing." And strangely, what people most often seek help with, or some people do, is saying, "God exists." If someone wrongs them, they say, "God exists." This is not the correct approach.
* Student: O Protector (ya Satir).
* Shaykh: Yes indeed, and "O Protector." "God exists." Does this help anyone? "God is a just Judge," this is what helps. Otherwise, for example, "The sultan exists," will he help you? He may help you and he may not. So the word "existent" does not mean help. For this reason we say to some people: be careful with this word. Do not say, "God exists." Say, "God is a just Judge, God is not unaware of what you do, God takes vengeance on the wrongdoer," and similar things.
* * *
* Student: I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan: ﴿And when God alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink; but when those besides Him are mentioned, behold, they rejoice. Say: O God, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ. And if those who did wrong possessed whatever is on earth entirely and the like of it with it, they would surely ransom themselves with it from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. And there will appear to them from God that which they had not expected. And there will appear to them the evils of what they earned, and there will envelop them that which they used to ridicule﴾ [Az-Zumar 45–48].
* Shaykh: In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful. I seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan. God, Exalted is He, says: ﴿Or have they taken intercessors besides God? Say: Even though they possess nothing and do not understand?﴾ [Az-Zumar 43]. What is (am) here?
* Student: (am) here is disjunctive (munqati'a), meaning (bal) ("rather").
* Shaykh: Disjunctive, meaning (bal), and the hamza (interrogative) is there. What is the difference between disjunctive (am) and its counterpart?
* Student: Disjunctive (am) is not preceded by a mention of alternatives, and it is used for a statement of fact. Connective (am) is preceded by a mention of alternatives.
* Shaykh: And it is used with the meaning of...
* Student: "Or" (aw).
* Shaykh: It is used with the meaning of (aw), like the disjunctive.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: And other things.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: What comes before it? ﴿Or do you ask them for payment?﴾ [At-Tur 40].
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: This is disjunctive. Now, connective. Give an example of connective.
* Student: The saying of God, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them﴾ [Al-Baqarah 6].
* Shaykh: ﴿It is the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them﴾ [Al-Baqarah 6]. The saying of God, Exalted: ﴿Say: To God belongs all intercession﴾ [Az-Zumar 44]. This sentence contains restriction (hasr). By what means?
* Student: Its means is that God, Glorified and Exalted...
* Shaykh: It is not needed. This is not a sermon. One word.
* Student: Because the predicate...
* Shaykh: Subhan Allah!
* Student: Fronting of the complement (...).
* Shaykh: There is no complement here.
* Student: "To God is the intercession," "to God" is the predicate.
* Shaykh: Yes, fronting of the predicate. Now why was fronting the predicate useful for restriction?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: No. You have a rule for this. There is a rule for which this is an example.
* Student: We said: fronting what should be delayed conveys restriction.
* Shaykh: Fronting what should be delayed conveys restriction. Good. His saying: ﴿Say: To God belongs all intercession﴾ [Az-Zumar 44], the word "all" (jami'an) indicates that there are kinds of intercession. Brother?
* Student: There are types of intercession: the Great Intercession...
* Shaykh: What is the intercession special to the Messenger ﷺ?
* Student: It is his intercession for his community to enter Paradise.
* Shaykh: His intercession for the people of Paradise that they enter Paradise. That is one. And the second?
* Student: Intercession for the people of the Standing Place (al-mawqif) to settle matters among them, and this is the Great Intercession.
* Shaykh: Well done. It is the Great Intercession for the people of the Standing Place, that judgment be passed among them.
* Student: The intercession for his uncle Abu Talib.
* Shaykh: The intercession for his uncle Abu Talib. Good. This is special to the Messenger ﷺ. What is our evidence that the intercession for his uncle is special to him?
* Student: Because it is reported from the Prophet ﷺ that he interceded for his uncle.
* Shaykh: That is not sufficient.
* Student: The saying of the Messenger ﷺ: "Had it not been for me, he would be in the lowest level of the Fire."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6208) and Muslim (209 / 357), from the hadith of al-Abbas.]]
* Shaykh: Yes, this is evidence that he interceded for him. But what is the evidence that it is special to him?
* Student: The saying of God, Exalted: ﴿And they do not intercede except for those whom He approves﴾ [Al-Anbiya' 28], and God approved his intercession.
* Shaykh: The saying of God, Exalted: ﴿And they do not intercede except for those whom He approves﴾ [Al-Anbiya' 28]. God does not approve of intercession for a disbeliever, so this is excepted. And His saying: ﴿So the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them﴾ [Al-Muddaththir 48], and this is excepted. Therefore, it is special to him.
* * *
God, Exalted, says. We are now at the beginning of the new lesson: ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; then to Him you will be returned﴾ [Az-Zumar 44]. This sentence contains restriction, which is fronting of what should be delayed. Here the predicate is fronted: ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens﴾, meaning, not to anyone else.
His saying: ﴿the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ includes dominion over their essences, meaning dominion over the very existence of the heavens and the earth, and dominion of disposal over them. He disposes of them as He wills. He is the One who brought them into being, and He is the One who holds them lest they cease. He is the One who manages what is in them, and He is the One who will destroy and annihilate them at the establishment of the Hour.
The saying of God, Exalted: ﴿And those who do not intercede except for whom He approves﴾ [Al-Anbiya' 28]: God does not approve of intercession for a disbeliever, so this is excepted. And His saying: ﴿So the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them﴾ [Al-Muddaththir 48], and this is excepted. Therefore it is special to them.
The saying of God, Exalted: ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; then to Him you will be returned﴾ [Az-Zumar 44]. This sentence contains restriction, which is fronting of what should be delayed. Here the predicate is fronted: ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens﴾, meaning, not to anyone else.
His saying: ﴿the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾ includes dominion over essences, that is, dominion over the very existence of the heavens and the earth, and dominion of disposal over them. He disposes of them as He wills. So to God belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth in creation, management, and disposal, and everything returns to Him, Glorified and Exalted. These gods possess none of that.
So, ﴿the dominion of the heavens﴾ means dominion over essences and disposal as He wills. Then we detail: He created them first, and He holds them lest they cease; He folds up the heaven like the folding of a scroll for writings, and on the Day of Resurrection He will seize the earths. All of these are among His acts of disposal over these things which are owned, the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And since the dominion of the heavens and the earth is His, no one intercedes except by His permission, and no one deserves worship except Him.
Then He said: ﴿Then to Him you will be returned﴾. When? On the Day of Resurrection. We will be returned to God, Mighty and Majestic, and He will call us to account according to our deeds. God, Exalted, has made clear to us, explained, and established the proof. "And He has explained that a good deed is multiplied tenfold up to seven hundred times and beyond, to many multiples, and that an evil deed is recompensed with its like."[[Narrated by al-Bukhari (41), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri.]] He has explained the things that are considered good deeds so that we may do them, and the things considered evil so that we may avoid them. Then our return to Him, Mighty and Majestic, will be a return with insight, and we will have no argument against opposing Him.
Now we return to the benefits of this noble verse. What comes before it, where?
﴿Or have they taken intercessors besides God?﴾ [Az-Zumar 43].
* In this verse: a denunciation of those who worship idols, a denunciation of whoever worships idols and takes them as intercessors. From where do we derive the denunciation? From the hamza contained in (am), because (am) means (bal) and the hamza.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the gross error of these polytheists, in that they worshipped idols and thought them to be intercessors, though they only increase them in distance from God.
* And among the benefits of this noble verse: establishing the rational proof in disputation with an opponent, which is His saying: ﴿Say: Even though they possess nothing and do not understand?﴾ [Az-Zumar 43]. If they possess nothing, how do you take them as intercessors and worship them besides God?
Know that we need rational proofs urgently when faith weakens. Whenever faith weakens, we need rational proofs, because the believer is sufficed by transmitted evidence, by the revealed text. God, Exalted, says: ﴿It is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when God and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should have any choice in their affair﴾ [Al-Ahzab 36]. And 'A'ishah, may God be pleased with her, argued against the woman who asked her: "Why does a menstruating woman make up the fasts but not the prayers?" She said: "This used to happen to us, and we were commanded to make up the fasts, and we were not commanded to make up the prayers."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (321), and Muslim (335 / 69), and the wording is his, from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]] So when faith is strong, deriving proof from the Sunnah and the Qur'an suffices. When faith is weak, convincing rational proof is necessary. For this reason we find God, Glorified, in the Mighty Book often arguing with sensible, observable rational matters to establish and confirm the meanings He wishes to affirm, such as the revival of the dead and similar things. We are now in an age where faith is weak and disputation is abundant, and we need to understand rational proofs so that we can convince our opponents. You know now that many people, if brought every verse, would not follow it, but if brought a rational proof, they are convinced. This is one point.
You also know that the enemies of Islam and the Muslims look for opportunities to refute the arguments of the Muslims. You find them in every gathering speaking about things with which they cast doubt upon the Muslim youth. If a person does not have a rational argument to refute their argument, he may be silenced, and that fierce adversary will prevail over him, as God, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿And among the people is one whose speech in the life of this world pleases you, and he calls God to witness what is in his heart, yet he is the most stubborn of opponents﴾ [Al-Baqarah 204]. So I urge you to take from rational proofs whatever will save you from the opposition of those fierce disputants, so that you may contend with them, argue against them, and overcome them with proof. Abraham, peace be upon him, argued with his people by reason. How? When the night covered him, he saw a star and said: "This is my lord." When it set, he said: ﴿I do not love the setting ones﴾ [Al-An'am 76], I do not love a deity that disappears from me and does not know my state. Then when he saw the moon rising, he said: "This is my lord." When it set, he established the proof against the error of those who worshipped the stars, saying: ﴿If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be among the people who are astray. Then when he saw the sun rising, he said, "This is my lord; this is greater." But when it set, he said, "O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate.﴾ [Al-An'am 77, 78].
Likewise, he argued against the one who disputed with him: ﴿Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord, because God had given him dominion? When Abraham said﴾, to the end of the verse: ﴿Indeed, God brings the sun from the east, so bring it from the west﴾ [Al-Baqarah 258], and so on. So today we need to exercise our minds in rational proofs, so that we may argue with them against those whose faith is weak through transmitted evidence, or against those whose faith in transmitted evidence has been lost.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: idols possess nothing for their worshippers, neither bringing benefit nor repelling harm.
If someone says: Some people call upon an idol and it answers them, as we often hear. How is the answer to this verse?
The answer to this verse: the words of God are true and right, exactly conforming to reality. God has explained in another verse that there is no one more misguided in mind or more foolish in way: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than God those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and who are unaware of their supplication? And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ [Al-Ahqaf 5, 6]. But whatever such things occur, such as a man calling upon a saint or the owner of a grave, or similar, and his harm is removed, that is only a trial from God, Mighty and Majestic, a trial that occurs at the thing, not through the thing.
For example: if a man calls upon a grave and his harm is lifted, do we say that the owner of the grave is the one who lifted it? Not at all. We are certain, like the sun, that the owner of the grave did not benefit him. Rather, God tested the worshipper of this grave by making the thing happen at his hand, not by it. There is a difference between a thing that happens by means of something and a thing that happens at something. God, Mighty and Majestic, may test a person with such a thing. He may make the means of disobedience and polytheism easy for him as a trial and test.
Have you considered the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ, when God forbade them hunting during the state of ihram? With what did God test them? God tested them with game that their hands and spears could reach. The bird is reached by the spear, and the ordinary running animal is reached by hands: that is, gazelles, hares, and similar, they catch with their hands, and birds with their spears, not with arrows; they did not need arrows. God tested them with this, so that God might know who fears Him in the unseen. God may test the servant by making the means of disobedience easy for him, until God, Glorified and Exalted, knows whether he will be patient or will proceed. Because some people find it easy to refrain from disobedience when it is difficult for them, as it requires effort and requires wealth. But when it becomes easy, and then he refrains, it is known that the man is sincere in his faith. Is that not so?
So we have understood the answer to His saying: ﴿Even though they possess nothing and do not understand?﴾ [Az-Zumar 43]: that what happens which is thought to be due to these gods has in fact occurred at them, not by them.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 39, verses 43–44 (part 3 of 3):

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: these deities lack intellect. This applies to those who worship what has no intellect, such as idols and trees, based on His words: ﴿and they do not understand﴾. Accordingly, if we restrict the matter to those who worship idols, trees, and the like, it is not objected that some people worshipped the Messiah, peace be upon him, who was among the most perfect of people in intellect, since he is one of the Messengers of firm resolve (Uli al-'Azm). We would say: God means by this the idols, which are what? Inanimate objects that do not understand.
Then God Most High said: ﴿Say: "To God belongs all intercession. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth"﴾ [az-Zumar 44], to the end.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of intercession, ﴿To God belongs all intercession﴾. The proof of its affirmation is that, were it not existent, it would not be correct to say ﴿To God belongs all intercession﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the refutation of the Mu'tazilah and the Khawarij, since the Mu'tazilah and the Khawarij deny intercession?
* Student: (...).
* The Shaykh: Yes. The Mu'tazilah and the Khawarij reject intercession for the people of major sins, whether they enter the Fire or not. This is because, according to the Mu'tazilah and the Khawarij, the people of major sins are eternal in the Fire. However, according to the Khawarij they are disbelievers, and according to the Mu'tazilah they are neither believers nor disbelievers, being in an intermediate position between two positions.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of multiple intercessions, based on His words: ﴿all﴾, since ﴿all﴾ requires that there be something gathered together.
* Among its benefits: no one intercedes except by God's permission. The reason is that if intercession belongs exclusively to God, then it exists only from Him and returns only to Him.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of God's dominion over the heavens and the earth, and His sole sovereignty, based on His words: ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth﴾.
* Among its benefits: the affirmation of the Resurrection and the return to God, based on His words: ﴿Then to Him you will be returned﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: warning and glad tidings, based on His words: ﴿Then to Him you will be returned﴾. The believer is undoubtedly delighted to meet God and loves to meet God, while the disbeliever is the opposite. The Prophet, peace be upon him, said: "Whoever loves to meet God, God loves to meet him, and whoever dislikes to meet God, God dislikes to meet him"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6507) and Muslim (2683/14), from the hadith of 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit.]]. So when we know that we will return to God, we love to meet God, and the disbeliever dislikes meeting God.
﴿Then to Him you will be returned﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that God, glorified and exalted, mentions a thing by warning of its necessary consequence, since mere return contains nothing worth mentioning. Rather, what is meant is the return by which reckoning and recompense take place.
God Most High said: ﴿Or have they taken intercessors besides God?﴾ [az-Zumar 43]. He said: (﴿Or﴾ means "rather," and ﴿they have taken besides God﴾). We do not, however, read ("ittakhadhu") with the cutting hamzah (hamzat al-qat'), because in the Qur'an the hamzah is not a cutting hamzah. But if the construction were outside the Qur'an, we would say: "Bal ittakhadhu min dunihi" (rather, they have taken besides Him). If we say "ittakhadhu," someone will ask: where did the connecting hamzah (hamzat al-wasl) in ﴿ittakhadhu﴾ go? We say: because the cutting hamzah entered upon the verb, we dispensed with the connecting hamzah, since the connecting hamzah is only brought in to facilitate beginning with a consonant cluster. When we do not begin with it, and begin with a cutting hamzah, we dispense with it and delete it. Recite: ﴿Has He chosen daughters over sons?﴾ [as-Saffat 153], "asta fa." Its original form is "istafa," and the hamzah was added to it. When the hamzah was added to it, we no longer needed the connecting hamzah, since the connecting hamzah is brought in only out of necessity. For this reason it is called the connecting hamzah: it is brought in out of necessity, to avoid beginning with a consonant. When that necessity disappears, it is dropped.
He said: (﴿Or have they taken besides God intercessors﴾ [az-Zumar 43], meaning the idols are gods that ﴿intercede﴾ with God ﴿according to their claim﴾). That is, they made these idols gods that would intercede for them with God.
The author's words "according to their claim" mean not in reality, because these idols do not intercede for them. Rather, on the Day of Resurrection, whoever took a god alongside God will disavow the worship of those who worshipped him. Is that correct? From where do we derive this? ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than God, one who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they are unaware of their supplication? And when mankind are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ [al-Ahqaf 5–6]. Likewise what you mentioned: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection, they will deny your association﴾ [Fatir 14]. Moreover, even those who took others than the Messengers as leaders, followers of misguidance, will disown them: ﴿When those who were followed disown those who followed﴾ [al-Baqarah 166]. Observe, glory be to God, that the Qur'an declares disbelief for those who were made partners in messengership, and declares disbelief for those who were made partners in worship. This is because each of them did not fulfil the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is the Messenger of God. As for those who took partners in worship, you have heard: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection, they will deny your association﴾, and ﴿When mankind are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾. As for those who took partners in messengership: ﴿When those who were followed disown those who followed﴾. This is because whoever follows someone other than the Messengers, opposing the words of the Messengers with his own words, has associated him with the Messengers in messengership.
Who among mankind must be followed? The Messengers. So if a person makes his leader equal in status to the Messenger, peace be upon him, taking from him in action, abandonment, and affirmation, he has made him a messenger. For this reason some scholars say: tawhid is of two kinds, tawhid of worship and tawhid of messengership. Tawhid of worship concerns the right of God, and tawhid of messengership concerns the right of the Messenger ﷺ. God Most High joins these two in the Qur'an: ﴿Do they not ponder the Word, or has there come to them what did not come to their forefathers of old? Or do they not recognize their Messenger, so that they deny him?﴾ [al-Mu'minun 68–69]. The conclusion is that those who took intercessors have strayed into manifest error, because these intercessors will not benefit them.
He said: (﴿Say﴾ to them: will they intercede even though ﴿they possess nothing and do not understand﴾). Will they intercede even though they are...? The author, may God have mercy on him, followed in this commentary one of the two well-known opinions regarding the case where the interrogative hamzah enters upon a conjunctive particle. What are the two?
* Student: (...) before the hamzah, or before the interrogative particle.
The second: that the conjunction is upon what follows the interrogative hamzah or the interrogative particle.
* The Shaykh: There are two views. The first view: that the conjunction is upon what preceded, and in this case the hamzah is understood to come after the conjunctive particle.
The second view: that the conjunction is upon an implied sentence whose content is determined by the context. Did the author follow the first or the second?
* Student: The first.
* Another student: The second.
* The Shaykh: Look, everyone, "will they intercede even though"?
* Students: The second.
* The Shaykh: Then it is the second, because he supposed the conjoined element between the hamzah and the conjunctive particle. "Will they intercede even though they possess nothing and do not understand" (﴿they possess nothing﴾ of intercession and other things, ﴿and do not understand﴾ that you worship them, nor anything else). The answer is no: these do not intercede, because they do not understand, and they do not possess. They do not understand the worship of one who worships them, and they do not possess anything for him, neither intercession nor anything else.
Then He said: (﴿Say: To God belongs all intercession﴾, meaning He alone is its possessor). From where did he derive "He alone is its possessor"? From the restriction, which is the fronting of the predicate. (He alone is its possessor, so no one intercedes except by His permission), and this is one of the two conditions of intercession. The second is God's approval of the intercessor and His approval of the one for whom intercession is made.
﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth; then to Him you will be returned﴾. He mentioned the comprehensiveness of His dominion and His sole sovereignty after mentioning intercession, because intercession in reality derives from sovereignty, and so it falls within God's general dominion over the heavens and the earth. ﴿Then to Him you will be returned﴾. He did not explain it, because it is clear.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 39, verse 45:

Allah the Exalted said: (﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink﴾) i.e., apart from their deities (﴿shrink﴾) recoil (nafarat). No, let us first explain.

﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink﴾ [Az-Zumar 45]. ﴿When Allah is mentioned﴾ means He is praised by remembrance and sincerity, and that He is the Lord who is worshipped, and that none other deserves worship, when He is mentioned in this manner. ﴿The hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink﴾, meaning they recoil from this and dislike it, because they do not want it. They want their gods to be equal to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿And when those other than Him are mentioned, behold, they rejoice﴾ (﴿those other than Him﴾ refers to the idols), and they are praised, ﴿behold, they rejoice﴾. (Here "idha" (إذا) is the particle of sudden surprise (fuja'iyyah), which introduces the answer to the condition, because the condition is sometimes linked with the particle "fa" (فـ) and sometimes with "idha". ﴿And if an evil befalls them for what their hands have sent forth, behold, they despair﴾ [Ar-Rum 36], meaning "fa-hum" (then they). So the answer to the condition here is linked with the sudden "idha", because it is a nominal sentence.)

Consider His saying ﴿behold, they rejoice﴾ [Az-Zumar 45], where the nominal sentence is used, indicating the continuity, firmness and rootedness of their rejoicing within themselves. And Allah knows best.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: What about?

* Student: The acceptance of the texts and how to deal with them, and also the refutation of the orientalists and others (...)?

* Shaykh: Does one rely on reason in accepting the texts, meaning whatever agrees with reason they accept and whatever does not, they reject? No, we do not want this, because any reason that contradicts a text is not reason. What ruined these people and undermined their minds is that they began relying on reason before examining the texts. Had they examined the texts first, then subjected them to reason, they would have known with certainty that the transmitted text agrees with reason.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: No, this is a mistake. In matters of the unseen, do you not refer to reason? That is why we say to those who refer to reason in unseen matters: you have now departed from reason. Reason can never speak about something that is absent from it at all.

If someone said to you: "Speak about what is behind this wall," could you rationally speak about it? If you did, you would be a raving fool. Those who have resorted to reason in this way have, in reality, resorted to whim. It is a whim and not reason. Yet it is called reason, because it has "restrained" them (the root meaning of "reason" ('aql) being restraint) from hitting the truth; otherwise it would not be reason. Clear? When we say "hold fast to rational proofs," we do not mean the reason of these people, because every argument they want is not a proof but a doubt (shubhah), and what removes it is what? Clear reason together with sound transmitted text.

* Student: (...).

* Shaykh: Yes indeed. Rational proofs may undoubtedly be hidden from some people, but when a person reflects on the indications of the Quran, he finds in it many rational proofs, such as Abraham's argument with his people and with the one who argued with him about his Lord, and such as Allah's argument concerning the Messenger at the end of Surat at-Tur. These are, in reality, all rational proofs. Likewise, contemplation and reflection on the universe and the creatures guide you to this. Also, in arithmetic methods you are greatly guided to reason. We know that half of two is one, and double one is two. By such methods you may be guided to rational proofs. In any case, rational proofs are, in reality, first an innate disposition (gharizah) placed by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in the heart of a person, and then an acquired skill through practice in studying books that investigate this, such as the books of Shaykh al-Islam Ibn Taymiyyah, from which you will benefit greatly.

* Student: We mean by rational proofs the sensory proofs.

* Shaykh: The sensory ones, because sensory proofs are a path to rational proofs. Rational proofs are of two kinds: sensory proofs, which are stronger than theoretical proofs. For example, how do we know that the world originated? By its change from state to state and from one person to another: this one dies and that one lives, and similar things.

We also argue for the origination of the world by saying: there is nothing existing except that it is either originated by itself, or its originator is other than itself, or it came into being by chance. All three of these are impossible except one. What is it? That its originator is other than it.

* * *

* Student: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate: ﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink, and when those other than Him are mentioned, behold, they rejoice (45). Say, "O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ" (46). And if for those who did wrong was whatever is on earth entirely and the like of it with it, they would surely ransom themselves therewith from the evil of the Day of Resurrection. And there will appear to them from Allah that which they had not been counting on (47). And there will appear to them the evils of what they earned, and there will surround them that which they used to mock﴾ [Az-Zumar 45–48].

* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: ﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink, and when those other than Him are mentioned, behold, they rejoice﴾. Where is the answer to "idha" in His saying ﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned﴾?

* Student: ﴿Behold, they rejoice﴾.

* Shaykh: ﴿When Allah alone is mentioned﴾?

* Student: ﴿Shrink﴾.

* Shaykh: ﴿Shrink﴾. And where is the answer to ﴿And when those other than Him are mentioned﴾?

* Student: ﴿Behold, they rejoice﴾.

* Shaykh: What is the link of the sentence? If the sentence is nominal, it must have a link (rabit). So what is its link here? The sudden "idha". I think we have not yet taken the benefits of the verse.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says, describing the state of these disbelieving deniers: ﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink﴾.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the intensity of these people's aversion to the remembrance of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and to His monotheism, as shown by His saying ﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned, they shrink﴾.

* And among its benefits: whenever a person finds aversion towards the law of Allah, there is in him a resemblance to these people, even if he does not resemble them in every respect, but there is some resemblance to them.

* And among the benefits of this noble verse: the intensity of these people's attachment to their idols, since they dislike what opposes them of monotheism. When these idols are mentioned, they rejoice.

* And among its benefits: that a person may rejoice at evil and at what opposes the natural disposition (fitrah), and this is shown by His saying ﴿And when those other than Him are mentioned, behold, they rejoice﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 39, verse 46–48 (part 1 of 4):

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Say, "O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ."﴾ [Az-Zumar 46] ﴿Allahumma﴾: this is a vocative (munada) from which the vocative particle "ya" has been dropped, and the letter "meem" has been substituted for it. The "meem" was added because it indicates plurality, as if the person has gathered his heart upon his Lord, may He be exalted. It was placed at the end for the sake of blessing, by beginning with the Name of Allah, may He be glorified and exalted. Accordingly, we say: "Allah" is a vocative (munada) built on the dammah, in a position of nasb.

As for His saying ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾: "fatir" of a thing means its innovator, without a precedent example, meaning its originator and creator for the first time; this is called "fatr," and from it comes "fatara al-bi'r" when he dug the well for the first time.

﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾: the heavens and the earth have passed by us often, and we have mentioned what relates to the plural form for the heavens and the singular form for the earth.

﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾: "fatir" and "alim" are all attributes of the vocative in His saying ﴿Allahumma﴾, but they are in the accusative because they are in construct form (mudaf).

﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾: the unseen (al-ghayb) is what is absent, and the witnessed (al-shahadah) is what is seen and present. Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, knows all of the unseen and all of the witnessed: ﴿Indeed, nothing is hidden from Allah on the earth or in the heaven﴾ [Al 'Imran 5].

Know that absence may be total or relative. Allah, may He be exalted, knows the unseen totally and also relatively. Unlike mankind, mankind does not know the unseen, meaning what is absent from him, whether totally or relatively. For this reason you do not know what is behind this wall, you do not know what is in the heart of another, you do not know the future, and you even forget what has passed. As for the Lord, may He be mighty and majestic, no such deficiency afflicts Him.

﴿You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ﴾ [Az-Zumar 46]: ﴿judge between Your servants﴾ means You will separate between them with judgment, and that is on the Day of Resurrection, when people dispute before their Lord, contending with one another. Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, has made clear the outcome of this dispute, that the victorious contenders are the believers, as He said: ﴿So Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾ [An-Nisa' 141]. Therefore, the victorious contender is the believers; since there is no way for the disbelievers over them, they are without doubt the victorious ones.

His saying ﴿You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ﴾ includes judgment in this world and judgment in the Hereafter. As for judgment in this world, the reference is to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him. As for the Hereafter, the reference is to Allah, may He be mighty and majestic, who judges between them with a judgment of recompense, each according to what he deserves.

His saying ﴿You will judge between Your servants﴾: the intended meaning of servitude here is the general servitude, which includes the believing servant and the disbelieving servant. The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, have divided servitude into two categories: general and specific. General servitude is submission to the decree (qadar), meaning it relates to the matter of divine decree; everyone in the heavens and the earth is a servant of Allah in this sense, unable to deviate from what Allah has decreed for him. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾ [Maryam 93]. This servitude, as I said, relates to qadar and decree, so it is in reality a universal servitude (kawniyyah).

The second is specific servitude: worshipping Allah, may He be exalted, by His law (shar'). Who is this specific servitude for? For the believers, who worship Allah by His law. This specific servitude also contains a more particular servitude, which is the servitude of prophethood and messengership, such as His saying: ﴿And mention Our servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, owners of strength and vision﴾ [Sad 45], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, he was a grateful servant﴾ [Al-Isra' 3], and the saying of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him: "Should I not love to be a grateful servant?"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4837), and the wording is his, and Muslim (2820/81), from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]]. The examples are many. So it has become clear now what servitude is?

* Student: General and specific.
* Shaykh: Yes. What is general servitude?
* Student: General servitude is worshipping Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, through decree.
* Shaykh: Yes, that is, humbling oneself to His decree. Does this include...?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes. And the specific?
* Student: The specific is worshipping Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, by His law.
* Shaykh: By His law. And this specific is for whom?
* Student: For the believers.
* Shaykh: For the believers. This specific servitude is divided into specific and more specific. Good, what is the more specific servitude?
* Student: The more specific is restricted to the prophets and messengers.
* Shaykh: Yes, to the prophets and messengers. Its example?
* Student: His saying: ﴿And mention Our servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, owners of strength and vision﴾ [Sad 45], and the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Should I not love to be a grateful servant?"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4837), and the wording is his, and Muslim (2820/81), from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]]
