* Student: ﴿He said, "I was only given it because of knowledge I have." Rather, it is a trial, but most of them do not know. [39:49] Those before them had said the same, but what they used to earn did not avail them. [39:50] So the evils of what they had earned struck them, and those who wronged among these will be struck by the evils of what they earned, and they will not escape. [39:51] Did they not know that Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ [al-Zumar 49–52].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Let us take the benefits from what preceded: ﴿Say, "O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ"﴾ [al-Zumar 46].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: seeking a means (tawassul) to Allah, the Exalted, by His actions, as indicated by His saying: ﴿Say, "O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth"﴾.

We have already passed, in what came before, that permissible tawassul (seeking a means to Allah) has seven types:
The first: seeking a means to Allah through His names.
The second: seeking a means to Allah through His attributes.
The third: seeking a means to Allah through His actions.
The fourth: seeking a means to Allah through the state of the one supplicating.
The fifth: seeking a means to Allah, the Exalted, through the supplication of one whose answer is hoped for.
The sixth: seeking a means to Allah through righteous deeds.
The seventh: seeking a means to Allah through faith. All of these are permissible forms of tawassul. So here, ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾ is an instance of seeking a means to Allah through His actions.

As for prohibited tawassul, it is seeking a means to Allah through something that Allah has not made a means, such as seeking a means through the rank of the Prophet (ﷺ), and seeking a means through the righteous in an unlawful manner. So the rule for prohibited tawassul is that one seeks a means to Allah through something that is not a means.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the heavens and the earth are not eternal and pre-existent; rather, they are originated after not having been. This is contrary to the philosophers who said that the world or the spheres are eternal.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's knowledge, indeed the affirmation that Allah's knowledge encompasses everything, as indicated by His saying: ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾.

* Among its benefits: warning a person against opposition, because if he believes that He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, he will be cautious, since however he acts, Allah, the Exalted, knows it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that judgment belongs to Allah alone, as indicated by His saying: ﴿You will judge between Your servants﴾. The point of restriction in His saying ﴿You will judge between Your servants﴾ is that He describes the judgment issued by Him as being between the servants, and a servant does not share his master's judgment. Otherwise, there is no known method of restriction (hasr) among us here, but we derived it from the meaning. Since a servant cannot be a judge over his master, rather the master is the judge.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: consolation for the believers, because Allah, the Exalted, judges between them concerning what they differ about with the disbelievers.
Here we ask: To whom is judgment passed in favor and against? To the believers, by the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾ [al-Nisa 141].
Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if those who wronged possessed whatever is on the earth﴾ to the end.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that if the wrongdoers were to expend everything on the earth to ransom themselves with it, it would not benefit them. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿And there will appear to them from Allah what they had not reckoned﴾.

* And among them: that everything in this world becomes worthless at the time of punishment, when the wrongdoer witnesses it, as indicated by His saying: ﴿they would ransom themselves with it from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection﴾.

* Among its benefits: warning against wrongdoing, because mentioning this implies a warning against wrongdoing.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the Resurrection and the Resurrection of the dead, as indicated by His saying: ﴿they would ransom themselves with it from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the punishment that befalls these wrongdoers does not occur to their minds, as indicated by His saying: ﴿And there will appear to them from Allah what they had not reckoned﴾.
Then the Exalted said: ﴿And there will appear to them the evils of what they earned, and what they used to mock will surround them﴾ [al-Zumar 48].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the recompense is of the same kind as the deed, as indicated by His saying: ﴿the evils of what they earned﴾.

* Among its benefits: the affirmation of acquisition (kasb) for the servant, which is a refutation of the Jabriyyah (determinists), who say that man is compelled in his actions. We say to them: Rather, man is not compelled, and his deed is his acquisition.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: rebuke of these tormented people, since what they used to mock has befallen them. Allah, the Exalted, has said that it will be said to them: ﴿Is this magic, or is it that you do not see?﴾ [al-Tur 15], because in the world they used to ridicule the one who brought this news and say that it is magic. So on the Day of Resurrection they will be rebuked, and it will be said to them: ﴿Is this magic, or is it that you do not see?﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that mocking Allah, the Exalted, and His verses is a cause of punishment, and it is disbelief that takes one out of the religion, as indicated by the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Say, "Was it Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking? Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief"﴾ [al-Tawbah 65–66]. Based on this, it should be attached to marriage, divorce, taking back a wife, and emancipation, because its joke is serious. There is no disagreement among the scholars that whoever says a statement mocking the religion of Allah disbelieves.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿So when adversity touches man, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow upon him a favor from Us, he says, "I was only given it because of knowledge"﴾ [al-Zumar 49]. ﴿So when adversity touches man﴾, that is, afflicts him. The intended meaning of "man" here is the species. It is said that the intended meaning is the disbeliever. As for the one who said the intended meaning is the species, and that it includes both believer and disbeliever, he said: This is the nature of man, and the believer who acknowledges the blessings of Allah to Him and thanks Him is outside the nature of man. That is, Allah bestowed grace upon him, and he went out of the requirement of human nature.

As for the one who said that the intended meaning (i.e., of "man") is the disbeliever, then it is from the category of the general term used to mean the specific. He said: Because this described attribute is only found in the disbeliever. When adversity touches him, he returns to Allah, and when He gives him a blessing, he exults in it and says: No one has any favor over me in it, and it is only through knowledge. And this latter view is closer to the truth, because when Allah grants a believer a blessing, he gives thanks, and he does not say, "I was only given it because of knowledge."

He says: ﴿So when adversity touches man, he calls upon Us﴾, that is, he asks Us to remove his harm. Then, when We remove the adversity and bestow upon him a favor from Us by removing the harm that had befallen him, he says: ﴿I was only given it because of knowledge﴾, meaning I was given this thing because of knowledge. And what is meant by "knowledge" here? Does the meaning mean "given it because of knowledge from Allah that I am deserving of it, so I am worthy and entitled to it," or does it mean "because of knowledge on my part of the ways of acquiring wealth"?

It includes both matters. He says: "I was given it because of knowledge that I am worthy, and I was also given it through my own acquisition." Thereby he becomes one who claims favor over Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and becomes self-willed, combining two things: claiming favor, and saying that there is no grace from Allah, since He gave me that because He knows I am worthy of it. And the second: self-reliance and not attributing the matter back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 39, verses 46–48 (part 3 of 4):

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Nay, it is a trial.﴾ ﴿Nay, it is﴾: that is, the statement or the state. Both readings are possible. It may mean that when Allah gives him these blessings, the giving itself is a trial for him. It may also mean that this statement is a trial for him. The first meaning is closer, however: Allah tests the servant by removing harm from him and bringing him good and blessings. How many people have been tested by the blessings of Allah, so that they were upright, but blessings turned them away! In a hadith, Allah the Exalted said: "Among My servants there is one whom, if I made him wealthy, wealth would corrupt him, and among them there is one whom, if I made him poor, poverty would corrupt him."[[Al-Asma' wa al-Sifat by al-Bayhaqi (231), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]] Allah is capable of all things, and He may choose for His servant what is better for him without the servant realizing it. The apparent meaning of His words ﴿Nay, it is a trial﴾ is: nay, this condition is a trial, namely the bestowing of blessings. Sulayman, upon him be prayers and peace, said: ﴿This is by the bounty of my Lord, to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful.﴾ [An-Naml 40] ﴿But most of them do not know.﴾ The resumptive particle here (al-istidrak, a corrective "but") means that those who were overwhelmed by the blessings of Allah were heedless of the One who bestowed them, the Giver and the Bestower of them. So they did not know the thankfulness due to this Benefactor, and they also did not know that these blessings were a trial. Instead, a person takes blessings as a matter of course and something natural, and he is heedless that Allah is testing him with them.

﴿Those before them had already said it.﴾ The pronoun in ﴿had already said it﴾ refers back to the statement ﴿I have only been given it on account of knowledge﴾. ﴿Those before them had already said it﴾, such as Qarun: ﴿He said: I have only been given it on account of knowledge I have.﴾ Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Did he not know that Allah had already destroyed before him generations that were stronger than him in might and greater in accumulation?﴾ [Al-Qasas 78]

﴿Those before them had already said it, but what they had earned did not avail them.﴾ The word (ma) here is negating. The verb ﴿avail﴾ (aghna) means "to ward off." So ﴿what they had earned did not avail them﴾ means that what they had earned did not ward off any of the punishment of Allah from them. Likewise, blessings do not avail whoever boasts of them and is heedless of obedience to Allah. Have you not seen how 'Ad were arrogant upon the earth, and ﴿said: Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾ [Fussilat 15]? That is because Allah had given them great strength. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them in strength? And they used to deny Our signs. So We sent upon them a furious wind during ill-omened days.﴾ [Fussilat 15–16] Consider how these people were punished with the wind, which is the most gentle of things. The wind is the gentlest of things, yet they were punished by it as retribution for their saying: ﴿Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾ That is, they were not destroyed by thunderbolts or by a stone-laden storm from the sky, but were destroyed by this gentle wind. When they saw what this wind brought and carried of sand, they said: ﴿This is a cloud bringing us rain.﴾ [Al-Ahqaf 24] Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Rather, it is that which you were impatient for: a wind containing painful punishment, destroying everything by the command of its Lord.﴾ [Al-Ahqaf 24–25]

The Exalted said: ﴿But what they had earned did not avail them. So the evils of what they had earned struck them.﴾ [Az-Zumar 50–51] That is, the recompense for their evil deeds struck them. He called the recompense "evils" because the evil deeds were its cause, and to make clear that the recompense corresponds exactly to the deed, so that it is as if it were the deed itself.

﴿So the evils of what they had earned struck them, and those who wronged among these will be struck by the evils of what they earned.﴾ [Az-Zumar 51] The conjunction (wa) in His words ﴿and those who wronged﴾ is resumptive (isti'nafiyya), and (alladhina) is the subject (mubtada'). The clause ﴿will strike them﴾ is the predicate. ﴿And those who wronged among these will be struck by the evils of what they earned, as those before them were struck.﴾

﴿And they cannot escape.﴾ (Ma) is negating. Is it Hijazi or Tamimi? In fact, nothing in the wording indicates either. However, the Qur'an is in the dialect of Quraysh, as evidenced by His words: ﴿This is not a human; this is none but a noble angel.﴾ [Yusuf 31] Accordingly, whenever (ma) occurs, it is to be understood as Hijazi. But how do we parse it in a construction like this? In ﴿and they cannot escape﴾ we say: ﴿they﴾ is its subject, the (ba') is an extra preposition, and ﴿cannot escape﴾ is its predicate, in the accusative, marked by an implied yā'. The yā' that appears is the mark of the genitive, not of the accusative. The genitive mark is due to the extra preposition (ba'). We gave the governing role to the visible element, the (ba'), while the position (mahall) is assumed by estimation. So it is accusative, with an implied yā' in place of the visible one governed by the extra preposition.

As for ﴿mu'jizin﴾: is it the active participle of (ajaza), or of (a'jaza)? It is from (a'jaza). That means they cannot make Allah incapable, so He cannot be prevented from punishing them. Their punishment is a light matter for Allah, the Exalted.

﴿Do they not know that Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ [Az-Zumar 52] The hamza here is interrogative (istifham), and the (wa) is a conjunction. What is the conjoined element? It is either omitted and to be supplied according to the context, or it is what came before. If we say it is what came before, then the hamza is taken to be placed after the conjunction. The implied sense is: "and have they not known?" If we take the first view, the hamza is attached to an omitted element, whose sense is: "have they been ignorant, and not known?"

﴿Do they not know that Allah extends provision﴾: ﴿extends﴾ means "widens," and ﴿provision﴾ means "gift." ﴿To whom He wills and restricts it﴾: ﴿to whom He wills﴾ means He widens it for him as a test for this person to whom it is extended. ﴿And restricts it﴾ means He narrows it, also as a test, because narrowing involves a test and expansion involves a test. However, among people, by custom, narrowing is generally called a trial (ibtila'), that is an affliction (bala'). Expansion is a test (imtihan), even though trial (ibtila') and test (imtihan) have the same meaning. A person is tried by whatever he is tried with, so that Allah may test him: will he be patient or will he be impatient? As for what Allah tries him with in blessings, the question is whether he will be thankful or ungrateful.

﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ ﴿In that﴾ refers to the extending and restricting. ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe﴾: that is, signs that Allah alone is the One who disposes of affairs. That is why we find some people who are skilled in buying and selling and in acquiring wealth, and who have ability and strength, yet their provision is restricted. And we find some people who are less than this, meaning they do not care about affairs and do not have that skill, yet Allah widens their provision for them. This shows that Allah, the Exalted, is the One who disposes of His servants: He widens for this one and restricts for that one. But this does not mean that we should not take the means, as we will mention, Allah willing, in the benefits (al-fawa'id).

We now return to the words of the author, may Allah have mercy on him, who says: ("﴿So when harm touches man﴾" – the generic noun) Yes, what?

In any case, we have a conflict between an affirming and a negating statement, and the affirming takes precedence over the negating.

Shaykh: Alright, it does not contradict. ﴿And if those who wronged possessed﴾: so this is a middle position. He said: ﴿And if those who wronged possessed everything on earth and the like of it with it, they would surely ransom themselves with it from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ [Az-Zumar 47] ﴿If those who wronged﴾: the author did not explain it or clarify it. But we have explained in the tafsir that it includes the greater injustice, which is shirk, and the lesser, which is anything below it. However, it appears, and Allah knows best, that what is meant is the greater.

﴿And the like of it with it﴾: that is, what is on earth and its like added to it. ﴿They would surely ransom themselves with it from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection, and there will appear to them﴾ [Az-Zumar 47]: ﴿appear﴾ means "become manifest."

Alright, it does not contradict. ﴿And if those who wronged﴾: so this is a middle position. He said: ﴿And if those who wronged possessed everything on earth and the like of it with it, they would surely ransom themselves with it from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ [Az-Zumar 47]

﴿If those who wronged﴾: the author did not explain it or clarify it. But we have explained in the tafsir that it may include the greater injustice, which is shirk, and the lesser, which is what is below it. However, it appears, and Allah knows best, that what is meant is the greater. ﴿And the like of it with it﴾: that is, what is in the earth, and its like added to it.

﴿And there will appear to them from Allah what they had not reckoned﴾ ("reckoned" means "expected"). The author, may Allah have mercy on him, does not explain what is clear. It is said (bada) and it is said (bada'a), and there is a difference between them. (Bada) means what? 

Students: "Appeared."

Shaykh: "Appeared." (Bada'a) means "began," and in the verbal noun for the first one one says (budūwan): (bada yabdu budūwan). For the second one says (bada'a yabda'u bad'an).

He says: (﴿And there will appear to them the evils of what they earned, and there will befall them what they used to mock﴾ [Az-Zumar 48], that is the punishment). That is, the punishment befalls them, meaning it descends upon them, and their evils become apparent to them and they recognize them. They used to say: ﴿Would that we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers.﴾ [Al-An'am 27] Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Nay, there has appeared to them what they had been concealing before. And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden.﴾ [Al-An'am 28] We seek refuge in Allah.

﴿So when harm touches man﴾ [Az-Zumar 49] (﴿man﴾ is the generic noun). That is, is the intended meaning the genus, so that it includes?

Students: The believer and the disbeliever.

Shaykh: The believer and the disbeliever. But it has become clear from what we discussed that the apparent intended meaning is?

Students: The disbeliever.

Shaykh: The disbeliever. So it is a general term that is intended in a specific sense. A general term used for a specific meaning is very common in the Arabic language, such as His words: ﴿Those to whom people said: Indeed the people have gathered against you﴾ [Al 'Imran 173]. We know that not all people came saying this, but the one who said it was one person, or some specific people. As for "all of the sons of Adam," no. So the intended meaning of "man" here is the genus according to the author's words, and according to the view we have chosen, it is the disbeliever.

("﴿Harm called upon Us, then when We bestow upon him a blessing from Us, he says: I have only been given it on account of knowledge.﴾" ) His words ﴿bestow﴾ mean "give," ﴿a blessing﴾ mean "a favor." There is something to consider here: the favor is the act of the benefactor, and the blessing is the gift of the benefactor, meaning the thing given. Which is more fitting: to explain "blessing" as "favor," or to explain "blessing" as what is given to the person?

Students: As what is given to the person.

Shaykh: The second is the apparent meaning, and it is also the actual reality, because "bestowing" means that there is something bestowed, namely the blessing, such as children, provision, wives, dwellings, and other things.

("﴿He said: I have only been given it on account of knowledge﴾" from Allah that I am deserving of it.) This is one of the two views on the verse. The second view is: ﴿on account of knowledge﴾ means on account of skill and expertise in what I have done. And Allah knows best.

Student: Those who said that the intended meaning of "man" is the generic and not the specific (...) the Prophet's hadith, peace and blessings be upon him, that Allah created creation (...) the hadith indicates that (...).

Shaykh: On the fitrah (natural disposition), yes.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: They say that this is after a person is created, he inclines toward this thing, because the nature of man is that he takes pride in himself, boasts of himself, and forgets others. But in any case, what we have mentioned is the correct view.

Student: The verse was said by (...).

Shaykh: This statement was said.

Student: This statement?

Shaykh: Yes.

Student: ﴿I have only been given it﴾.

Shaykh: That is: "I was given what I was granted."

Student: Not the pronoun.

Shaykh: The (ha') (...).

Student: It refers to (...).

Shaykh: It refers to what was bestowed. "I have only been given what I was granted." The (ha') in ("given it") refers to the one bestowed.

Student: Is the attribution of a thing to oneself an attribution of honor? And if so, does the meaning of His words ﴿You judge between Your servants﴾ [Az-Zumar 46] include some groups of people?

Shaykh: Yes. Something attributed to Allah may be attributed to Him as an attribution of creation and origination, or it may be an attribution of honor. Here "servants" is general. If it is general, what is meant becomes what?

Student: Creation.

Shaykh: Creation and origination. If it is specific, meaning servanthood is attributed to a specific person or to a group described by a certain quality, then it is an attribution of honor.

Student: When Allah, glorified and exalted is He, bestows a blessing on a servant, when does the servant know whether it is a favor or a test?

Shaykh: Yes, this question will come to us, Allah willing, in the explanation of the benefits. But he knows that if he remains upon obedience to Him, it is a favor, and if it is the opposite, it is a test.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: There is no attribution here. Here there is no attribution.

Student: No, I mean it was attributed to Allah, the Exalted.

Shaykh: (...) what?

Student: (...) the attribution of creation.

Shaykh: No, he meant "servants." It is not "judging."

Student: (...).

Shaykh: No, he means "servants." He says: how can "servants" be attributed to Allah, when what is attributed to Allah implies honor? We say: the servants here include the disbeliever and the believer, and the disbeliever is not deserving of honor. So we say: what is attributed to Allah is so in both cases.

Student: Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿But most of them do not know.﴾ Can we be certain that the intended meaning of "man" is the genus, since all disbelievers do not know?

Shaykh: How?

Student: He said: ﴿But most of them do not know﴾ (...) is the intended meaning of "man" (...)?

Shaykh: No. Among the disbelievers there is one who is obstinate and knows the truth but is obstinate about what he is upon. Yes (...).

* * *

Student: ﴿And those who wronged among these will be struck by the evils of what they earned, and they cannot escape. Do they not know that Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ [Az-Zumar 51–52]

Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. I think we are discussing the author's commentary. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, said: ﴿So when harm touches man, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow upon him a blessing from Us, he says: "I have only been given it on account of knowledge." Nay, it is a trial, but most of them do not know.﴾ [Az-Zumar 49] Up to here, I think?

Student: (...).

Shaykh: Yes. He said: ﴿Nay, it is a trial﴾ [Az-Zumar 49]. (﴿Nay, it is﴾ that is, the statement ﴿a trial﴾, a calamity by which the servant is tested.) This is the view the author followed, that the trial refers to the statement he made. But the correct view is that the trial is the blessing Allah gave him, or the condition he was in when harm touched him and then the harm was removed from him and replaced with a blessing. This is a trial by which Allah tests His servants. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We test you with evil and with good as a trial, and to Us you will be returned.﴾ [Al-Anbiya' 35]

(﴿But most of them do not know﴾) That granting of provision is a lure (istidraj) and a trial. ﴿But most of them﴾ means most people, and the pronoun has returned to an unmentioned antecedent because of context and the flow of the discourse. It is also possible that what is meant is "most of them" in the sense of most of mankind, the sons of Adam, so the pronoun here returns to "man" according to meaning rather than wording. As for his statement, "that granting of provision is a lure and a trial": if someone asks, "How do we know that granting of provision is a lure and a trial?"

The answer: we know this from a person's persistence in disobedience while the blessings of Allah, glorified and exalted, keep coming to him. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that the respite We give them is good for their souls. We only give them respite that they may increase in sin, and for them there is a humiliating punishment﴾ [Ali 'Imran 178]. This is the sign: when you see Allah bestowing blessings upon you while you persist in His disobedience, know that this is a lure (istidraj). But when you see Allah bestowing blessings upon you while you are establishing His obedience, know that this is an increase of His bounty and blessings. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿If you are grateful, I will surely increase you﴾ [Ibrahim 7].

(﴿Indeed, this was said before them﴾ [az-Zumar 50] by the nations before them, such as Qarun and his people who were content with it) That is, with this saying: those before them said it. That is, after Allah had given them blessings, they said: ﴿I was only given it on account of knowledge I have﴾. Allah has explicitly mentioned this about Qarun in Surah al-Qasas, when he went out before his people in his finery. His people advised him and said to him: ﴿Do not forget your share of this world, and do good as Allah has done good to you, and do not seek corruption in the land. Indeed, Allah does not love the corrupters.﴾ He said: ﴿I was only given it on account of knowledge I have﴾ [al-Qasas 77–78]. So the statement is the same statement. It has already been noted that a person is impressed by his own deeds and thinks that what he has gained of blessings is due to his deeds, although it is from the bounty of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

﴿So what they used to earn did not avail them﴾. Here "ma" is a negation particle, and we explained it previously. (﴿So the evil consequences of what they earned afflicted them﴾ [az-Zumar 51], that is, their recompense) that is, the evil deeds. He expressed it with the evil deeds themselves, because the recompense is of the same kind as the deed, corresponding to it without exceeding it.

The author said: (﴿And those who wronged among these﴾, that is, the Quraysh, ﴿will be struck by the evil consequences of what they earned, and they will not escape﴾ [az-Zumar 51], meaning, they will not escape Our punishment). They were afflicted with famine for seven years, then provision was expanded for them. They were afflicted with famine for seven years through the supplication of the Prophet (ﷺ) when he said: "O Allah, make it upon them as the years of Joseph."[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (6200) and Muslim (675/295) from Abu Hurayrah.]] They were struck with a severe famine for seven years, to the extent that a person among them would look at the sky and a haze between him and it, like smoke, because of severe hunger and exhaustion.

He said: ﴿Do they not know that Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it﴾ [az-Zumar 52], and so on to the end. This is the beginning of today's lesson, and the benefits have been taken up previously.

* Student: (...) ﴿Say: O My servants﴾.
* Shaykh: Good, let us proceed with the author.

(﴿Do they not know that Allah extends provision﴾, expands it, ﴿to whom He wills﴾, as a test, ﴿and restricts it﴾ [az-Zumar 52], restricts it for whom He wills, as a trial.) In reality, both expansion and restriction are a test and a trial. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We test you with evil and good as a trial; and to Us you will be returned﴾ [al-Anbiya 35]. However, the author followed this approach as a matter of variation in expression, while the meaning is one.

(﴿Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ in it) That is, in this expansion and restriction. Whoever believes in that, that is, in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and in His expansion and restriction, comes to know through it the wisdom of Allah, glorified and exalted.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 39, verse 46–48 (part 1 of 4):

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Say, "O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ."﴾ [Az-Zumar 46] ﴿Allahumma﴾: this is a vocative (munada) from which the vocative particle "ya" has been dropped, and the letter "meem" has been substituted for it. The "meem" was added because it indicates plurality, as if the person has gathered his heart upon his Lord, may He be exalted. It was placed at the end for the sake of blessing, by beginning with the Name of Allah, may He be glorified and exalted. Accordingly, we say: "Allah" is a vocative (munada) built on the dammah, in a position of nasb.

As for His saying ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾: "fatir" of a thing means its innovator, without a precedent example, meaning its originator and creator for the first time; this is called "fatr," and from it comes "fatara al-bi'r" when he dug the well for the first time.

﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾: the heavens and the earth have passed by us often, and we have mentioned what relates to the plural form for the heavens and the singular form for the earth.

﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾: "fatir" and "alim" are all attributes of the vocative in His saying ﴿Allahumma﴾, but they are in the accusative because they are in construct form (mudaf).

﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾: the unseen (al-ghayb) is what is absent, and the witnessed (al-shahadah) is what is seen and present. Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, knows all of the unseen and all of the witnessed: ﴿Indeed, nothing is hidden from Allah on the earth or in the heaven﴾ [Al 'Imran 5].

Know that absence may be total or relative. Allah, may He be exalted, knows the unseen totally and also relatively. Unlike mankind, mankind does not know the unseen, meaning what is absent from him, whether totally or relatively. For this reason you do not know what is behind this wall, you do not know what is in the heart of another, you do not know the future, and you even forget what has passed. As for the Lord, may He be mighty and majestic, no such deficiency afflicts Him.

﴿You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ﴾ [Az-Zumar 46]: ﴿judge between Your servants﴾ means You will separate between them with judgment, and that is on the Day of Resurrection, when people dispute before their Lord, contending with one another. Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, has made clear the outcome of this dispute, that the victorious contenders are the believers, as He said: ﴿So Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾ [An-Nisa' 141]. Therefore, the victorious contender is the believers; since there is no way for the disbelievers over them, they are without doubt the victorious ones.

His saying ﴿You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ﴾ includes judgment in this world and judgment in the Hereafter. As for judgment in this world, the reference is to the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him. As for the Hereafter, the reference is to Allah, may He be mighty and majestic, who judges between them with a judgment of recompense, each according to what he deserves.

His saying ﴿You will judge between Your servants﴾: the intended meaning of servitude here is the general servitude, which includes the believing servant and the disbelieving servant. The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, have divided servitude into two categories: general and specific. General servitude is submission to the decree (qadar), meaning it relates to the matter of divine decree; everyone in the heavens and the earth is a servant of Allah in this sense, unable to deviate from what Allah has decreed for him. Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant﴾ [Maryam 93]. This servitude, as I said, relates to qadar and decree, so it is in reality a universal servitude (kawniyyah).

The second is specific servitude: worshipping Allah, may He be exalted, by His law (shar'). Who is this specific servitude for? For the believers, who worship Allah by His law. This specific servitude also contains a more particular servitude, which is the servitude of prophethood and messengership, such as His saying: ﴿And mention Our servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, owners of strength and vision﴾ [Sad 45], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, he was a grateful servant﴾ [Al-Isra' 3], and the saying of the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him: "Should I not love to be a grateful servant?"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4837), and the wording is his, and Muslim (2820/81), from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]]. The examples are many. So it has become clear now what servitude is?

* Student: General and specific.
* Shaykh: Yes. What is general servitude?
* Student: General servitude is worshipping Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, through decree.
* Shaykh: Yes, that is, humbling oneself to His decree. Does this include...?
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: Yes. And the specific?
* Student: The specific is worshipping Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, by His law.
* Shaykh: By His law. And this specific is for whom?
* Student: For the believers.
* Shaykh: For the believers. This specific servitude is divided into specific and more specific. Good, what is the more specific servitude?
* Student: The more specific is restricted to the prophets and messengers.
* Shaykh: Yes, to the prophets and messengers. Its example?
* Student: His saying: ﴿And mention Our servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, owners of strength and vision﴾ [Sad 45], and the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Should I not love to be a grateful servant?"[[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4837), and the wording is his, and Muslim (2820/81), from the hadith of 'A'ishah.]]
* Shaykh: Well done. Now, which of these types is the object of praise, the specific or the general?
* Students: The specific.
* Shaykh: The specific. As for the general, a person is not praised for it, because it is not by his choice; he is humbled before Allah and worships Him whether he likes it or not.

﴿You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ﴾ [Az-Zumar 46], meaning concerning that over which they differ. The verse has come in this form: ﴿concerning that over which they used to differ﴾, and in another verse: ﴿concerning that over which they differ﴾ [Az-Zumar 3], and He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And whatever you differ over, its ruling is with Allah﴾ [Ash-Shura 10]. It includes what they differ over in matters of religion and also matters of worldly affairs. Allah will judge all of that with His just judgment, which contains no injustice toward anyone.

﴿And if those who wronged had everything on earth and the like of it with it, they would surely ransom themselves therewith from the terrible punishment on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Az-Zumar 47], and so on to the end. "Law" (lau) here is conditional.

Someone may say: where is the protasis (fi'l al-shart)?

The answer: it is implied, meaning "and if it were to occur that..." or "and if it were established that for those who wronged..." As for the apodosis (jawab), it is His saying: ﴿they would surely ransom themselves therewith from the terrible punishment on the Day of Resurrection﴾. "Law" may come as a conditional particle and may come as a verbal-nominal (masdariyyah) particle, such as His saying: ﴿They wish you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾ [Al-Qalam 9], meaning they wish for your compromise, so they would compromise.

﴿And if those who wronged﴾: so "an" and what follows it are in the interpretation of a verbal noun serving as the subject of the implied protasis, meaning "and if it were established that those who wronged." The word "wronged" here means disbelief. Injustice in its original sense is deficiency, as in His saying: ﴿Each of the two gardens produced its fruit and did not fall short of it in anything﴾ [Al-Kahf 33], meaning it did not diminish anything from it. Injustice is divided into two kinds: greater injustice, which is the injustice of disbelief mentioned in His saying: ﴿And it is the disbelievers who are the wrongdoers﴾ [Al-Baqarah 254], and lesser injustice, which is anything below that, such as a person's injustice to another in his wealth, family, and the like. Is the intended injustice here the greater or the lesser? In ﴿And if those who wronged﴾, the intended meaning is the greater, as He said in another verse: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved, if they had whatever is on the earth...﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 36].

﴿Whatever is on the earth, all of it﴾: ﴿ma﴾ is a relative pronoun, meaning "that which." What is its position?  ﴿And if those who wronged had whatever is on the earth﴾.

* Student: It is a relative, O Shaykh.
* Shaykh: Yes, "ma." What is its grammatical position?
* Student: The subject of "inna."
* Shaykh: The subject of "inna," postponed.

﴿And if those who wronged had whatever is on the earth, all of it, and the like of it with it﴾ [Az-Zumar 47], and so on. His saying: ﴿on the earth﴾ is the relative clause complement. It is well known that the relative clause must be a sentence, so how can we make this a relative clause complement when it is not a sentence?

The answer: we say this is a quasi-sentence (shibh jumlah), and it is connected to an omitted verb whose estimate is: "what is settled on the earth."

﴿Whatever is on the earth, all of it﴾: ﴿jami'an﴾ is a circumstantial qualifier (hal) from ﴿ma﴾, meaning in the state of being all gathered for them. ﴿And the like of it with it﴾ means: the like of what is on the earth in its entirety, from its beginning to its end. ﴿They would surely ransom themselves therewith from the terrible punishment on the Day of Resurrection﴾: ﴿they would surely ransom themselves therewith﴾ means they would offer it as a ransom by which they would redeem themselves from the punishment of Allah, may He be mighty and majestic.

But when will this be? This will be on the Day of Resurrection. These people will wish that they had what is on the earth in its entirety and the like of it with it, so that they could ward off the punishment from themselves, but it will not happen. Yet in the world they were asked for something easier than that: what was asked of them? That they worship Allah alone, without partner, and that they establish His law. That is easy, but they, may Allah protect us, were arrogant.

﴿They would surely ransom themselves therewith from the terrible punishment on the Day of Resurrection﴾: that is, from the evil punishment that has no equal in this world, and which the mind cannot grasp by imagination, because just as Paradise contains what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived of bliss, so too the Fire contains a punishment of that kind.

His saying ﴿the Day of Resurrection﴾ is the day on which people will be resurrected. It is called the Day of Resurrection for three reasons:

First: people will stand before the Lord of the worlds, as He said: ﴿The Day when mankind will stand before the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin 6].

Second: justice will be established on it, as He said: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be wronged at all﴾ [Al-Anbiya' 47].

Third: the witnesses will stand on it: ﴿Indeed, We will support Our messengers and those who believed in the life of this world and on the day the witnesses stand﴾ [Ghafir 51]. This is the Day of Resurrection, named for these three matters.

﴿And there will appear to them from Allah that which they had not been counting on﴾ [Az-Zumar 47]: also there will appear to them from Allah, may He be mighty and majestic, ﴿that which they had not been counting on﴾, meaning that which had not been in their reckoning, and it never occurred to them that they would encounter this punishment. They thought the matter was light, they thought the idols would intercede for them, and they entertained many assumptions, but these assumptions did not benefit them; there appeared to them something they had never reckoned with.

﴿And there will appear to them the evils of what they earned, and what they used to mock will surround them﴾ [Az-Zumar 48]: "there will appear to them" means "there will become manifest to them." "The evils of what they earned" means the evil of the deeds they acquired, and they had acquired nothing but evil. Allah, the Exalted, has said: ﴿So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it, and whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it﴾ [Az-Zalzalah 7–8].

(﴿﴿And what they used to mock will surround them﴾﴾ means "descend upon them" ﴿﴿what they used to mock﴾﴾), that is, what they used to mock in the world. As for the Hereafter, they will say: ﴿The messengers of our Lord had certainly come with the truth﴾ [Al-A'raf 53], but at that time it will not benefit them. In the world they used to mock and ridicule the messengers and ridicule those who believed: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they would exchange winks. And when they returned to their own people, they returned jesting. And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are misguided"﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin 29–32].

Glory be to Allah! These verses apply perfectly to our time, just as they applied to those before us. ﴿They used to laugh at those who believed﴾, and this is the reality: you find these corrupt and criminal people, when a pious believer passes by them, they start laughing. ﴿And when they passed by them, they would exchange winks﴾: when they pass by them. Is it when believers pass by criminals or criminals pass by believers? Both. ﴿They would exchange winks﴾: some of them wink at others. Look at this, look at the poor fellow, look at his clothes.

﴿And when they returned to their own people, they returned jesting﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin 31]: that is, they return to their families, ﴿jesting﴾, meaning delighted and amused by what they said about these believers.

﴿And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are misguided"﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin 32]: the subject of "ra'awhum" is the criminals. When those who committed crimes saw these believers, they said: indeed these are misguided, lost. This is the reality even at the present time: when they see the religious person, they say: this one is backward, this one is reactionary, or this one is fundamentalist, meaning extremist, and similar things.

Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿So today those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin 34]. On the Day of Resurrection the believers will laugh at the disbelievers, and that laughter will have no weeping after it, whereas the laughter of those others will be followed by weeping, pain, and regret. ﴿On couches, they will look﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin 35], looking at what Allah has bestowed upon them and at what Allah has punished those others with. ﴿Have the disbelievers not been rewarded for what they used to do?﴾ [Al-Mutaffifin 36].

So these criminals will, on the Day of Resurrection, see manifest what they used to mock of the law of Allah, of Allah's recompense, and similar things. They used to ridicule the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, and what he was promised of bliss and of punishment, saying: O Muhammad, if you are truthful that we will meet this, then let it be for you. Cause the earth to gush forth springs, make the gardens into farms of palm trees, and similar things.

We now return to the words of the author, may Allah have mercy on him, who says: (﴿﴿Say, "O Allah"﴾﴾ meaning "O Allah," i.e., "ya Allah"). How?

﴿And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink with aversion﴾ [Az-Zumar 45]. (﴿﴿When Allah alone is mentioned﴾﴾ means apart from their gods.) ﴿The hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink﴾ (﴿﴿shrink﴾﴾ he says: they recoil and are constricted), so they recoil and do not accept the truth, and they contract and are not opened to the truth. ﴿The hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter﴾, meaning: they do not acknowledge it and do not affirm it, because they said: ﴿There is nothing but our life of this world; we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time﴾ [Al-Jathiyah 24]. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they have no knowledge of that; they only assume﴾ [Al-Jathiyah 24]. Those who do not believe in the Hereafter, and if they had believed in the Hereafter they would have worked for it, and when Allah alone was mentioned they would have rejoiced and been delighted.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 39, verses 46–48 (part 2 of 4):

(﴿And when those other than Him are mentioned﴾) that is, the idols. (﴿behold, they rejoice﴾) When the idols are mentioned with praise and commendation, they rejoice. For this reason it is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he recited: "﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other?﴾ [al-Najm 19–20]," "Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is to be hoped for."[[Musnad al-Bazzar (5096) and al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (12450), from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas. Scholars have rejected this story and declared it weak; see, for example, Fath al-Qadir by al-Shawkani (3/546). Shaykh al-Albani wrote a work on it titled Nasb al-Majaniq li-Nasf Qissat al-Gharaniq.]] It was the Shaytan who cast this into the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ), but the Messenger (ﷺ) did not recite it. Rather, the Shaytan made the Quraysh hear this statement, and they said: "They prostrated with the Prophet (ﷺ) when he finished the surah and prostrated." They said: "Now he has returned to us," or at least "he has flattered us, because he praised our idols, so they prostrated with him." This story is well known, and the exegetes differed about it. Some of them denied it vehemently, and some of them considered it authentic and said that it does not contradict infallibility ('ismah), because Allah said: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he spoke, Satan cast into his speech﴾ [al-Hajj 52]. That is, he recited ﴿Satan cast into his wish﴾, meaning Satan cast into his recitation. It is not that he himself cast it; Satan casts it. ﴿Satan casts into his wish, but Allah abolishes what Satan casts, then Allah makes His verses firm, and Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾ [al-Hajj 52]. "Abolishes" (yansakh) means He makes clear its falsehood and that it has no reality. Then He stated the reason for this: ﴿That He may make what Satan casts a trial for those in whose hearts is disease and whose hearts are hardened, and indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension. And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord and believe in it, and their hearts humble before Him. And indeed, Allah is the Guide of those who believe to a straight path﴾ [al-Hajj 53–54]. So in any case, if the story is authentic, it does not contradict infallibility, because it was Satan who praised these idols. But those who heard it thought it was the recitation of the Prophet (ﷺ). And if it is not authentic, there is no difficulty.

But if someone says: If it is not authentic, how did the polytheists prostrate with the Prophet (ﷺ) when he said: ﴿So prostrate to Allah and worship﴾ [al-Najm 62]?

The answer to that: We say that the final verses of this surah grip the heart and mind, so that a person is moved without being aware of it. These polytheists were so moved by what they heard that they found themselves prostrating without being aware of it. This is the answer if the story is not authentic.

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: (﴿And when those other than Him are mentioned, behold, they rejoice﴾ [39:45]). (﴿Say, "O Allah"﴾) meaning "O Allah," so the mim is a substitute for the vocative particle ya. (﴿Say, "O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth"﴾) its Creator and Originator. (﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾) what is hidden and what is witnessed. (﴿You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ﴾). Here, in my view, the word (fi) is separated from (ma). What is it in your view, is it joined? The rule at the end is that it is separated, but perhaps the rule on which the exegete relies is the first codex, meaning the first rule.

The scholars differed about whether it is permissible to deviate from the 'Uthmanic orthography (al-rasm al-'Uthmani), with three opinions: permissibility, prohibition, and a distinction. The distinction is between writing for a child and writing for an adult. A child is written for according to the rules he knows, because if it were written for him according to the 'Uthmanic orthography he would make mistakes; for example, if the word for prayer (al-salah) were written with a waw and the word for zakah with a waw, and whatever is elongated, meaning with an alif, had its alif omitted, like al-Rahman and similar words, if it were written that way for him he would err and say "inna al-Salawat" and "inna al-Zakawat," and similar. But if it is for a sane adult who knows, it is written in the 'Uthmanic script.

The correct view is that adherence to the script is not obligatory, because the Quran was not revealed in this script. If it had been revealed in this script, as the Torah was revealed written down, we would say it is not permissible to oppose it. But it was revealed as speech, and it happened that the orthographic rule at the time it was written was in this form. Had the writing been in another form, it would have been written in that different form. So the matter is conventional. That is to say, the Quran was not revealed in this form. It is true that we may say that out of courtesy the Quran should be written in the 'Uthmanic orthography, out of respect and veneration for what the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, wrote. But to say this as an obligation and a requirement, and to say that it is not permissible to write a verse of the Book of Allah on the board according to the familiar, well-known rule, is questionable.

(﴿concerning that over which they used to differ﴾) of the matter of religion. The author said: "Guide me to the truth regarding what has been differed about." But this interpretation is questionable, because the intent of the verse is to entrust the matter to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and to complain to Him about these people, who (﴿when Allah alone is mentioned, their hearts shrink from those who do not believe in the Hereafter, but when those other than Him are mentioned, behold, they rejoice﴾). And this is not a place for supplication. Rather, the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say this as a supplication at the beginning of the night prayer. And Allah knows best.

* Student: ﴿He said, "I was only given it because of knowledge I have." Rather, it is a trial, but most of them do not know. [39:49] Those before them had said the same, but what they used to earn did not avail them. [39:50] So the evils of what they had earned struck them, and those who wronged among these will be struck by the evils of what they earned, and they will not escape. [39:51] Did they not know that Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ [al-Zumar 49–52].
* Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Shaytan. Let us take the benefits from what preceded: ﴿Say, "O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ"﴾ [al-Zumar 46].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: seeking a means (tawassul) to Allah, the Exalted, by His actions, as indicated by His saying: ﴿Say, "O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth"﴾.

We have already passed, in what came before, that permissible tawassul (seeking a means to Allah) has seven types:
The first: seeking a means to Allah through His names.
The second: seeking a means to Allah through His attributes.
The third: seeking a means to Allah through His actions.
The fourth: seeking a means to Allah through the state of the one supplicating.
The fifth: seeking a means to Allah, the Exalted, through the supplication of one whose answer is hoped for.
The sixth: seeking a means to Allah through righteous deeds.
The seventh: seeking a means to Allah through faith. All of these are permissible forms of tawassul. So here, ﴿Originator of the heavens and the earth﴾ is an instance of seeking a means to Allah through His actions.

As for prohibited tawassul, it is seeking a means to Allah through something that Allah has not made a means, such as seeking a means through the rank of the Prophet (ﷺ), and seeking a means through the righteous in an unlawful manner. So the rule for prohibited tawassul is that one seeks a means to Allah through something that is not a means.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the heavens and the earth are not eternal and pre-existent; rather, they are originated after not having been. This is contrary to the philosophers who said that the world or the spheres are eternal.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of Allah's knowledge, indeed the affirmation that Allah's knowledge encompasses everything, as indicated by His saying: ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾.

* Among its benefits: warning a person against opposition, because if he believes that He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, he will be cautious, since however he acts, Allah, the Exalted, knows it.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that judgment belongs to Allah alone, as indicated by His saying: ﴿You will judge between Your servants﴾. The point of restriction in His saying ﴿You will judge between Your servants﴾ is that He describes the judgment issued by Him as being between the servants, and a servant does not share his master's judgment. Otherwise, there is no known method of restriction (hasr) among us here, but we derived it from the meaning. Since a servant cannot be a judge over his master, rather the master is the judge.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: consolation for the believers, because Allah, the Exalted, judges between them concerning what they differ about with the disbelievers.
Here we ask: To whom is judgment passed in favor and against? To the believers, by the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will never give the disbelievers a way over the believers﴾ [al-Nisa 141].
Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if those who wronged possessed whatever is on the earth﴾ to the end.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that if the wrongdoers were to expend everything on the earth to ransom themselves with it, it would not benefit them. From where is this taken? From His saying: ﴿And there will appear to them from Allah what they had not reckoned﴾.

* And among them: that everything in this world becomes worthless at the time of punishment, when the wrongdoer witnesses it, as indicated by His saying: ﴿they would ransom themselves with it from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection﴾.

* Among its benefits: warning against wrongdoing, because mentioning this implies a warning against wrongdoing.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the affirmation of the Resurrection and the Resurrection of the dead, as indicated by His saying: ﴿they would ransom themselves with it from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that the punishment that befalls these wrongdoers does not occur to their minds, as indicated by His saying: ﴿And there will appear to them from Allah what they had not reckoned﴾.
Then the Exalted said: ﴿And there will appear to them the evils of what they earned, and what they used to mock will surround them﴾ [al-Zumar 48].

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the recompense is of the same kind as the deed, as indicated by His saying: ﴿the evils of what they earned﴾.

* Among its benefits: the affirmation of acquisition (kasb) for the servant, which is a refutation of the Jabriyyah (determinists), who say that man is compelled in his actions. We say to them: Rather, man is not compelled, and his deed is his acquisition.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: rebuke of these tormented people, since what they used to mock has befallen them. Allah, the Exalted, has said that it will be said to them: ﴿Is this magic, or is it that you do not see?﴾ [al-Tur 15], because in the world they used to ridicule the one who brought this news and say that it is magic. So on the Day of Resurrection they will be rebuked, and it will be said to them: ﴿Is this magic, or is it that you do not see?﴾.

* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that mocking Allah, the Exalted, and His verses is a cause of punishment, and it is disbelief that takes one out of the religion, as indicated by the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Say, "Was it Allah and His verses and His Messenger that you were mocking? Make no excuse; you have disbelieved after your belief"﴾ [al-Tawbah 65–66]. Based on this, it should be attached to marriage, divorce, taking back a wife, and emancipation, because its joke is serious. There is no disagreement among the scholars that whoever says a statement mocking the religion of Allah disbelieves.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿So when adversity touches man, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow upon him a favor from Us, he says, "I was only given it because of knowledge"﴾ [al-Zumar 49]. ﴿So when adversity touches man﴾, that is, afflicts him. The intended meaning of "man" here is the species. It is said that the intended meaning is the disbeliever. As for the one who said the intended meaning is the species, and that it includes both believer and disbeliever, he said: This is the nature of man, and the believer who acknowledges the blessings of Allah to Him and thanks Him is outside the nature of man. That is, Allah bestowed grace upon him, and he went out of the requirement of human nature.

As for the one who said that the intended meaning (i.e., of "man") is the disbeliever, then it is from the category of the general term used to mean the specific. He said: Because this described attribute is only found in the disbeliever. When adversity touches him, he returns to Allah, and when He gives him a blessing, he exults in it and says: No one has any favor over me in it, and it is only through knowledge. And this latter view is closer to the truth, because when Allah grants a believer a blessing, he gives thanks, and he does not say, "I was only given it because of knowledge."

He says: ﴿So when adversity touches man, he calls upon Us﴾, that is, he asks Us to remove his harm. Then, when We remove the adversity and bestow upon him a favor from Us by removing the harm that had befallen him, he says: ﴿I was only given it because of knowledge﴾, meaning I was given this thing because of knowledge. And what is meant by "knowledge" here? Does the meaning mean "given it because of knowledge from Allah that I am deserving of it, so I am worthy and entitled to it," or does it mean "because of knowledge on my part of the ways of acquiring wealth"?

It includes both matters. He says: "I was given it because of knowledge that I am worthy, and I was also given it through my own acquisition." Thereby he becomes one who claims favor over Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and becomes self-willed, combining two things: claiming favor, and saying that there is no grace from Allah, since He gave me that because He knows I am worthy of it. And the second: self-reliance and not attributing the matter back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 39, verses 46–48 (part 3 of 4):

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Nay, it is a trial.﴾ ﴿Nay, it is﴾: that is, the statement or the state. Both readings are possible. It may mean that when Allah gives him these blessings, the giving itself is a trial for him. It may also mean that this statement is a trial for him. The first meaning is closer, however: Allah tests the servant by removing harm from him and bringing him good and blessings. How many people have been tested by the blessings of Allah, so that they were upright, but blessings turned them away! In a hadith, Allah the Exalted said: "Among My servants there is one whom, if I made him wealthy, wealth would corrupt him, and among them there is one whom, if I made him poor, poverty would corrupt him."[[Al-Asma' wa al-Sifat by al-Bayhaqi (231), from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik.]] Allah is capable of all things, and He may choose for His servant what is better for him without the servant realizing it. The apparent meaning of His words ﴿Nay, it is a trial﴾ is: nay, this condition is a trial, namely the bestowing of blessings. Sulayman, upon him be prayers and peace, said: ﴿This is by the bounty of my Lord, to test me whether I will be grateful or ungrateful.﴾ [An-Naml 40] ﴿But most of them do not know.﴾ The resumptive particle here (al-istidrak, a corrective "but") means that those who were overwhelmed by the blessings of Allah were heedless of the One who bestowed them, the Giver and the Bestower of them. So they did not know the thankfulness due to this Benefactor, and they also did not know that these blessings were a trial. Instead, a person takes blessings as a matter of course and something natural, and he is heedless that Allah is testing him with them.

﴿Those before them had already said it.﴾ The pronoun in ﴿had already said it﴾ refers back to the statement ﴿I have only been given it on account of knowledge﴾. ﴿Those before them had already said it﴾, such as Qarun: ﴿He said: I have only been given it on account of knowledge I have.﴾ Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Did he not know that Allah had already destroyed before him generations that were stronger than him in might and greater in accumulation?﴾ [Al-Qasas 78]

﴿Those before them had already said it, but what they had earned did not avail them.﴾ The word (ma) here is negating. The verb ﴿avail﴾ (aghna) means "to ward off." So ﴿what they had earned did not avail them﴾ means that what they had earned did not ward off any of the punishment of Allah from them. Likewise, blessings do not avail whoever boasts of them and is heedless of obedience to Allah. Have you not seen how 'Ad were arrogant upon the earth, and ﴿said: Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾ [Fussilat 15]? That is because Allah had given them great strength. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Did they not see that Allah, who created them, is mightier than them in strength? And they used to deny Our signs. So We sent upon them a furious wind during ill-omened days.﴾ [Fussilat 15–16] Consider how these people were punished with the wind, which is the most gentle of things. The wind is the gentlest of things, yet they were punished by it as retribution for their saying: ﴿Who is mightier than us in strength?﴾ That is, they were not destroyed by thunderbolts or by a stone-laden storm from the sky, but were destroyed by this gentle wind. When they saw what this wind brought and carried of sand, they said: ﴿This is a cloud bringing us rain.﴾ [Al-Ahqaf 24] Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Rather, it is that which you were impatient for: a wind containing painful punishment, destroying everything by the command of its Lord.﴾ [Al-Ahqaf 24–25]

The Exalted said: ﴿But what they had earned did not avail them. So the evils of what they had earned struck them.﴾ [Az-Zumar 50–51] That is, the recompense for their evil deeds struck them. He called the recompense "evils" because the evil deeds were its cause, and to make clear that the recompense corresponds exactly to the deed, so that it is as if it were the deed itself.

﴿So the evils of what they had earned struck them, and those who wronged among these will be struck by the evils of what they earned.﴾ [Az-Zumar 51] The conjunction (wa) in His words ﴿and those who wronged﴾ is resumptive (isti'nafiyya), and (alladhina) is the subject (mubtada'). The clause ﴿will strike them﴾ is the predicate. ﴿And those who wronged among these will be struck by the evils of what they earned, as those before them were struck.﴾

﴿And they cannot escape.﴾ (Ma) is negating. Is it Hijazi or Tamimi? In fact, nothing in the wording indicates either. However, the Qur'an is in the dialect of Quraysh, as evidenced by His words: ﴿This is not a human; this is none but a noble angel.﴾ [Yusuf 31] Accordingly, whenever (ma) occurs, it is to be understood as Hijazi. But how do we parse it in a construction like this? In ﴿and they cannot escape﴾ we say: ﴿they﴾ is its subject, the (ba') is an extra preposition, and ﴿cannot escape﴾ is its predicate, in the accusative, marked by an implied yā'. The yā' that appears is the mark of the genitive, not of the accusative. The genitive mark is due to the extra preposition (ba'). We gave the governing role to the visible element, the (ba'), while the position (mahall) is assumed by estimation. So it is accusative, with an implied yā' in place of the visible one governed by the extra preposition.

As for ﴿mu'jizin﴾: is it the active participle of (ajaza), or of (a'jaza)? It is from (a'jaza). That means they cannot make Allah incapable, so He cannot be prevented from punishing them. Their punishment is a light matter for Allah, the Exalted.

﴿Do they not know that Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ [Az-Zumar 52] The hamza here is interrogative (istifham), and the (wa) is a conjunction. What is the conjoined element? It is either omitted and to be supplied according to the context, or it is what came before. If we say it is what came before, then the hamza is taken to be placed after the conjunction. The implied sense is: "and have they not known?" If we take the first view, the hamza is attached to an omitted element, whose sense is: "have they been ignorant, and not known?"

﴿Do they not know that Allah extends provision﴾: ﴿extends﴾ means "widens," and ﴿provision﴾ means "gift." ﴿To whom He wills and restricts it﴾: ﴿to whom He wills﴾ means He widens it for him as a test for this person to whom it is extended. ﴿And restricts it﴾ means He narrows it, also as a test, because narrowing involves a test and expansion involves a test. However, among people, by custom, narrowing is generally called a trial (ibtila'), that is an affliction (bala'). Expansion is a test (imtihan), even though trial (ibtila') and test (imtihan) have the same meaning. A person is tried by whatever he is tried with, so that Allah may test him: will he be patient or will he be impatient? As for what Allah tries him with in blessings, the question is whether he will be thankful or ungrateful.

﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ ﴿In that﴾ refers to the extending and restricting. ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe﴾: that is, signs that Allah alone is the One who disposes of affairs. That is why we find some people who are skilled in buying and selling and in acquiring wealth, and who have ability and strength, yet their provision is restricted. And we find some people who are less than this, meaning they do not care about affairs and do not have that skill, yet Allah widens their provision for them. This shows that Allah, the Exalted, is the One who disposes of His servants: He widens for this one and restricts for that one. But this does not mean that we should not take the means, as we will mention, Allah willing, in the benefits (al-fawa'id).

We now return to the words of the author, may Allah have mercy on him, who says: ("﴿So when harm touches man﴾" – the generic noun) Yes, what?

In any case, we have a conflict between an affirming and a negating statement, and the affirming takes precedence over the negating.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: How? No, there is also another evidence. I told you that His words ("Guide me to the truth in what has been disputed, by Your permission") have no proof for them, and that it is said at the opening of the night prayer.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: Alright, it does not contradict. ﴿And if those who wronged possessed﴾: so this is a middle position. He said: ﴿And if those who wronged possessed everything on earth and the like of it with it, they would surely ransom themselves with it from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ [Az-Zumar 47] ﴿If those who wronged﴾: the author did not explain it or clarify it. But we have explained in the tafsir that it includes the greater injustice, which is shirk, and the lesser, which is anything below it. However, it appears, and Allah knows best, that what is meant is the greater.

﴿And the like of it with it﴾: that is, what is on earth and its like added to it. ﴿They would surely ransom themselves with it from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection, and there will appear to them﴾ [Az-Zumar 47]: ﴿appear﴾ means "become manifest."

Alright, it does not contradict. ﴿And if those who wronged﴾: so this is a middle position. He said: ﴿And if those who wronged possessed everything on earth and the like of it with it, they would surely ransom themselves with it from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ [Az-Zumar 47]

﴿If those who wronged﴾: the author did not explain it or clarify it. But we have explained in the tafsir that it may include the greater injustice, which is shirk, and the lesser, which is what is below it. However, it appears, and Allah knows best, that what is meant is the greater. ﴿And the like of it with it﴾: that is, what is in the earth, and its like added to it.

﴿And there will appear to them from Allah what they had not reckoned﴾ ("reckoned" means "expected"). The author, may Allah have mercy on him, does not explain what is clear. It is said (bada) and it is said (bada'a), and there is a difference between them. (Bada) means what? 

Students: "Appeared."

Shaykh: "Appeared." (Bada'a) means "began," and in the verbal noun for the first one one says (budūwan): (bada yabdu budūwan). For the second one says (bada'a yabda'u bad'an).

He says: (﴿And there will appear to them the evils of what they earned, and there will befall them what they used to mock﴾ [Az-Zumar 48], that is the punishment). That is, the punishment befalls them, meaning it descends upon them, and their evils become apparent to them and they recognize them. They used to say: ﴿Would that we could be returned, and not deny the signs of our Lord, and be among the believers.﴾ [Al-An'am 27] Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Nay, there has appeared to them what they had been concealing before. And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden.﴾ [Al-An'am 28] We seek refuge in Allah.

﴿So when harm touches man﴾ [Az-Zumar 49] (﴿man﴾ is the generic noun). That is, is the intended meaning the genus, so that it includes?

Students: The believer and the disbeliever.

Shaykh: The believer and the disbeliever. But it has become clear from what we discussed that the apparent intended meaning is?

Students: The disbeliever.

Shaykh: The disbeliever. So it is a general term that is intended in a specific sense. A general term used for a specific meaning is very common in the Arabic language, such as His words: ﴿Those to whom people said: Indeed the people have gathered against you﴾ [Al 'Imran 173]. We know that not all people came saying this, but the one who said it was one person, or some specific people. As for "all of the sons of Adam," no. So the intended meaning of "man" here is the genus according to the author's words, and according to the view we have chosen, it is the disbeliever.

("﴿Harm called upon Us, then when We bestow upon him a blessing from Us, he says: I have only been given it on account of knowledge.﴾" ) His words ﴿bestow﴾ mean "give," ﴿a blessing﴾ mean "a favor." There is something to consider here: the favor is the act of the benefactor, and the blessing is the gift of the benefactor, meaning the thing given. Which is more fitting: to explain "blessing" as "favor," or to explain "blessing" as what is given to the person?

Students: As what is given to the person.

Shaykh: The second is the apparent meaning, and it is also the actual reality, because "bestowing" means that there is something bestowed, namely the blessing, such as children, provision, wives, dwellings, and other things.

("﴿He said: I have only been given it on account of knowledge﴾" from Allah that I am deserving of it.) This is one of the two views on the verse. The second view is: ﴿on account of knowledge﴾ means on account of skill and expertise in what I have done. And Allah knows best.

Student: Those who said that the intended meaning of "man" is the generic and not the specific (...) the Prophet's hadith, peace and blessings be upon him, that Allah created creation (...) the hadith indicates that (...).

Shaykh: On the fitrah (natural disposition), yes.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: They say that this is after a person is created, he inclines toward this thing, because the nature of man is that he takes pride in himself, boasts of himself, and forgets others. But in any case, what we have mentioned is the correct view.

Student: The verse was said by (...).

Shaykh: This statement was said.

Student: This statement?

Shaykh: Yes.

Student: ﴿I have only been given it﴾.

Shaykh: That is: "I was given what I was granted."

Student: Not the pronoun.

Shaykh: The (ha') (...).

Student: It refers to (...).

Shaykh: It refers to what was bestowed. "I have only been given what I was granted." The (ha') in ("given it") refers to the one bestowed.

Student: Is the attribution of a thing to oneself an attribution of honor? And if so, does the meaning of His words ﴿You judge between Your servants﴾ [Az-Zumar 46] include some groups of people?

Shaykh: Yes. Something attributed to Allah may be attributed to Him as an attribution of creation and origination, or it may be an attribution of honor. Here "servants" is general. If it is general, what is meant becomes what?

Student: Creation.

Shaykh: Creation and origination. If it is specific, meaning servanthood is attributed to a specific person or to a group described by a certain quality, then it is an attribution of honor.

Student: When Allah, glorified and exalted is He, bestows a blessing on a servant, when does the servant know whether it is a favor or a test?

Shaykh: Yes, this question will come to us, Allah willing, in the explanation of the benefits. But he knows that if he remains upon obedience to Him, it is a favor, and if it is the opposite, it is a test.

Student: (...).

Shaykh: There is no attribution here. Here there is no attribution.

Student: No, I mean it was attributed to Allah, the Exalted.

Shaykh: (...) what?

Student: (...) the attribution of creation.

Shaykh: No, he meant "servants." It is not "judging."

Student: (...).

Shaykh: No, he means "servants." He says: how can "servants" be attributed to Allah, when what is attributed to Allah implies honor? We say: the servants here include the disbeliever and the believer, and the disbeliever is not deserving of honor. So we say: what is attributed to Allah is so in both cases.

Student: Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿But most of them do not know.﴾ Can we be certain that the intended meaning of "man" is the genus, since all disbelievers do not know?

Shaykh: How?

Student: He said: ﴿But most of them do not know﴾ (...) is the intended meaning of "man" (...)?

Shaykh: No. Among the disbelievers there is one who is obstinate and knows the truth but is obstinate about what he is upon. Yes (...).

* * *

Student: ﴿And those who wronged among these will be struck by the evils of what they earned, and they cannot escape. Do they not know that Allah extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾ [Az-Zumar 51–52]

Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. I think we are discussing the author's commentary. Allah, glorified and exalted is He, said: ﴿So when harm touches man, he calls upon Us; then when We bestow upon him a blessing from Us, he says: "I have only been given it on account of knowledge." Nay, it is a trial, but most of them do not know.﴾ [Az-Zumar 49] Up to here, I think?

Student: (...).

Shaykh: Yes. He said: ﴿Nay, it is a trial﴾ [Az-Zumar 49]. (﴿Nay, it is﴾ that is, the statement ﴿a trial﴾, a calamity by which the servant is tested.) This is the view the author followed, that the trial refers to the statement he made. But the correct view is that the trial is the blessing Allah gave him, or the condition he was in when harm touched him and then the harm was removed from him and replaced with a blessing.
