* Among its benefits: demonstrating the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in that He folds these heavens, despite their greatness, as a scroll is folded up for writings.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: declaring Allah, Mighty and Majestic, free of every deficiency and defect, based on His saying: ﴿Glory be to Him﴾ [Az-Zumar 67]. Likewise, declaring Him free of resemblance to created beings, because resemblance to created beings is a defect, for likening the Perfect to the imperfect makes Him imperfect. The poet said:

*Have you not seen that the sword's worth diminishes*
*when it is said: "The sword is more effective than the staff"?*

So how much more so when it is said: "The sword is like the staff"? Likening Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to a created being is therefore a belittling of Him, Mighty and Majestic, because likening the Perfect to the imperfect makes Him imperfect.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirming the elevation (ʿuluww) of Allah, based on His saying: ﴿Exalted is He above what they associate﴾ [Az-Zumar 67].

The elevation of Allah, Glory be to Him, is divided into two types: elevation of essence (ʿuluww al-dhat) and elevation of attributes (ʿuluww al-sifah). As for elevation of attributes, no one among the people of the qiblah (ahl al-qiblah) has disagreed about it. Even the people of ta'til (denial of attributes) affirm for Allah elevation of attributes, but they differ with the people of the Sunnah on whether this is an elevation or a descent, because they consider that among Allah's elevation in His attributes is the negation of attributes from Him. As for Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah, they hold that among His elevation is affirming for Him all the attributes of perfection, in the manner in which they have come in the Book and the Sunnah. The people of the qiblah agree on affirming – what? – elevation of attributes, but they have disagreed about how elevation of attributes is to be understood. As for elevation of essence, they have disagreed greatly, to the extent that some who claim to belong to Islam said: affirming elevation of essence is disbelief. Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah said: affirming elevation of essence is obligatory, and we must affirm for Allah elevation of essence just as we affirm for Him elevation of attributes.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the vast difference between the Lord, the Creator, the Great, and the idols worshipped alongside Allah, based on His saying: ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate﴾ [Az-Zumar 67], meaning: a declaration of His purity, His greatness, and His exaltation above what these people associate with Him. For this reason the rhetorical question of rebuke and contempt for these idols came in His saying: ﴿He had certainly seen of the greatest signs of his Lord. Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other one?﴾ [An-Najm 18–20]. That is, tell me: what standing do these idols have in relation to the great and mighty signs of Allah which the Prophet (ﷺ) saw? That is, after these great signs have been established, tell me: what is there for these idols? ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other one?﴾ [An-Najm 19–20]: what are they in the face of these great signs? They are – what? – nothing. For this reason He said: ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate﴾ [Az-Zumar 67]. Allah, Exalted, has also made clear in the Noble Quran the lowliness of the rank of these idols: ﴿Is then He who creates like one who does not create? Will you not be reminded?﴾ [An-Nahl 17]; ﴿Say: Do you worship besides Allah that which holds for you neither harm nor benefit?﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 76]. The verses on this are many, belittling the status of these idols and making clear that the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is free of these idols and exalted above them. And Allah knows best.

* A student: (...) He said, for example, "Allah is Hearing, Seeing..."
* The Shaykh: He placed his finger on the eye and the ear.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: The way to reconcile them is that what the Sunnah has brought we take up, and what it has not brought, the basic ruling is prohibition. If you say, for example, taking this watch and saying "I grasped it," it is clear that you have specified a modality (takyif). But we say, "His grip": that this earth, entirely, is in the hand of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. As for how, Allah knows best.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: We answer that the Prophet did this to realize (tahqiq) the meaning, not to specify a modality (takyif), so as to realize the meaning of hearing and seeing: that they are real hearing and real seeing. In any case, we restrict ourselves in this to what has been reported, whatever the matter.
* A student: (...) He says: Allah has the attribute of folding and gripping.
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. We say: He folds and grips. ﴿And Allah withholds and extends﴾ [Al-Baqarah 245], and ﴿the Day We will fold up the heaven﴾ [Al-Anbiya 104].
* A student: "The hearts of the children of Adam are between two fingers of the Most Merciful." Do we say it this way?
* The Shaykh: What will he say? "Between two fingers, between two fingers, between two fingers, between two fingers, between two fingers, between two fingers, between two fingers." Where are the fingers? He cannot [see them]. Then, if he points like this, the observer may understand that the fingers of the Most Merciful, Mighty and Majestic, are directly touching the heart, and that is not so. The heart is between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Merciful, but we do not say that they are directly touching it. No, not directly.
So if someone says: How can it be conceivable that the heart is between two fingers of the Most Merciful without direct contact?
We say: Listen to His saying: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of night and day...﴾ [Al-Baqarah 164], up to His saying: ﴿and the clouds subjected between the sky and the earth are signs for a people who reason﴾ [Al-Baqarah 164]. Clouds subjected between the sky and the earth: do they touch the sky and the earth? No. So being "between" does not necessarily entail direct contact. Is that clear?
* A student: (...)
* The Shaykh: No, not at all, that is not permissible. If he says it like this, it implies that he has asserted with certainty that it is between these two fingers.
* A student: (...) "Both of the hands of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are right (yamin)" (...)?
* The Shaykh: Did this not come up before? It came up before, and we said: Allah has a right hand and a left hand. But the Prophet said: «Both His hands are yamin» [[Narrated by Muslim (1827/18) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr.]]. That is, yamin from al-yumn, which is blessing. And it is to prevent the assumption that the other hand is deficient, because for us the left hand is deficient in comparison with the right hand. Shaykh al-Islam Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned at the end of Kitab al-Tawhid: "In it there is an explicit statement of the left hand of Allah, Mighty and Majestic." End of quote.
* * *
* A student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall unconscious, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and immediately they will be standing, looking on. And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the Record will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and judgment will be made between them in truth, and they will not be wronged. And every soul will be fully compensated for what it did, and He is most knowing of what they do. And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them: "Did there not come to you messengers from among you reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?" They will say: "Yes, but the word of punishment has come into effect upon the disbelievers." It will be said: "Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein. How wretched is the residence of the arrogant."﴾ [Az-Zumar 68–72].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. What is the meaning of His saying: ﴿They have not esteemed Allah with true esteem﴾ [Az-Zumar 67]?
* A student: (...) of glorification.
* The Shaykh: With what?
* The student: By making for Him equals, and not (...).
* The Shaykh: What is the evidence that the meaning is associating partners? Recite the verse.
* The student: ﴿They have not esteemed Allah with true esteem, while the earth entirely will be His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate﴾ [Az-Zumar 67].
* The Shaykh: That is the evidence: the meaning of ﴿They have not esteemed﴾ is that they made a partner with Him.
* The Shaykh: His saying: ﴿while the earth entirely will be His grip on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Az-Zumar 67]: is this clause a circumstantial clause (ḥāl)?
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: That is, ﴿They have not esteemed﴾ while the earth is His grip. Or: ﴿They have not esteemed Allah with true esteem﴾ [Az-Zumar 67], then He informed, saying: ﴿while the earth entirely will be His grip on the Day of Resurrection﴾.
* The Shaykh: What is the meaning of ﴿His grip﴾ according to what the author (al-Mu'allif) held and according to what is the preponderant view?
* A student: The preponderant view is that it is in His right hand's grip.
* The Shaykh: What is the meaning of "in His right hand's grip"? That He grips it literally with His hand?
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: And the author?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: He said.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand﴾.
* The student: That is, Allah, Exalted, folds the heavens with His right hand: He gathers some of them over others, wraps some of them over others, like the folding of a scroll for writings.
* The Shaykh: And what is the meaning of ﴿in His right hand﴾?
* The student: That is, with His right hand.
* The Shaykh: That is precisely with His right hand. And the author?
* The student: The author said: "They are folded," meaning gathered.
* The Shaykh: No, leave aside "gathered" or "wrapped up." But what did he say about "in His right hand"?
* The student: "By His power."
* The Shaykh: By His power. What does tasbih (glorification) mean?
* A student: (...) declaring free of (...) Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
* The Shaykh: And from what is Allah declared free?
* A student: From defect, imperfection, and taking a partner for Him.
* Another student: And from resemblance.
* The Shaykh: From every defect and imperfection, and from resemblance to created beings. What is the evidence for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, being free of imperfection?
* A student: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [Ash-Shura 11].
* The Shaykh: That is for imperfection?
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: That is one proof. Another proof?
* The student: ﴿And no weariness touched Us﴾ [Qaf 38].
* The Shaykh: ﴿And no weariness touched Us﴾, meaning: no fatigue or exhaustion. What is the evidence for His being free of resemblance?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾ [Ash-Shura 11]?

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Rather, worship Allah alone, and be among the grateful.﴾ [Az-Zumar 66].

﴿Bal﴾ (rather): this is for idrab (a turning away from what precedes). Is it idrab of nullification (ibtal) or of transition (intiqal)? It is idrab of nullification, because idrab among them is of two kinds: one kind intended to nullify what came before and establish what follows, and another kind intended as a transition from one thing to another.

An example of the first is this verse. An example of the second is His saying: ﴿Rather, their knowledge of the Hereafter has failed. Rather, they are in doubt about it. Rather, they are blind to it﴾ [An-Naml 66]. Here there are transitions from bad to worse. ﴿Rather, their knowledge has failed﴾ means: it has been exhausted, ﴿of the Hereafter. Rather, they are in doubt about it. Rather, they are blind to it.﴾ Here He says: ﴿Rather, worship Allah﴾ [Az-Zumar 66]. This is idrab of nullification of the shirk that preceded; that is, "Rather, leave off shirk, for it is false, and worship Allah."

As for His saying: ﴿Rather, worship Allah﴾, the author said: (alone). From where did he derive this oneness that conveys restriction (hasr)? He derived it from the fronting of the object (taqdim al-ma'mul), and the rule in rhetoric is that fronting what should be postponed conveys restriction and exclusiveness. Everything that should be postponed, if fronted, the judgment is specific to it. It is known that the direct object should be postponed, so when it is fronted before its governing verb, it conveys exclusiveness and restriction, meaning: rather, Allah alone.

﴿Fa'budh﴾ (so worship): the fa' — they say it is brought in to embellish the wording. If it were removed in other than the Qur'an, the speech would still be sound, but in the Qur'an it cannot be removed, because it was revealed from Allah and cannot be altered. Such a particle is called fa' al-tazyin (the decorative fa'), and it has a parallel, such as their saying: "I have such-and-such, only (faqat)," meaning qatt, and the fa' is extra to embellish the wording.

He said: ﴿Rather, worship Allah﴾. ﴿U'bud﴾ is an imperative verb, meaning: humble yourself before Him, humble yourself to Allah. Know that worship ('ibadah) is used in two senses: the first is ta'abbud (the act of worshipping), and the second is al-muta'abbad bih (that which is worshipped).

As for ta'abbud, its meaning is humbling oneself before Allah the Exalted, out of love and veneration, by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions. So if we see a person praying, for example, we say: this one is worshipping, that is, humbling himself to Allah the Exalted by performing prayer. It is also used for the object of worship, that is, the act itself. Shaykh al-Islam defined it in this sense by saying: "Worship is a comprehensive term for everything Allah loves and is pleased with, of statements and acts, outward and inward." On this basis, prayer itself we call worship, and charity is worship, fasting is worship, Hajj is worship, kindness to parents is worship, maintaining ties of kinship is worship, and benevolence to the poor is worship, and so on. So His saying ﴿fa'budh﴾ means: humble yourself to Him by performing His worship, by carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions.

(﴿Rather, worship Allah and be among the grateful﴾ for His blessing upon you.) ﴿Wa kun﴾: kun is an imperative verb, and ﴿min al-shakirin﴾ means: among those who thank Allah.

Know that when (al) is attached to a participle (mushtaq), it becomes a general relative pronoun among the relative nouns, so it is equivalent to (man) and to (ma) when attached to a participle, such as al-shakir (the thankful), al-mashkur (the one thanked), al-ahsan (the best), and similar words. On this basis, His saying ﴿min al-shakirin﴾ conveys generality, meaning: among those who engage in thanking Allah.

If it is asked: what is shukr (gratitude)? It is said: gratitude is the act of obeying the Benefactor in belief, speech, and action; this is shukr. For this reason a poet said:

"Three things have been gained by you through my blessings: my hand, my tongue, and the concealed conscience."

He means: by your bestowing favours on me, you have possessed my heart, my tongue, and my limbs.

If someone asks: is shukr the same as hamd (praise) or something else?
We say: there is a general and specific relationship between them. They coincide when they are in response to a blessing, for hamd is shukr, since it is praise of Allah by the tongue. If a person eats or drinks and says "Al-hamdu lillah," he is thereby grateful and praising. Hamd stands alone in describing Allah with perfection apart from response to a blessing; so if you praise Allah as "the Living, the Mighty" and similar, that is hamd and not shukr, since it is not in response to a blessing. However, we may sometimes consider it shukr insofar as it is worship, and obeying the Benefactor is part of shukr.

And if you praise Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, or even if you perform obedience to Allah the Glorified and Exalted in return for His blessing, and it was not in your mind (...) perfection, it becomes shukr to Him. In any case, it may be difficult for one to be separated from the other, because praise itself, even if not in response to a blessing, is considered shukr, since it is the performance of obedience to the Benefactor. ﴿Rather, worship Allah and be among the grateful﴾ [Az-Zumar 66].

Then the Exalted said: ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure﴾ [Az-Zumar 67]. ﴿Ma﴾ is negative, and ﴿qadaru﴾ means: they magnified. The word Allah is the object of ﴿qadaru﴾, and ﴿haqqa qadrihi﴾ is an absolute object (maf'ul mutlaq), because it is an idafa to a verbal noun, and what is attached to a verbal noun is called an absolute object because it stands in the place of the verbal noun. On this basis we say: ﴿haqqa qadrihi﴾ means: its true magnification.

The commentator said: (they did not know Him with true knowledge, or they did not magnify Him with true magnificence when they associated others with Him). The correct one is the second: that the meaning is they did not magnify Him with true magnificence when they associated others with Him. The evidence for this is that these people knew Allah: ﴿If you asked them who created them, they would surely say, Allah﴾ [Az-Zukhruf 87], ﴿If you asked them who created the heavens and the earth, they would surely say, Allah﴾ [Az-Zumar 38]. But did they magnify the One they knew with true magnification? No, and this is what (...).

So the correct possibility is the second, that they did not magnify Him with true magnificence, by what? By associating others with Him; for whoever magnifies Allah with true magnification cannot associate anyone with Him.

Then He said: ﴿While the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection﴾. The waw is for the circumstantial clause (hal), and it may be resumptive (isti'nafiyyah) to explain Allah's greatness.

﴿Wal-ard﴾ is the subject (mubtada'), ﴿jamian﴾ is a circumstantial qualifier (hal), and ﴿qabdatuhu﴾ is the predicate of the subject, meaning: the whole earth, all of the seven earths, will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection.

The commentator said: (﴿wal-ard jamian﴾: hal, that is, the seven). ﴿Jamian﴾ is a hal from what? From the earth. From this we know that a hal may come from the subject before the predicate is mentioned, as you might say: Zayd standing is better than him sitting.

He says: (﴿While the earth entirely is His handful﴾ means: held in His grip, that is, in His dominion and disposal). So the author explained the qabd (grip) as meaning dominion and disposal. This is clearly questionable; rather, it is a distortion, because dominion and disposal extend to everything, the earth and heavens both on the Day of Resurrection and before it. Rather, qabda in the sense of the thing grasped, which the hand encloses, is the handful, as one says: a handful of food. What is a handful of food? It means a person grasps food with his hand like this. So the earth on the Day of Resurrection is the handful of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and this has been explained in the hadith of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud concerning the Prophet ﷺ and a rabbi of the Jews: "Allah will place the earth on one finger, the trees on one finger, and the mountains on one finger," etc. [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4811), Muslim (2786/19), from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud.] So the correct and definite position is that the qabdah means that it is within His hand, Mighty and Majestic.

If someone says: may we depict this handful, by taking a date or an apple and placing it in our hands, and saying ﴿His handful﴾, and then closing our hand on the apple or date?
The answer: No; for if we did that, it would be a likening of Allah's grip of the earth, and this is impermissible. As for explaining the meaning of qabdah, there is no harm, by saying: qabdah is placing a thing in the hand and then grasping it with it. But to specify how Allah the Mighty and Majestic grips the earth is contrary to the belief of the People of the Sunnah and the Community, as is well known to all.

His saying ﴿Yawm al-qiyamah﴾ is a time adverb for the handful; that is, it will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection. The Day of Resurrection is the day when people are raised from their graves to Allah the Mighty and Majestic, and it is named thus for three reasons. Enumerate them for us; we mentioned them shortly before.

* Student: the standing of people before the Lord of the worlds.
* Shaykh: for people's standing from their graves before the Lord of the worlds.
* Student: the establishment of justice on the Day of Resurrection.
* Shaykh: the establishment of justice on the Day of Resurrection.
* Student: (...).
* Shaykh: What? No.
* Student: the standing of the spirits, the angels.
* Shaykh: No.
* Student: the witnesses stand.
* Shaykh: "The day the witnesses stand."

﴿While the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand﴾. The author said: (folded [mijmu'at] by His power). The heavens are "mutawiyyat" (folded). Folding is known: turning cloth over one part upon another is called tayy, and from it: folding a page when the scribe finishes with it, meaning turning part of it over another. Allah the Mighty and Majestic compared His folding of the heavens to the folding of a scroll for books, saying: ﴿On the day We will roll up the heaven like the rolling of a scroll for writings﴾ [Al-Anbiya 104]. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds: this great heaven of vast expanse, whose thickness is reported to be five hundred years, Allah the Mighty and Majestic will fold these heavens as a scroll is folded for books, or as the scroll in which cases are recorded is folded: ﴿On the day We will roll up the heaven like the rolling of a scroll for writings﴾ [Al-Anbiya 104], meaning as the scroll is rolled, which is the judge's scribe's record, or as the scroll in which matters are written is rolled. Folding is known; we said it is turning cloth over one part upon another, or paper, or similar.

He says: ﴿The heavens are folded﴾: the agent is omitted, or the form of the passive participle is used for knowledge of the folder. Who is the folder? Allah, as the other verse explains: ﴿On the day We will roll up the heaven like the rolling of a scroll for writings﴾.

The author said: (folded [mijmu'at]). This is questionable, because we say: it is folded (tayyan) as a collection; if we explain it as gathered, we have not given a precise explanation, since a thing may be gathered without being folded. But if it is folded, this is a meaning beyond mere gathering. The correct statement is: ﴿mutawiyyat﴾ means some of them are wrapped up within others.

﴿Folded in His right hand﴾. He said: (by His power). This is a distortion according to the doctrine of those who do not affirm Allah's informative attributes (sifat khabariyyah). The correct view is that the right hand is meant by the yamin, the right hand; He folds them with His right hand, Mighty and Majestic.

He said: ﴿Folded in His right hand, glorified is He and exalted above what they associate﴾ [Az-Zumar 67]. Subhana (glory be to): an ism al-masdar (verbal noun form), its verb is sabbaha, and the masdar of sabbaha is tasbih; the ism al-masdar is subhan, which is always in the accusative as an absolute object and usually attached to a noun. On this basis one should not err in its parsing: parse it always as an absolute object of an omitted verb, the estimate being: he glorifies with glorification.

﴿Subhanahu wa ta'ala 'amma yushrikun﴾ [Az-Zumar 67]: meaning, tanzihan (declaring Him far above) him. What is the meaning of tasbih? We have now explained the word morphologically, but what is the meaning of tasbih? They said: the meaning of tasbih is tanzih (exalting Allah above imperfection), because it derives from sabbaha, yasbahu, when one moves far away in water. So tanzih is distancing from evil. On this basis the meaning of "Subhan Allah" is: declaring Him far above. From what is Allah declared far above?

He is declared far above two things: from resemblance to creation, and from every deficiency and defect in His attributes. His power, for example, is exalted above incapacity; His knowledge is exalted above ignorance and forgetfulness; His strength is exalted above weakness, and so on. His hand is exalted above resemblance to the hands of creatures, and His face likewise. Thus the tanzih of Allah the Mighty and Majestic returns to two things: first, resemblance to creation; second, defect and deficiency.

His saying ﴿Ta'ala﴾: He is exalted in His greatness above what they associate with Him, or above what they associate with Him alongside Him, and there is no doubt this is the reality.

From the two noble verses we take the following benefits:

* First: the obligation of sincerely devoting worship to Allah, from His saying ﴿Rather, worship Allah alone﴾ [Az-Zumar 66].
It follows from this principle that if a person associates someone with Allah, his deeds are nullified: why? Because if he associates with Allah, he performs an act not commanded by Allah and His Messenger, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever does an action that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697), Muslim (1718/17), from Aisha]. This is apart from the preceding verse, ﴿If you were to associate others with Allah, your deeds would surely be nullified﴾ [Az-Zumar 65], which is an explicit text. But if we want to derive it from His saying ﴿Rather, worship Allah﴾ [Az-Zumar 66], we say:
* Among its benefits: whoever associates anyone with Allah, his deed is nullified and rejected. The proof is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever does an action that is not in accordance with our command, it is rejected" [Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (2697), Muslim (1718/17), from Aisha].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the obligation of gratitude upon everyone, from His saying ﴿And be among the grateful﴾ [Az-Zumar 66]; and when gratitude is obligatory, its opposite, disbelief, is forbidden.
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that sincerity to Allah the Exalted is part of gratitude to Him, since He followed His saying ﴿Rather, worship Allah﴾ [Az-Zumar 66] with His saying ﴿And be among the grateful﴾ [Az-Zumar 66].

As for the second verse: among its benefits is showing the greatness of Allah the Mighty and Majestic, from His saying ﴿While the earth entirely is His handful﴾ and ﴿the heavens are folded in His right hand﴾ [Az-Zumar 67].
* Among its benefits: that whoever associates with Allah has not magnified Allah with true magnification; rather, the opposite, from His saying ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure﴾ [Az-Zumar 67].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: the goodness of describing the Qur'an, for when He negated from them that they measured Allah with His true measure, He explained the reason for it: that He, Mighty and Majestic, is greater than everything, ﴿while the earth entirely is His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens are folded in His right hand﴾ [Az-Zumar 67].
* Among the benefits of the noble verse: that it is obligatory to magnify Allah with true magnification. But someone may say: this involves great hardship, because Allah the Exalted is greater and more majestic than that the deed of the servant could encompass Him. For this reason, when the verse ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah with the fear due to Him﴾ [Ali 'Imran 102] was revealed, it was difficult for the Companions: who can fear Allah with the fear due to Him? It is said that this noble verse is qualified by His saying ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ [At-Taghabun 16]. Otherwise, who can compass magnifying Allah with true magnification in the manner Allah the Mighty and Majestic intended? But we say: magnifying Allah with true magnification is by carrying out His command, and this is attained to the extent of one's capacity, by His saying ﴿Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity﴾ [Al-Baqarah 286], and by His saying ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾ [At-Taghabun 16].

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 39, verse 66–67 (part 2 of 2):

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirming that Allah has a hand, based on His saying: ﴿His grip﴾ [Az-Zumar 67], and His saying: ﴿in His right hand﴾ [Az-Zumar 67].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that on the Day of Resurrection Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will grip the earth in His hand, based on His saying: ﴿And the earth entirely will be His grip on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Az-Zumar 67].
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: that the heavens will be folded up on the Day of Resurrection, based on His saying: ﴿and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand﴾ [Az-Zumar 67].
* Among its benefits: demonstrating the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in that He folds these heavens, despite their greatness, as a scroll is folded up for writings.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: declaring Allah, Mighty and Majestic, free of every deficiency and defect, based on His saying: ﴿Glory be to Him﴾ [Az-Zumar 67]. Likewise, declaring Him free of resemblance to created beings, because resemblance to created beings is a defect, for likening the Perfect to the imperfect makes Him imperfect. The poet said:

*Have you not seen that the sword's worth diminishes*
*when it is said: "The sword is more effective than the staff"?*

So how much more so when it is said: "The sword is like the staff"? Likening Allah, Mighty and Majestic, to a created being is therefore a belittling of Him, Mighty and Majestic, because likening the Perfect to the imperfect makes Him imperfect.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: affirming the elevation (ʿuluww) of Allah, based on His saying: ﴿Exalted is He above what they associate﴾ [Az-Zumar 67].

The elevation of Allah, Glory be to Him, is divided into two types: elevation of essence (ʿuluww al-dhat) and elevation of attributes (ʿuluww al-sifah). As for elevation of attributes, no one among the people of the qiblah (ahl al-qiblah) has disagreed about it. Even the people of ta'til (denial of attributes) affirm for Allah elevation of attributes, but they differ with the people of the Sunnah on whether this is an elevation or a descent, because they consider that among Allah's elevation in His attributes is the negation of attributes from Him. As for Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah, they hold that among His elevation is affirming for Him all the attributes of perfection, in the manner in which they have come in the Book and the Sunnah. The people of the qiblah agree on affirming – what? – elevation of attributes, but they have disagreed about how elevation of attributes is to be understood. As for elevation of essence, they have disagreed greatly, to the extent that some who claim to belong to Islam said: affirming elevation of essence is disbelief. Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah said: affirming elevation of essence is obligatory, and we must affirm for Allah elevation of essence just as we affirm for Him elevation of attributes.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the vast difference between the Lord, the Creator, the Great, and the idols worshipped alongside Allah, based on His saying: ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate﴾ [Az-Zumar 67], meaning: a declaration of His purity, His greatness, and His exaltation above what these people associate with Him. For this reason the rhetorical question of rebuke and contempt for these idols came in His saying: ﴿He had certainly seen of the greatest signs of his Lord. Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other one?﴾ [An-Najm 18–20]. That is, tell me: what standing do these idols have in relation to the great and mighty signs of Allah which the Prophet (ﷺ) saw? That is, after these great signs have been established, tell me: what is there for these idols? ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other one?﴾ [An-Najm 19–20]: what are they in the face of these great signs? They are – what? – nothing. For this reason He said: ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate﴾ [Az-Zumar 67]. Allah, Exalted, has also made clear in the Noble Quran the lowliness of the rank of these idols: ﴿Is then He who creates like one who does not create? Will you not be reminded?﴾ [An-Nahl 17]; ﴿Say: Do you worship besides Allah that which holds for you neither harm nor benefit?﴾ [Al-Ma'idah 76]. The verses on this are many, belittling the status of these idols and making clear that the Lord, Mighty and Majestic, is free of these idols and exalted above them. And Allah knows best.

* A student: (...) He said, for example, "Allah is Hearing, Seeing..."
* The Shaykh: He placed his finger on the eye and the ear.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: The way to reconcile them is that what the Sunnah has brought we take up, and what it has not brought, the basic ruling is prohibition. If you say, for example, taking this watch and saying "I grasped it," it is clear that you have specified a modality (takyif). But we say, "His grip": that this earth, entirely, is in the hand of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. As for how, Allah knows best.
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: We answer that the Prophet did this to realize (tahqiq) the meaning, not to specify a modality (takyif), so as to realize the meaning of hearing and seeing: that they are real hearing and real seeing. In any case, we restrict ourselves in this to what has been reported, whatever the matter.
* A student: (...) He says: Allah has the attribute of folding and gripping.
* The Shaykh: Yes indeed. We say: He folds and grips. ﴿And Allah withholds and extends﴾ [Al-Baqarah 245], and ﴿the Day We will fold up the heaven﴾ [Al-Anbiya 104].
* A student: "The hearts of the children of Adam are between two fingers of the Most Merciful." Do we say it this way?
* The Shaykh: What will he say? "Between two fingers, between two fingers, between two fingers, between two fingers, between two fingers, between two fingers, between two fingers." Where are the fingers? He cannot [see them]. Then, if he points like this, the observer may understand that the fingers of the Most Merciful, Mighty and Majestic, are directly touching the heart, and that is not so. The heart is between two fingers of the fingers of the Most Merciful, but we do not say that they are directly touching it. No, not directly.
So if someone says: How can it be conceivable that the heart is between two fingers of the Most Merciful without direct contact?
We say: Listen to His saying: ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of night and day...﴾ [Al-Baqarah 164], up to His saying: ﴿and the clouds subjected between the sky and the earth are signs for a people who reason﴾ [Al-Baqarah 164]. Clouds subjected between the sky and the earth: do they touch the sky and the earth? No. So being "between" does not necessarily entail direct contact. Is that clear?
* A student: (...)
* The Shaykh: No, not at all, that is not permissible. If he says it like this, it implies that he has asserted with certainty that it is between these two fingers.
* A student: (...) "Both of the hands of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, are right (yamin)" (...)?
* The Shaykh: Did this not come up before? It came up before, and we said: Allah has a right hand and a left hand. But the Prophet said: «Both His hands are yamin» [[Narrated by Muslim (1827/18) from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Amr.]]. That is, yamin from al-yumn, which is blessing. And it is to prevent the assumption that the other hand is deficient, because for us the left hand is deficient in comparison with the right hand. Shaykh al-Islam Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, may Allah have mercy on him, mentioned at the end of Kitab al-Tawhid: "In it there is an explicit statement of the left hand of Allah, Mighty and Majestic." End of quote.
* * *
* A student: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan: ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall unconscious, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and immediately they will be standing, looking on. And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the Record will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and judgment will be made between them in truth, and they will not be wronged. And every soul will be fully compensated for what it did, and He is most knowing of what they do. And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them: "Did there not come to you messengers from among you reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this your Day?" They will say: "Yes, but the word of punishment has come into effect upon the disbelievers." It will be said: "Enter the gates of Hell, to abide therein. How wretched is the residence of the arrogant."﴾ [Az-Zumar 68–72].
* The Shaykh: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. What is the meaning of His saying: ﴿They have not esteemed Allah with true esteem﴾ [Az-Zumar 67]?
* A student: (...) of glorification.
* The Shaykh: With what?
* The student: By making for Him equals, and not (...).
* The Shaykh: What is the evidence that the meaning is associating partners? Recite the verse.
* The student: ﴿They have not esteemed Allah with true esteem, while the earth entirely will be His grip on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand. Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate﴾ [Az-Zumar 67].
* The Shaykh: That is the evidence: the meaning of ﴿They have not esteemed﴾ is that they made a partner with Him.
* The Shaykh: His saying: ﴿while the earth entirely will be His grip on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Az-Zumar 67]: is this clause a circumstantial clause (ḥāl)?
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: That is, ﴿They have not esteemed﴾ while the earth is His grip. Or: ﴿They have not esteemed Allah with true esteem﴾ [Az-Zumar 67], then He informed, saying: ﴿while the earth entirely will be His grip on the Day of Resurrection﴾.
* The Shaykh: What is the meaning of ﴿His grip﴾ according to what the author (al-Mu'allif) held and according to what is the preponderant view?
* A student: The preponderant view is that it is in His right hand's grip.
* The Shaykh: What is the meaning of "in His right hand's grip"? That He grips it literally with His hand?
* The student: Yes.
* The Shaykh: And the author?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: He said.
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿and the heavens will be folded up in His right hand﴾.
* The student: That is, Allah, Exalted, folds the heavens with His right hand: He gathers some of them over others, wraps some of them over others, like the folding of a scroll for writings.
* The Shaykh: And what is the meaning of ﴿in His right hand﴾?
* The student: That is, with His right hand.
* The Shaykh: That is precisely with His right hand. And the author?
* The student: The author said: "They are folded," meaning gathered.
* The Shaykh: No, leave aside "gathered" or "wrapped up." But what did he say about "in His right hand"?
* The student: "By His power."
* The Shaykh: By His power. What does tasbih (glorification) mean?
* A student: (...) declaring free of (...) Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
* The Shaykh: And from what is Allah declared free?
* A student: From defect, imperfection, and taking a partner for Him.
* Another student: And from resemblance.
* The Shaykh: From every defect and imperfection, and from resemblance to created beings. What is the evidence for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, being free of imperfection?
* A student: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [Ash-Shura 11].
* The Shaykh: That is for imperfection?
* A student: (...).
* The Shaykh: That is one proof. Another proof?
* The student: ﴿And no weariness touched Us﴾ [Qaf 38].
* The Shaykh: ﴿And no weariness touched Us﴾, meaning: no fatigue or exhaustion. What is the evidence for His being free of resemblance?
* The student: (...).
* The Shaykh: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing﴾ [Ash-Shura 11]?

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall unconscious, except whom Allah wills.﴾ [Az-Zumar 68] "Nufikha" (was blown): the blowing is well known, and the one who blows is Israfil. He left him unnamed for the sake of glorifying the matter, because ambiguity (ibham) comes for the sake of magnification, as in His saying: ﴿So there covered them of the sea that which covered them﴾ [Ta-Ha 78], for this indicates the greatness of what overtook them. The blowing is undoubtedly a momentous matter, and for this reason the one who blows is not specified. Every mention of blowing into the Horn in the Qur'an comes in the form of the passive participle: ﴿And the Day when it is blown﴾ [An-Naml 87], and ﴿And the Horn will be blown﴾ [Az-Zumar 68].

As for His saying: ﴿And the Horn will be blown﴾, the verb here is in the past tense although the event is yet to come, but it is expressed in the past tense to affirm that it will certainly occur, as in His saying: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it﴾ [An-Nahl 1], although it has not yet come.

As for His saying: ﴿into the Horn﴾: the Horn (as-Sur) is a great trumpet. It was said that the breadth of its circumference is as the distance between the heavens and the earth. This Horn is blown into by Israfil.

The author says: (The First Blast). ﴿And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall unconscious, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and immediately they will be standing, looking on﴾ [Az-Zumar 68]. The author said: (The First Blast). This is based on the view that the blowing into the Horn occurs twice. It was also said: rather, the blowing into the Horn occurs three times, and this is indicated by the hadith of the Horn, which Ibn Kathir, may Allah have mercy on him, quoted at length in Surat al-An'am, and that these three are the blast of terror (nafkhat al-faza'), the blast of swooning (nafkhat as-sa'q), and the blast of resurrection (nafkhat al-ba'th). This is based on His saying: ﴿And the Day when the Horn is blown, whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will be terrified﴾ [An-Naml 87] in Surat an-Naml, and here He said: ﴿will fall unconscious﴾ [Az-Zumar 68]. Then: ﴿Then it will be blown again﴾ [Az-Zumar 68]. It was also said: rather, the blowing is two times, and this is what the author, may Allah have mercy on him, followed, and that the blast of terror is the blast of swooning, and that when people hear it the first time they are terrified, then it continues to be prolonged, and they fall unconscious, dying after the terror. On this view the blowing is twice: the first produces terror and then swooning, because He prolongs the blowing and then people fall unconscious. There is no doubt that something that causes people to swoon must be something great, alarming and terrifying, and so it is.

As for His saying: ﴿fall unconscious﴾ [Az-Zumar 68], he said: (died). ﴿whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, except whom Allah wills﴾ [Az-Zumar 68]. "Man" (whoever) is a relative pronoun indicating generality, and it is used mostly for rational beings, though it may be used for others by extension or for inclusiveness. An example of its extended use is: ﴿And Allah created every moving creature from water. Of them are some that move on their bellies, and of them are some that walk on two legs, and of them are some that walk on four﴾ [An-Nur 45]. It is known that what moves on its belly or on four is not of those with intellect, but "man" (min) was used by extension. It may also be used for generality, as in this verse: ﴿whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, except whom Allah wills﴾ [Az-Zumar 68], so everyone in the heavens and the earth, whether humans, animals or others, will all die.

He says: ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾ [Az-Zumar 68], meaning those who will not swoon, for they do not swoon. The scholars differed concerning who is excepted. The author and a group held that the excepted are the houris (hur) and the young boys (wildan), who are in Paradise. It was said: the houris, the young boys and the angels. The author's statement does not preclude this, because of his words: (and others). It was said: Allah knows best.

We say: ﴿except whom Allah wills﴾ as Allah, mighty and majestic, left it ambiguous, and we do not delve into details, because there is no sound and explicit proof specifying those excepted.

﴿Then it will be blown again﴾ [Az-Zumar 68]. And who is the one who blows? Israfil.

His saying: ﴿again﴾ is an absolute object (maf'ul mutlaq), meaning "a blast again." Indeed: ﴿Then it will be blown again﴾. Or we may say it is an adjective for an omitted noun, the implied meaning being "a blast again," as in His saying: ﴿And when the Horn is blown with one blast﴾ [Al-Haqqah 13].

(﴿and immediately they﴾, meaning all the dead creatures, ﴿will be standing, looking on﴾ [Az-Zumar 68], awaiting what will be done to them.)

His saying: ﴿and immediately they﴾: the fa' is a conjunction particle, and "idha" is the sudden particle (idha fuja'iyya), which indicates that what follows occurs suddenly, meaning that it comes quickly. And ﴿they are standing﴾ [Az-Zumar 68] is a nominal sentence, as is evident, and its purpose is affirmation and continuity. It is more eloquent than if He had said "then they stood," because His saying ﴿and immediately they are standing﴾ indicates that this condition is established for them, as if it were a fixed, long-settled matter, even though they will only stand up at the single final blast.

As for His saying: ﴿looking on﴾, he said: (awaiting what will be done to them). It may also mean: looking at what has happened, from seeing with the eye, and this interpretation does not contradict what the author or the commentator mentioned, so the verse includes both: they look with their eyes at what has occurred, and they await what will be done to them.

* Among the benefits of this noble verse:

* The affirmation of the blowing into the Horn, and that it is certain to occur, derived from His saying: ﴿And it was blown﴾ [Az-Zumar 68], where it is expressed in the past tense.

* The greatness of this blowing, derived from the ambiguity of the agent.

* That this blowing is mighty in its effect, as people are terrified by it and then fall unconscious, that is, die.

* Another benefit of this noble verse: that swooning encompasses everyone in the heavens and on the earth except whom Allah wills, and those excepted are fewer than those who swoon, because generally the exception is smaller than what is excepted.

* A benefit of the verse: the affirmation of Allah's will, mighty and majestic, which occurs frequently in the Book of Allah, glorified and exalted. No one denies it except regarding the actions of the servants, where the Qadariyya denied it.

* A benefit of the verse: that the Horn is blown twice, as indicated by His saying: ﴿Then it will be blown again﴾ [Az-Zumar 68].

* A benefit of it: that the blowing "again" or "the other" is the one by which resurrection occurs, as indicated by His saying: ﴿immediately they are standing, looking on﴾ [Az-Zumar 68].

* A benefit of the verse: that standing up from the graves immediately follows the blast into the Horn, which we derive from the sudden particle "idha."

* A benefit of the noble verse: that those who rise—that is, those who stand up—stand as if they had a long time standing, as indicated by the use of the nominal form for it.

* A benefit of it: the perfection of the power of Allah, mighty and majestic, since all creatures rise at once with this single blast, and Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Then it will be but one shout, and immediately they will be on the surface [of the earth]﴾ [An-Nazi'at 13, 14], meaning on the surface of the earth and the back of the earth.

If someone asks: what is the connection between the blowing into the Horn and people's life and their resurrection from the graves?

The answer: this Horn is the gathering place of souls. The souls of all creatures are gathered in it, and when the blast occurs, the souls scatter and each soul enters its own body which it used to inhabit in this world, never mistaking it, despite the multitude of creation and their dispersion, for their souls do not mistake their bodies. Each soul enters the body it used to inhabit in the world.

Then Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord﴾ [Az-Zumar 69]. "Ashraqat" (shone): the author said: (lit up). From it comes "ashraqat ash-shams" when its light spreads, and "sharaqat" when it emerges. It is said: the sun "sharaqat" when it appears above the horizon, and "ashraqat" when it rises and its light lengthens or spreads. For this reason the prayer performed after it has risen a spear's length is called the prayer of ishraq, not the prayer of shuruq. Shuruq is the sun's appearance on the horizon, and ishraq is its rising and the spreading of its light.

So here He says: ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord﴾ [Az-Zumar 69], with the light of Allah which is His light, and not with created light. The attribution of light to the Lord, mighty and majestic, is an attribution of a quality to what it qualifies, meaning that Allah, exalted is He, illuminates the earth with His light.

(﴿with the light of its Lord﴾ [Az-Zumar 69] when He manifests Himself to judge.) "Manifests" means appears to judge, and He, mighty and majestic, comes to judge between the servants. It has been reported that Allah, glorified and exalted, sends down angels in the lowest heaven until they surround creation, then the angels of the second heaven descend until they surround the people of the lowest heaven, because the people of the second heaven are more numerous than those of the lowest, since the second heaven is wider than the lowest, so its inhabitants are more. Then the people of the third heaven descend and surround those before them, and they are more than the people of the second heaven, and so on up to the seventh heaven. Allah said: ﴿And your Lord comes, and the angels, rank upon rank﴾ [Al-Fajr 22]. And He said: ﴿And the Day the heaven will be split open with clouds, and the angels will be sent down in descent﴾ [Al-Furqan 25]. "Nuzzila" (sent down): they descended gradually, the people of the lowest heaven, then the second, then the third, up to the seventh. The heaven will be split open with clouds. The people of knowledge said: this cloud is what precedes the coming of Allah, mighty and majestic, a great cloud whose extent and nature we do not know. For this reason He said: ﴿the heaven will be split open﴾ [Al-Furqan 25], not "will be broken open" (tanshaqqu), but "will be split" (tashaqqaqu), as if something emerges from it little by little. This will be a great matter, occurring before the coming of the Lord, glorified and exalted. Then He, glorified and exalted, will descend to judge between the servants, and at that time the earth will shine with the light of its Lord. We cannot now imagine how this illumination is, how this light is, or how this cloud is; it is something our minds do not now grasp.

He says: (﴿And the Book will be placed﴾ [Az-Zumar 69], the book of deeds for reckoning). "Wuddi'a" (placed): placed before the people. Allah said: ﴿And We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a record which he will find laid open﴾ [Al-Isra 13]. This book contains the deeds of the servants, good or bad, except what has been erased through forgiveness or repentance, for it is not found in the book. For example, minor sins are recorded, but when a person prays, the five prayers erase sins through them, and perhaps a person repents of evil deeds (...). Nothing remains in the book except what a person faced his Lord with and what was sealed upon him during his life.

As for His saying: ﴿And the Book will be placed﴾ [Az-Zumar 69], does "al" here indicate generality or the genus? Does it mean every book is placed, or the Book as a kind? The apparent meaning, which is better, is generality: every book is placed, and its owner takes it. This book in which deeds are recorded will be said to its owner: ﴿Read your record; sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner﴾ [Al-Isra 14]. And when he reads it, can he deny what is in it? He cannot; he must acknowledge it, except the polytheists, who deny and say: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ [Al-An'am 23], because when they see that the monotheists who were sincere are saved from punishment, their souls tempt them to deny polytheism, perhaps to be saved from punishment. But this will not benefit them. When they say ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists,﴾ their hearing, sight and skins will testify against them regarding what they used to do, and at that time those who disbelieved will wish the earth were levelled over them, and they will not conceal from Allah any statement.

He said: (﴿And the Book will be placed﴾, the book of deeds for reckoning). How is the book distributed? It is distributed in two ways:

The first: that it is given in the right hand. The second: that it is given in the left.

The believer is given his record in his right hand and says to the people: ﴿Here, read my record!﴾ [Al-Haqqah 19], look, read. He says this in joy at Allah's blessing and in recounting Allah's favor, just as if one of you were given his result and it reads "excellent, one hundred percent." What does he do? Each student shows it to the others: look! And if each mark had a red circle on it, what would he say? He would tear it up. But on the Day of Resurrection he cannot tear it up; in this world he can tear it or hide it. In any case, it is a natural human trait that a person takes pride in Allah's blessing, shows it to people and says: ﴿Here, read my record! Indeed, I was certain that I would meet my reckoning﴾ [Al-Haqqah 19, 20]. Here "zanantu" (I was certain) means "I was certain," that is: I was certain that I would meet my reckoning and that Allah, glorified and exalted, would reckon me. ﴿But as for he who is given his record in his left hand﴾, may Allah protect us, ﴿he will say: "Oh, I wish I had not been given my record, and I had not known what my reckoning is!"﴾ [Al-Haqqah 25, 26], just as one says to an unwelcome visitor: "I wish he had not come, I wish I had never seen his face." The record given in the left hand, may Allah protect us, its owner knows what is in it, and he says: ﴿Oh, I wish I had not been given my record, and had not known what my reckoning is!﴾ [Al-Haqqah 25, 26].

In the Noble Qur'an, Allah mentioned that whoever is not given his record in his right hand takes it in his left, and in another verse, from behind his back. Are these two attributes or one attribute?

Some scholars said: they are two attributes. Others said: they are one attribute, meaning he is given the record in his left, from behind his back, not from the front, but from behind his back, and in this there is a warning and a reminder to him of what he did with Allah's Book in the world.

Where did he place it?

* Student: (...).

* The Shaykh: What is it?

* The student: (...).

* The Shaykh: No, that is not it. We said: it is a reminder to him of his state in the world, that he cast the Book of Allah behind his back: ﴿So they cast it behind their backs and sold it for a small price﴾ [Ali 'Imran 187]. It is as if it is said to him: your recompense is of the same kind as your deed. It was also said: some people are given it in the left from the left side, and some are given it from behind their backs, so they are two attributes. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 39, verse 69 (part 1 of 2):

He says: ﴿And the Book will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought forward﴾ [Az-Zumar 69]. "The prophets will be brought": who brings them? Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, because the dominion on that day belongs to Allah, and He has the disposal of it. So the prophets are brought. The word "the prophets" here includes both the prophets who were sent as messengers and the prophets who were not sent as messengers. It is general. "And the witnesses": "witnesses" is the plural of "shahid." Is the intended meaning of "witnesses" those who were martyred in the cause of Allah, or those who will bear witness on the Day of Resurrection? The second is what is meant. So who are the witnesses?

The author, may Allah have mercy on him, said: (That is, with Muhammad (ﷺ) and his community, who bear witness for the messengers that they conveyed the message.)

As for his words, (That is, with Muhammad), their apparent meaning is that he wants to explain "the prophets" as referring to Muhammad (ﷺ). On this explanation, the general term would be used to mean a specific group, and this is not accepted. Rather, the correct view is that it is general and remains general. That is, all the prophets will be brought, and they will bear witness against their peoples that they conveyed the message to them.

As for his words, "the witnesses," this is the mention of the general after the specific (ʿaṭf al-ʿāmm ʿalā al-khāṣ). Those meant are the ones who bear witness against the nations and for the messengers, and they are this community. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And thus We have made you a justly balanced nation, that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger will be a witness over you﴾ [Al-Baqarah 143]. Muhammad (ﷺ) is a witness over you. So the messengers are witnesses over their nations. They will say: "Our Lord, we bear witness that You sent us to our peoples and that we conveyed to them." No one will be able to say on that day, "This is a claim, so where is the proof?" In other words, if someone said such a thing, who would testify? Your limbs will testify, and Allah witnesses before everything. As for the witnesses, yes, we say: they are the community of Muhammad (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), based on His saying ﴿Thus We have made you a justly balanced nation, that you may be witnesses over the people﴾ [Al-Baqarah 143]. This community, all praise be to Allah, bears witness over people in this world and in the Hereafter. We now bear witness that Allah sent Nuh to his people, and we bear witness that his people conveyed the message in the most perfect manner, and we bear witness that he remained among them for a thousand years less fifty years. We bear witness to all of this with what Allah the Mighty and Majestic has taught us in His Book. So on the Day of Resurrection, the testimony will be in our favour over the nations.

As for the author's words, may Allah have mercy on him, (they bear witness for the messengers that they conveyed the message), if he had said, "and against the nations with the establishment of the proof," that would have been better. Likewise, we bear witness against nations that they conveyed the message and that the proof was established against them. So for us there are two testimonies: a testimony for the messengers and a testimony against the nations.

He said: (﴿And it will be judged between them with truth﴾ [Az-Zumar 69], that is, with justice.) Judged between them: by whom? By Allah the Mighty and Majestic. But He left the agent unnamed out of magnification, and it is known. That is, there is no need to specify, because it is known that the Judge is Allah, Lord of the worlds.

﴿And it will be judged between them﴾, that is, between the people (﴿with truth﴾, that is, with justice, ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾ [Az-Zumar 69] at all). People will be judged on the Day of Resurrection with justice. Indeed, judgment will not be only between people with justice; rather, it will be between the animals with justice. The Messenger (ﷺ) informed that "retribution will be taken for the hornless sheep from the horned sheep."[1] Subhan Allah! Then after that they will become dust, because they have neither Paradise nor Hellfire. But this is to manifest justice and to heal what is in the breasts. When the horned sheep butts the hornless sheep, something stirs in the heart of the hornless one, but it cannot retaliate, because the other has horns and it does not. On the Day of Resurrection, however, Allah the Glorified and Exalted will give the hornless sheep the ability to retaliate, or Allah the Mighty and Majestic will show it how retaliation is taken for it from the horned sheep. For this reason, it is said, "It will be judged between them with truth."

The author says: (that is, justice). Why did he explain "truth" here as "justice" and not as "truthfulness"? Because the context is one of ruling and judgment, and justice is what fits it. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾ [Az-Zumar 69]. The pronoun in "they" refers to the people. They will not be wronged at all, that is, nothing will be reduced from their rights. Rather, every person will be given his right in full. And Allah knows best.

Let us take the benefits. Allah the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the Book will be placed﴾ [Az-Zumar 69]. In this verse, there are the following benefits:

* Among them: the affirmation of light as an attribute of Allah, from His saying, ﴿with the light of its Lord﴾ [Az-Zumar 69].
* Among them, from the benefits of the verse: the affirmation of a specific lordship of Allah on that day, since lordship is attributed to the earth, even though He is the Lord of everything. Attributing Allah's lordship to a specific thing implies the magnification of that thing. ﴿I have only been commanded to worship the Lord of this city, which He has made sacred, and to Him belongs everything﴾ [An-Naml 91]. Since His saying ﴿the Lord of this city﴾ might suggest that He is the Lord of this city only and not of others, He said ﴿and to Him belongs everything﴾.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of the Book in which deeds are recorded, from His saying, ﴿and the Book will be placed﴾ [Az-Zumar 69].
* Among its benefits: the affirmation of witnesses over people for what they did, from His saying, ﴿and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought forward﴾ [Az-Zumar 69].
* Among its benefits: that judgment will be made between the prophets and those who denied them, from His saying, ﴿and it will be judged between them with truth﴾ [Az-Zumar 69].
* Among its benefits: that judgment will be made between the scholar and his community, from His saying, ﴿the prophets and the witnesses﴾. Scholars are undoubtedly witnesses; indeed, they are the leaders of the witnesses after the prophets. ﴿And it will be judged between them with truth.﴾ The scholar conveys on behalf of the messengers, so judgment will be made between him and those to whom the message reached through him.
* Among the benefits of this noble verse: the affirmation of judgment among creatures on that day, from His saying, ﴿and it will be judged between them with truth﴾.
* Among its benefits also: that judgment has no bias and no injustice in it, from His saying, ﴿with truth﴾, so a person will be given his full right.
* Among its benefits also: the absence of injustice on that day, from His saying, ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾ [Az-Zumar 69]. The negation of injustice here does not mean only the negation of injustice; rather, it means the affirmation of complete justice in which there is no injustice in any way, from His saying the Exalted, ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾ [Az-Zumar 69].

* Student: (...)
* Shaykh: Did you hear the question? He asks: why did we say that we declare Allah free from every deficiency and from resemblance? Is not resemblance a deficiency? Yes, it is a deficiency, and we pointed to this, but sometimes you forget.
* Student: Would it not be (...) that the disbelievers take their book with their left hand from behind their backs?
* Shaykh: No, the answer to the question: we say that deficiency is one thing and resemblance is another. For example, Allah has power. We say it is not like the power of the created being. But can deficiency attach to it? Therefore we must say "free from every deficiency." Does negating resemblance suffice? Perhaps "free from every deficiency" suffices for negating resemblance, because resemblance is a deficiency. But we say: since Allah has stated it, saying ﴿There is nothing like Him﴾ [Ash-Shura 11], it is appropriate that we draw attention to it.
* Student: Would it not be fitting that the characteristic of the disbelievers who turn away from the Book of Allah, blessed and exalted, and His signs, is that they take their book with their left hand from behind their backs, and that they are not equal to the sinning believers who take their book with their left hand (...)?
* Shaykh: Wait, who says this? I mean, who says that sinning believers take their books with their left hands?
* Student: The saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Say: Are those who know equal to those who do not know?﴾ [Az-Zumar 9]. Does this not come from it (...)?
* Shaykh: No, this does not come from it. Yes, if it were established that sinning believers take with the left hand, there would be no harm. But the verse indicates: ﴿And as for he who is given his record in his left hand, he will say, "O I wish I had not been given my record, and had not known what my account is. O I wish it had been the end [of me]. My wealth has not availed me. My authority has gone from me." Seize him and chain him, then into Hellfire drive him, then in a chain whose length is seventy cubits, insert him. Indeed, he did not believe in Allah the Great﴾ [Al-Haqqah 25–33]. And this one is a disbeliever.
* Student: You mentioned that the souls will be inside the Trumpet during the second blowing, and therefore after the blowing the bodies will be resurrected and each soul will enter its body. This is undoubtedly one of the unseen matters, so what is their proof for this?
* Shaykh: This is the long hadith about the Trumpet, and it contains things that are rejected (munkar), but it also contains things that are supported by other authentic texts, and it contains things that are not rejected, for which no authentic hadith supports them. However, the scholars accepted it.
* Student: We said: if the particle "fa-idhā" (suddenly) (...) follows (...). The hadith of Abu Hurayrah, O Shaykh, says that between the two blowings there are forty (years). How do we reconcile that it is immediate and that it is...?
* Shaykh: Do you know what you are saying now? Pay attention, not so that we answer. We mentioned that His saying ﴿and behold, they are standing, looking on﴾ [Az-Zumar 68] is for suddenness, and suddenness indicates that the thing happens immediately. Now you have brought to us the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: "Between the two blowings are forty," but the verse concerns the second blowing. Is that clear?
* Student: May Allah bless you. You mentioned that the blowing in the Trumpet is twice (...). ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall unconscious, except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and immediately they will be standing, looking on﴾ up to the end of the verses [Az-Zumar 68]. So does it mean (...)?
* Shaykh: What do you say about this question?
* Student: (...)
* Shaykh: We explained this. If the mention of the blowing in the Trumpet came with "fa-saʿiqa" (they fall unconscious) and "fa-idhā hum qiyām" (behold, they are standing), it came with three expressions: ﴿And the day the Trumpet is blown, and those in the heavens and those on the earth will be terrified﴾ [An-Naml 87] and ﴿And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall unconscious﴾ [Az-Zumar 68]. It was said that the terror is the first blowing, then the fainting is the second, then the resurrection is the third.
It was also said that the terror and the fainting are one blowing: it is blown, and the people are terrified, "What has happened? What has happened?" Then the blowing prolongs, and the people faint. On this view, it is one blast, but it extends: its beginning is terror and its end is fainting. Do you understand? On this view, the author's words, "the first blowing," are because he sees that the blast of terror is the blast of fainting.

Then the Blessed and Most High said: ﴿And every soul will be paid in full what it did﴾ [Az-Zumar 70]. "Wuffiyat" means: it was given its full recompense, as you say, "I paid him his right in full," i.e., I gave it to him in full.
﴿Kullu nafs﴾ [Az-Zumar 70]: "kullu" is with a ḍammah, as it is the deputy subject (nāʾib fāʿil).
﴿Kullu nafsin mā ʿamilat﴾ [Az-Zumar 70]: That is, "that which" it did. So "mā" here is a relative pronoun, and it is the second object of "wuffiyat." The first object is "kullu." Although it is with a ḍammah, the deputy of the subject takes the place of the object, so "kullu" is in the position of the first object and "mā ʿamilat" is in the position of the second object.
The commentator said: "(i.e., its recompense)." What led him to this interpretation is that the deed has already passed in the world, and what is paid in full to the soul is the recompense, as Allah the Most High said: ﴿As a reward for what they used to do﴾ [Al-Waqiʿah 24].
If someone says: The matter is clear as the commentator said, but what is the wisdom in Allah, Mighty and Majestic, expressing the recompense of the deed by the deed itself? The wisdom in that is an indication that the recompense does not exceed the deed nor fall short of it, so it is as if it is the deed itself. Since it does not exceed it nor fall short of it, it is as if it is the deed itself. This is the perfection of justice, and "as you judge, so you will be judged."
﴿And every soul will be paid in full what it did, and He is most knowing of what they do﴾ [Az-Zumar 70]. "Huwa" (He) refers back to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It is as if someone says: How can He know what the soul did, when ages upon ages have passed, and in both the minute and the great deeds? So He said: ﴿And He﴾ [Az-Zumar 70], that is, Allah, ﴿is most knowing of what they do﴾ [Az-Zumar 70], meaning nothing is hidden from Him. He, glorified and exalted, neither errs nor forgets, so it is impossible for any part of a person's deeds to be lost.
The commentator's words: "(i.e., the Knower of 'what they do')" – explaining "aʿlam" (most knowing) as "ʿālim" (knowing) is an insufficient interpretation, because "aʿlam" is a higher degree than "ʿālim." You say, "Zayd is knowing, and ʿAmr is knowing," and they are equal in knowledge. You say, "Zayd is more knowing than ʿAmr," and then Zayd is more knowing and of a higher degree than ʿAmr. So when the author says, "(aʿlam, i.e., ʿālim)," he has diminished Allah's knowledge, because the word "ʿālim" does not preclude sharing, but "aʿlam" precludes sharing, since the superior and the inferior are not equal.
What is strange is that if someone asked us: Why did the author shift from the superlative form to the active participle? He would say: Because there should be no comparison or preference between the Creator and the created. If you say "aʿlam," its meaning is that you preferred the Creator over the created. We say to him: Subhan Allah! And if you say "ʿālim," you have equated the Creator with the created. See how he deviated from the apparent wording to a corrupt meaning, so he committed two errors, may Allah forgive him. The first: contradicting the apparent wording. The second: diminishing the Creator's knowledge. So we say: Allah is most knowing and most merciful. In the Qur'an: ﴿And You are the best of the merciful﴾ [Al-A'raf 151], and most wise: ﴿Is not Allah the most just of judges?﴾ [At-Tin 8]. Even more than that, Allah said: ﴿Is Allah better, or what they associate?﴾ [An-Naml 59], even though no one thinks or imagines that the idols are like the Creator; but He said this to silence the opponent and show his error. We say to him: Is Allah better, or the one you associate with Him? In sum, our obligation is to take "aʿlam" in its apparent sense, that it indicates Allah's superiority in knowledge over His servants, so He is most knowing of what they do.
If someone says: The author shifted from "aʿlam" to "ʿālim" because people do not know what they do, so knowledge is negated, and then explaining it as "aʿlam" with "ʿālim" would not be harmful. We say: This is also wrong. Rather, the people do know what they do. Every person knows what he did, and everyone who sees another doing something knows what he did.
The words of the Most High: ﴿And He is most knowing of what they do﴾ [Az-Zumar 70]. Sometimes it comes as "yafʿalūn" (they do), sometimes as "yaʿmalūn" (they work), and sometimes as "yaksibūn" (they earn). Is there a difference between them? We say: No, there is no difference between them, because their meaning is one. But when it is said "qawl" and "fiʿl" (speech and action), speech is with the tongue and action with the limbs. When it is said "ʿamal" (deed), it includes both speech and action. And when it is said "qawl," it can include both speech and action. From this (i.e., the use of "speech" for action) is the statement of the Messenger ﷺ to ʿAmmar ibn Yasir: "It would have sufficed you to say thus," then he struck the ground with his hand.[Narrated by Muslim (368/110) from the hadith of ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud and ʿAmmar ibn Yasir.] It is known that this is not speech but action.
﴿And He is most knowing of what they do﴾ [Az-Zumar 70]. He said: "So He has no need of a witness." Yes, He has no need of a witness; "Allah suffices as a witness" [An-Nisa 79 / Ar-Ra'd 43 context]. But He, glorified and exalted, establishes witnesses to manifest justice and to rebuke the doer. Have you understood? Because when witnesses are established against him after he denied it, that is a sterner rebuke.
